````markdown
 1: # Visualize: Direction Comps & Asset Production
 2: 
 3: Load this from [new-work.md](new-work.md) on a comp-led build, when image generation is available (a harness-native tool or the API fallback `impeccable context` reports). A code-led contract skips this file by design, not by drift; do not load it then. PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md are preconditions. New-work has already resolved the visual world; this file must not reopen it. A surface-scope structure round that already put three visualized cards before the user (new-work.md, established world) has discharged this round: the locked card's comp is the approved comp, so record the approval and continue at After approval; generate nothing new.
 4: 
 5: A probe tests composition, narrative, hierarchy, density, focal moment, signature use, and image requirements. It is not a second identity workshop. Keep DESIGN.md's palette, typography direction, material language, component character, imagery stance, and motion grammar fixed.
 6: 
 7: ## Generate three compositional options
 8: 
 9: The comp round runs inside the build's phase state: `impeccable build-phase start --direction <seed key> --kind <...>` has already run (the roll's output names the command) and its `comps` phase is open before the first comp is generated; a comp rendered before that sits outside the state, and a session resumed from that point has no phases to follow. `impeccable generate-image` refuses to write under `.impeccable/mocks/` until start has run; a harness-native image tool is bound by the same order.
10: 
11: Render three distinct high-fidelity north-star comps of the requested surface, saved under `.impeccable/mocks/` so they survive the session. Comp at the surface's own viewport: portrait at device size for a native app or mobile-first surface, desktop landscape otherwise; a phone screen comped landscape misstates the composition before anything is built against it. Comps are the build thread's own work, never delegated: the thread that writes the prompts holds the direction's full context and has seen every comp when the build starts. Open every image by its workspace-relative path; sandboxed viewers reject absolute paths, and everything under the project root has a relative one. Base the comps on real content and the surface concepts already developed with the user. On an established world, anchor every comp on the real identity: capture a screenshot of a representative existing page and pass it as a reference image (the harness image tool's input image, or `impeccable generate-image --ref`); the prompt leads with the new surface's structure while the reference carries palette, type, and component character, because DESIGN.md words alone drift where a pixel reference does not. Name what the reference contributes and what it must not: chrome, palette, type, and component character carry over; the reference page's own content does not, and a banner, hero, or card lifted verbatim is the reference leaking, not fidelity. Three is the number: one comp invites rubber-stamping; the spread between three surfaces the composition worth building. The chosen card's decision comp is the first of the three: it already renders this direction at full fidelity under this discipline, so generate two more that vary what the first held fixed, and send all three to the approval point together. Only a round arriving with no decision comp (a degraded roll, an identity-mode page, a direction pinned without the decision round) renders all three here.
12: 
13: - A comp is a designed surface, not a picture of the subject. Lead the prompt with the surface's own structure: the regions this design has, named in order with their scale relationships; a page with no navigation says so instead of inventing one, and an unconventional surface states its unconventional skeleton. A prompt that leads with atmosphere gets a vignette back: the model paints the fish market instead of the fish market's website. Self-check every render: if it could hang as a poster, or reads as a photograph with some text on it, it is not a comp; regenerate with the layout scaffold stated more literally.
14: - The inverse is also a failure: a surface with none of its subject in it. The subject appears as the content the regions hold; the world dresses the frame and never displaces what the frame shows. The deletion usually rides in on the prompt's exclusion list, so exclusions bind invented claims, and a medium ban belongs to the committed imagery stance, never to caution. Before accepting a render, point at the subject; a render that depicts everything about the world and nothing of the subject fails however faithful its atmosphere. Regenerate with the subject's content named region by region.
15: - Judge a comp as the shipped screen: the visitor's job must be readable from the image alone. Name the surface's mode from the render with no caption; a render whose mode cannot be read back is art direction without a surface. Regenerate with the visitor's job as the prompt's spine.
16: - Commitment is depth, not coverage. The world enters through one dominant move plus the material, type, and spacing that support it; the remaining regions hold still so that move can be read. A region that simply does its job in the world's grammar carries the direction further than a region performing the concept. The check cuts competition, never content: a quieted region keeps its information and stops performing. A second element competing with the named focal moment at the same scale means the comp is shouting; with no named focal moment, several regions performing the concept at once is the same shout. Regenerate keeping the strongest move and quieting the rest. Busy is louder, not bolder.
17: - When the user shortlisted multiple concepts, spread the three across them.
18: - When one direction is committed, vary the structural uncertainty an image can resolve: topology, sequence, density, hierarchy, focal composition, or interaction framing.
19: - Show enough beyond the opening moment to prove the concept can govern the whole surface.
20: - Do not generate a palette artifact, ask new atmosphere questions, introduce a different type voice, or invent a new motif. If the committed world cannot support the concept, return to the concept shortlist rather than changing the world.
21: 
22: Each comp is a direction test, not a screenshot specification. Core UI text, responsive behavior, accessibility, semantics, and interaction states remain implementation responsibilities.
23: 
24: ## One approval point
25: 
26: Show the three together on the decision page (`impeccable serve-question`, one option per comp with the comp as its hero), or in the harness only when it renders images inline; a text-only surface does not count as display. Ask what should carry forward, what feels false to the world, and whether the selected concept should be approved, combined, revised, or rejected. Then stop and wait. A structured simulated user counts as attended and receives the same question.
27: 
28: Do not begin code until the user approves a direction or explicitly delegates the choice. If they delegate, choose using the task brief, PRODUCT.md, and DESIGN.md, and state the evidence. Approval refines the task concept; it does not modify DESIGN.md.
29: 
30: This approval point has no substitute and no skip condition. When the structured question tool errors, fall back to the decision page; only after both fail may you treat the choice as delegated, and a delegated pick is recorded exactly as an approval is and disclosed in your first reply, not your last. The finish reviewer treats comp-round comps with no recorded approval as a material finding; decision comps under `.impeccable/mocks/decision/` are the direction round's hand, not comp-round output, and imply no approval on their own.
31: 
32: After approval, record the choice where tools can find it: the approved comp's path goes in the surface brief, and its `.json` prompt sidecar gains `"approved": true` (every comp generated through `impeccable generate-image` has one; create it if a native tool didn't). The sidecar travels with the mocks folder, so the approval survives sessions and machines that never see the brief, and it is what `impeccable build-phase advance` reads to close the comps phase. Summarize the composition and the parts of the comp that must not be literalized, return to new-work.md, record the direction contract from the approved concept, and build.
33: 
34: ## After approval: the comp becomes a spec
35: 
36: The approved comp is a north star for translation into semantic, responsive, accessible code, never a license to recompose: keeping the palette and mood while redrawing the topology is a second art direction. Do not rasterize core UI text or controls. Do not substitute a different visual driver after approval without asking.
37: 
38: What the comp shows is measured, not remembered. new-work.md section 6 runs the build as phases (`impeccable build-phase`): the spec phase turns the comp into region boxes with sampled palettes (`impeccable comp-spec`), and the medium of every region follows from what the pixels are, never from what feels buildable: a figure, a product object, machinery, any illustration with perspective, shading, or drawing skill in it, and any texture by name (woven cloth, paper grain, fabric, leather, brushed metal) is a `plate` / `image` / `texture` region and ships as a raster; text, controls, chrome, diagrams with countable elements, flat shape systems, and anything that must move, scale, or respond are semantic. Writing "CSS" for a sculpted panel's finish, or a many-vertex `clip-path` for a torn edge, is the quiet deletion of the approved design; the detector's organic-clip-path and buried-raster rules and the hero gate's region scores catch it. Dropping an image-native region is a scope decision the user makes at the approval point, never a silent flattening after it. Generated imagery is a material, not a claim: evidence rules bind assertions, specs, testimonials, and photographs presented as real, never render fidelity.
39: 
40: ## Plates and provenance
41: 
42: Every raster region's plate is produced in the plates phase, before any page code, by the shipped asset producer or in the current thread (use `impeccable comp-spec --crop <id>` and save `impeccable comp-spec --plate-prompt <id>` to a prompt file; pass the crop and prompt to the harness image tool, or use `impeccable generate-image --ref <crop.png> --prompt-file <prompt.txt> --out <plate.png> --size <WxH> --quality high`). For isolated cutouts, add `--background transparent` to both the plate-prompt and API generation commands; use native PNG alpha and preserve white paint and clear gaps. Use `--background opaque` for full-frame imagery. Create output directories first and inspect alpha on light and dark grounds. Generation context is part of the asset: after generating any image with any tool, run `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable embed-prompt <image> --prompt "<prompt>"` with the exact string the tool received (`impeccable generate-image` does this itself), so the intent lives inside the file; `--read` recovers it, `--scan <dir>` lists rasters still missing one. The embedded prompt plus the region's row in the spec is the raster's **provenance**, and every raster the artifact references carries it; a sourced, stock, or pre-existing raster embeds its origin instead. A raster created or replaced later, in a fix batch or a reviewer's rebuild, is produced the same way; a raster a fix abandons is deleted in the same batch.
43: 
44: Convert images with a converter `impeccable context` reported at boot (the IMAGE_TOOLS line); probe only when it reported none, at most once per session, never per image.
45: 
46: Return to [new-work.md](new-work.md) for the direction contract, the phased build, and the finishing pass.
````

## File: .github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable
````
  1: #!/bin/sh
  2: # Impeccable launcher. Runs the platform binary shipped next to this script:
  3: #   <this dir>/bin/<os>-<arch>/impeccable
  4: # Order: $IMPECCABLE_BIN, the sibling binary, ~/.impeccable/bin/impeccable,
  5: # the version-pinned cache, then `impeccable` on PATH. Never needs Node.
  6: # The unversioned home binary and the PATH candidate are validated with the
  7: # engine-probe handshake first: the retired 3.x npm CLI also installed a bin
  8: # named `impeccable`, and exec'ing it would fail every verb with
  9: # "Unknown command". Trusted candidates (IMPECCABLE_BIN, the sibling binary,
 10: # the version-pinned cache) are exec'd without a probe: hooks run them on
 11: # every edit and must stay fast.
 12: set -eu
 13: 
 14: # True when the candidate answers the engine handshake (prints
 15: # "impeccable-engine <version>", exit 0). Quiet and fast (<100ms).
 16: # IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE marks the child as a probe: a copy of this
 17: # launcher reached recursively (e.g. symlinked onto PATH as `impeccable`)
 18: # then skips its own probes and refuses to download, so probing stays cheap
 19: # and can never loop.
 20: probe_ok() {
 21:   case "$(IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE=1 "$1" engine-probe 2>/dev/null || true)" in
 22:     impeccable-engine*) return 0 ;;
 23:   esac
 24:   return 1
 25: }
 26: probing=${IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE:-}
 27: 
 28: dir=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
 29: 
 30: # What the binary needs to know about its home: the skill directory (for
 31: # reference/*.md and command-metadata.json) and how to name itself in the
 32: # commands it prints. Exported BEFORE any exec below, including the
 33: # IMPECCABLE_BIN override: an engine binary reached with no IMPECCABLE_SKILL_DIR
 34: # cannot find reference/*.md (so native platform refs never inline) or read its
 35: # own version (so UPDATE_AVAILABLE never fires). Setting it here covers every
 36: # candidate the launcher can exec.
 37: : "${IMPECCABLE_SKILL_DIR:=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$dir/.." && pwd)}"
 38: : "${IMPECCABLE_SELF:=$0}"
 39: export IMPECCABLE_SKILL_DIR IMPECCABLE_SELF
 40: 
 41: if [ -n "${IMPECCABLE_BIN:-}" ] && [ -x "${IMPECCABLE_BIN}" ]; then
 42:   exec "${IMPECCABLE_BIN}" "$@"
 43: fi
 44: 
 45: case "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)" in
 46:   Darwin) os=darwin ;;
 47:   Linux) os=linux ;;
 48:   MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*|Windows_NT) os=windows ;;
 49:   *) os=unknown ;;
 50: esac
 51: case "$(uname -m 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)" in
 52:   arm64|aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
 53:   x86_64|amd64) arch=x64 ;;
 54:   *) arch=unknown ;;
 55: esac
 56: 
 57: bin="$dir/bin/$os-$arch/impeccable"
 58: [ "$os" = windows ] && bin="$bin.exe"
 59: 
 60: if [ -x "$bin" ]; then
 61:   exec "$bin" "$@"
 62: fi
 63: if [ -f "$bin" ]; then
 64:   # Lost the executable bit in transit (zip extraction, some copiers).
 65:   chmod +x "$bin" 2>/dev/null && exec "$bin" "$@"
 66: fi
 67: # On Windows (an MSYS/Git Bash shell) the cached names carry .exe so this
 68: # launcher and impeccable.cmd share one cache.
 69: exe=""
 70: [ "$os" = windows ] && exe=".exe"
 71: home_bin="${HOME:-/nonexistent}/.impeccable/bin/impeccable$exe"
 72: if [ -z "$probing" ] && [ -x "$home_bin" ] && probe_ok "$home_bin"; then
 73:   exec "$home_bin" "$@"
 74: fi
 75: # Version-pinned user cache, filled by the download below or by `impeccable update`.
 76: version=""
 77: [ -f "$dir/VERSION" ] && version=$(tr -d '[:space:]' < "$dir/VERSION")
 78: cache_root="${IMPECCABLE_HOME:-${HOME:-/nonexistent}/.impeccable}"
 79: cached="$cache_root/bin/$version/impeccable$exe"
 80: if [ -n "$version" ] && [ -x "$cached" ]; then
 81:   exec "$cached" "$@"
 82: fi
 83: if [ -z "$probing" ] && command -v impeccable >/dev/null 2>&1 && probe_ok impeccable; then
 84:   exec impeccable "$@"
 85: fi
 86: 
 87: # Last resort: fetch this version's binary for the current platform from the
 88: # public release channel into the user cache. Needs network; sandboxes without
 89: # egress preinstall the binary on PATH instead.
 90: setup_help() {
 91:   echo "Engine $version setup needs network access and write permission to $cache_root/bin/$version." >&2
 92:   echo "Run this launcher ($0) with engine-probe in a terminal that has those permissions, then retry the original command." >&2
 93:   echo "Alternatively, set IMPECCABLE_HOME to a writable cache location, or IMPECCABLE_BIN to a preinstalled engine binary." >&2
 94: }
 95: fetch_url() {
 96:   if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 97:     curl -fsSL --retry 2 -o "$tmp" "$1" 2>/dev/null
 98:   elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 99:     wget -q -O "$tmp" "$1" 2>/dev/null
100:   else
101:     return 1
102:   fi
103: }
104: check_download() {
105:   download_file=${1:-$tmp}
106:   if [ ! -f "$download_file" ]; then
107:     rm -f "$tmp.sha256"
108:     echo "impeccable: download completed but the file was removed before execution: $url; check your antivirus quarantine or logs. Refusing to continue; do not disable protection." >&2
109:     exit 127
110:   fi
111:   if [ ! -s "$download_file" ]; then
112:     rm -f "$download_file" "$tmp.sha256"
113:     echo "impeccable: downloaded file is empty: $url; refusing the unverified download" >&2
114:     exit 127
115:   fi
116: }
117: if [ -n "$probing" ]; then
118:   # Inside another launcher's probe: no download, fail fast and quiet.
119:   exit 127
120: fi
121: if [ -n "$version" ] && [ "$os" != unknown ] && [ "$arch" != unknown ]; then
122:   base="${IMPECCABLE_DOWNLOAD_BASE:-https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/releases/download}"
123:   asset="impeccable-$os-$arch"
124:   [ "$os" = windows ] && asset="$asset.exe"
125:   url="$base/engine-v$version/$asset"
126:   tmp="$cache_root/bin/$version/.impeccable.part.$$"
127:   if ! mkdir -p "$cache_root/bin/$version" 2>/dev/null; then
128:     echo "impeccable: engine $version is not installed; cannot create cache directory: $cache_root/bin/$version" >&2
129:     setup_help
130:     exit 127
131:   fi
132:   # Check the actual staging file, not just directory existence: a cache from
133:   # an earlier run can be readable but no longer writable inside a sandbox.
134:   if ! (umask 077; : > "$tmp") 2>/dev/null; then
135:     echo "impeccable: engine $version is not installed; cannot write to cache directory: $cache_root/bin/$version" >&2
136:     setup_help
137:     exit 127
138:   fi
139:   fetched=0
140:   if fetch_url "$url"; then
141:     fetched=1
142:   elif [ "$os" = windows ] && [ "$arch" = arm64 ]; then
143:     # Windows on ARM runs x64 binaries; fall back when no arm64 asset exists.
144:     url="$base/engine-v$version/impeccable-windows-x64.exe"
145:     fetch_url "$url" && fetched=1
146:   fi
147:   if [ "$fetched" = 1 ]; then
148:     check_download
149:     # Fail closed: a freshly downloaded binary runs only after verifying
150:     # against its .sha256 sidecar. A sidecar that cannot be fetched, or a
151:     # machine with no sha256 tool, refuses the download instead of exec'ing
152:     # an unverified binary. (A binary already on PATH or in the cache that
153:     # passes engine-probe is unaffected.)
154:     sidecar_ok=0
155:     if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
156:       curl -fsSL --retry 2 -o "$tmp.sha256" "$url.sha256" 2>/dev/null && sidecar_ok=1
157:     elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
158:       wget -q -O "$tmp.sha256" "$url.sha256" 2>/dev/null && sidecar_ok=1
159:     fi
160:     check_download
161:     expected=""
162:     [ "$sidecar_ok" = 1 ] && expected=$(cut -d' ' -f1 < "$tmp.sha256")
163:     actual=""
164:     if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
165:       if digest=$(shasum -a 256 "$tmp" 2>/dev/null); then actual=${digest%% *}; fi
166:     elif command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
167:       if digest=$(sha256sum "$tmp" 2>/dev/null); then actual=${digest%% *}; fi
168:     fi
169:     check_download
170:     rm -f "$tmp.sha256"
171:     if [ -z "$expected" ] || [ -z "$actual" ]; then
172:       rm -f "$tmp"
173:       echo "impeccable: cannot verify $url against $url.sha256 (sidecar unavailable or hashing failed); refusing the unverified download" >&2
174:       exit 127
175:     fi
176:     if [ "$actual" != "$expected" ]; then
177:       rm -f "$tmp"
178:       echo "impeccable: checksum mismatch downloading $url" >&2
179:       exit 127
180:     fi
181:     check_download
182:     if ! chmod +x "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
183:       check_download
184:       rm -f "$tmp"
185:       echo "impeccable: could not make the verified download executable: $url" >&2
186:       exit 127
187:     fi
188:     check_download
189:     if ! mv -f "$tmp" "$cached" 2>/dev/null; then
190:       check_download
191:       rm -f "$tmp"
192:       echo "impeccable: could not cache the verified download: $url" >&2
193:       exit 127
194:     fi
195:     check_download "$cached"
196:     exec "$cached" "$@"
197:   fi
198:   rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
199:   echo "impeccable: could not download engine $version from $url; check network access, the release URL, and curl or wget availability." >&2
200:   setup_help
201:   exit 127
202: fi
203: 
204: echo "impeccable: no engine binary for $os-$arch found (looked in $bin, $cached, PATH)." >&2
205: echo "Download impeccable-$os-$arch from https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/releases (tag engine-v$version) into $cache_root/bin/$version/impeccable$exe (then chmod +x), or set IMPECCABLE_BIN to a preinstalled engine binary. Docs: https://impeccable.style" >&2
206: exit 127
````

## File: .github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable.cmd
````batch
  1: @echo off
  2: setlocal
  3: rem Impeccable launcher (Windows). Runs bin\windows-<arch>\impeccable.exe next
  4: rem to this file, else a cached or freshly downloaded engine binary.
  5: rem
  6: rem Structure notes (this file is exercised by dry parsing and string-level
  7: rem tests, not yet on a real Windows machine):
  8: rem - No multi-line parenthesized blocks: cmd expands %var% at block parse
  9: rem   time, which made the old download path read back empty %url%/%cached%.
 10: rem   Linear goto flow keeps every expansion on its own line, and avoids
 11: rem   delayed expansion eating ! characters in user arguments.
 12: rem - The unversioned user binary and the PATH candidate are validated with
 13: rem   the engine-probe handshake (see :probe) so the retired 3.x npm CLI,
 14: rem   whose bin is also named impeccable, is never exec'd. IMPECCABLE_BIN,
 15: rem   the sibling binary, and the version-pinned cache stay trusted.
 16: rem - Downloads are verified against the .sha256 sidecar via certutil and
 17: rem   fail closed: a missing sidecar or hash tool refuses the download. On
 18: rem   ARM64 the arm64 asset is tried first and the x64 asset is the
 19: rem   fallback (Windows on ARM runs x64 binaries).
 20: if not defined IMPECCABLE_SKILL_DIR set "IMPECCABLE_SKILL_DIR=%~dp0.."
 21: if not defined IMPECCABLE_SELF set "IMPECCABLE_SELF=%~f0"
 22: set "arch=x64"
 23: if /I "%PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE%"=="ARM64" set "arch=arm64"
 24: 
 25: if not defined IMPECCABLE_BIN goto no_env_bin
 26: if not exist "%IMPECCABLE_BIN%" goto no_env_bin
 27: set "run=%IMPECCABLE_BIN%"
 28: goto run
 29: :no_env_bin
 30: 
 31: set "bin=%~dp0bin\windows-%arch%\impeccable.exe"
 32: if not exist "%bin%" goto no_sibling
 33: set "run=%bin%"
 34: goto run
 35: :no_sibling
 36: 
 37: set "home_bin=%USERPROFILE%\.impeccable\bin\impeccable.exe"
 38: if not exist "%home_bin%" goto no_home_bin
 39: if defined IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE goto no_home_bin
 40: call :probe "%home_bin%"
 41: if not "%probe_ok%"=="1" goto no_home_bin
 42: set "run=%home_bin%"
 43: goto run
 44: :no_home_bin
 45: 
 46: set "version="
 47: if exist "%~dp0VERSION" set /p version=<"%~dp0VERSION"
 48: if not defined IMPECCABLE_HOME set "IMPECCABLE_HOME=%USERPROFILE%\.impeccable"
 49: set "cached=%IMPECCABLE_HOME%\bin\%version%\impeccable.exe"
 50: if not defined version goto no_cache
 51: if not exist "%cached%" goto no_cache
 52: set "run=%cached%"
 53: goto run
 54: :no_cache
 55: 
 56: if defined IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE goto download
 57: where impeccable >nul 2>nul
 58: if errorlevel 1 goto download
 59: call :probe impeccable
 60: if not "%probe_ok%"=="1" goto download
 61: impeccable %*
 62: exit /b
 63: 
 64: :download
 65: rem Last resort: fetch this version's binary from the release channel into
 66: rem the version-pinned user cache, verify it, then run it. Never inside
 67: rem another launcher's probe: fail fast and quiet instead.
 68: if defined IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE exit /b 127
 69: if not defined version goto fail
 70: where curl.exe >nul 2>nul
 71: if errorlevel 1 goto curl_missing
 72: if not defined IMPECCABLE_DOWNLOAD_BASE set "IMPECCABLE_DOWNLOAD_BASE=https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/releases/download"
 73: if exist "%IMPECCABLE_HOME%\bin\%version%\" goto cache_ready
 74: mkdir "%IMPECCABLE_HOME%\bin\%version%" >nul 2>nul
 75: if errorlevel 1 goto cache_directory_failed
 76: :cache_ready
 77: rem Check the staging file too: an existing directory may be read-only.
 78: rem Redirection failures do not reliably update ERRORLEVEL in cmd.exe;
 79: rem branch on the command's failure directly. Never treat a directory as a
 80: rem staging file (later del cleanup would prompt to delete its contents).
 81: if exist "%cached%.part\" goto cache_write_failed
 82: (type nul >"%cached%.part") 2>nul || goto cache_write_failed
 83: set "asset=impeccable-windows-%arch%.exe"
 84: set "url=%IMPECCABLE_DOWNLOAD_BASE%/engine-v%version%/%asset%"
 85: curl.exe -fsSL -o "%cached%.part" "%url%" >nul 2>nul
 86: if not errorlevel 1 goto verify
 87: if not "%arch%"=="arm64" goto download_failed
 88: set "asset=impeccable-windows-x64.exe"
 89: set "url=%IMPECCABLE_DOWNLOAD_BASE%/engine-v%version%/%asset%"
 90: curl.exe -fsSL -o "%cached%.part" "%url%" >nul 2>nul
 91: if errorlevel 1 goto download_failed
 92: 
 93: :verify
 94: call :check_download
 95: if errorlevel 1 exit /b 127
 96: rem Mirrors the sh launcher and fails closed: a freshly downloaded binary
 97: rem runs only after verifying against its .sha256 sidecar. A sidecar that
 98: rem cannot be fetched, or an empty certutil result, refuses the download
 99: rem instead of running an unverified binary.
100: curl.exe -fsSL -o "%cached%.sha256" "%url%.sha256" >nul 2>nul
101: if errorlevel 1 goto verify_refuse
102: set "expected="
103: set /p expected=<"%cached%.sha256"
104: for /f "tokens=1" %%h in ("%expected%") do set "expected=%%h"
105: call :check_download
106: if errorlevel 1 exit /b 127
107: set "actual="
108: rem Reuse the sidecar staging file after reading expected. Check certutil's
109: rem status before parsing: its error text on stdout is not a digest.
110: certutil -hashfile "%cached%.part" SHA256 >"%cached%.sha256" 2>nul
111: if errorlevel 1 goto verify_refuse
112: call :check_download
113: if errorlevel 1 exit /b 127
114: for /f "usebackq skip=1 delims=" %%h in ("%cached%.sha256") do if not defined actual set "actual=%%h"
115: del "%cached%.sha256" >nul 2>nul
116: if not defined expected goto verify_refuse
117: if not defined actual goto verify_refuse
118: set "actual=%actual: =%"
119: if /I "%actual%"=="%expected%" goto place
120: del "%cached%.part" >nul 2>nul
121: echo impeccable: checksum mismatch downloading %url% 1>&2
122: exit /b 127
123: 
124: :verify_refuse
125: call :check_download
126: if errorlevel 1 exit /b 127
127: del "%cached%.part" >nul 2>nul
128: del "%cached%.sha256" >nul 2>nul
129: echo impeccable: cannot verify %url% against %url%.sha256; refusing the unverified download 1>&2
130: exit /b 127
131: 
132: :check_download
133: set "download_file=%~1"
134: if not defined download_file set "download_file=%cached%.part"
135: if not exist "%download_file%" goto download_missing
136: for %%f in ("%download_file%") do if %%~zf==0 goto download_empty
137: exit /b 0
138: 
139: :download_missing
140: del "%cached%.sha256" >nul 2>nul
141: echo impeccable: download completed but the file was removed before execution: %url%; check your antivirus quarantine or logs. Refusing to continue; do not disable protection. 1>&2
142: exit /b 127
143: 
144: :download_empty
145: del "%download_file%" >nul 2>nul
146: del "%cached%.sha256" >nul 2>nul
147: echo impeccable: downloaded file is empty: %url%; refusing the unverified download 1>&2
148: exit /b 127
149: 
150: :place
151: call :check_download
152: if errorlevel 1 exit /b 127
153: move /y "%cached%.part" "%cached%" >nul 2>nul
154: if errorlevel 1 goto place_failed
155: call :check_download "%cached%"
156: if errorlevel 1 exit /b 127
157: set "run=%cached%"
158: goto run
159: 
160: :place_failed
161: call :check_download
162: if errorlevel 1 exit /b 127
163: del "%cached%.part" >nul 2>nul
164: echo impeccable: could not cache the verified download: %url% 1>&2
165: exit /b 127
166: 
167: :run
168: "%run%" %*
169: exit /b
170: 
171: :probe
172: rem Sets probe_ok=1 when %1 answers the engine handshake: prints
173: rem "impeccable-engine <version>" and exits 0. The 3.x npm CLI answers any
174: rem unknown verb with "Unknown command", exit 1, so it never passes.
175: set "probe_ok="
176: set "probe_tmp=%TEMP%\impeccable-probe-%RANDOM%%RANDOM%.txt"
177: set "IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE=1"
178: "%~1" engine-probe >"%probe_tmp%" 2>nul
179: set "probe_err=%ERRORLEVEL%"
180: set "IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE="
181: if not "%probe_err%"=="0" goto probe_done
182: findstr /b /c:"impeccable-engine" "%probe_tmp%" >nul 2>nul
183: if not errorlevel 1 set "probe_ok=1"
184: :probe_done
185: del "%probe_tmp%" >nul 2>nul
186: exit /b 0
187: 
188: :cache_directory_failed
189: echo impeccable: engine %version% is not installed; cannot create cache directory: "%IMPECCABLE_HOME%\bin\%version%" 1>&2
190: goto setup_failed
191: 
192: :cache_write_failed
193: echo impeccable: engine %version% is not installed; cannot write to cache directory: "%IMPECCABLE_HOME%\bin\%version%" 1>&2
194: goto setup_failed
195: 
196: :curl_missing
197: echo impeccable: cannot download engine %version%; curl.exe is unavailable. 1>&2
198: goto setup_failed
199: 
200: :download_failed
201: del "%cached%.part" >nul 2>nul
202: echo impeccable: could not download engine %version% from %url%; check network access and the release URL. 1>&2
203: 
204: :setup_failed
205: echo Engine %version% setup needs network access and write permission to "%IMPECCABLE_HOME%\bin\%version%". 1>&2
206: echo Run this launcher ("%~f0") with engine-probe in a terminal that has those permissions, then retry the original command. 1>&2
207: echo Alternatively, set IMPECCABLE_HOME to a writable cache location, or IMPECCABLE_BIN to a preinstalled engine binary. 1>&2
208: exit /b 127
209: 
210: :fail
211: del "%cached%.part" >nul 2>nul
212: echo impeccable: no engine binary found (looked in %bin%, %cached%, PATH). 1>&2
213: echo Download impeccable-windows-%arch%.exe from https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/releases (tag engine-v%version%) and save it as %cached%, or set IMPECCABLE_BIN to a preinstalled engine binary. Docs: https://impeccable.style 1>&2
````

 2438:       });

 2441:         dot.addEventListener('click', (e) => {

 9711:   function updateGlobalBarState() {

 9723:       btn.dataset.active = active ? 'true' : 'false';

10262:   function renderDesignChrome() {
10263:     const root = designShadow.querySelector('.root');
10264:     root.innerHTML = '';
10265:     // (Panel toggle lives in the global bar - no floating FAB.)
10266:     // Panel
10267:     const panel = document.createElement('aside');
10268:     panel.className = 'panel';
10269:     panel.setAttribute('data-open', designState.open ? 'true' : 'false');
10270:     panel.appendChild(buildDesignHeader());
10271:     const body = document.createElement('div');
10272:     body.className = 'panel-body';
10273:     body.id = 'panel-body';
10274:     panel.appendChild(body);
10275:     root.appendChild(panel);
10276:     renderDesignBody();
10277:   }
10278:   function buildDesignHeader() {
10279:     const header = document.createElement('div');
10280:     header.className = 'panel-header';
10281:     const title = document.createElement('div');
10282:     title.className = 'panel-title';
10283:     title.textContent = 'DESIGN.md';
10284:     header.appendChild(title);
10285:     const tabs = document.createElement('div');
10286:     tabs.className = 'tabs';
10287:     for (const t of [['visual', 'Visual'], ['raw', 'Raw']]) {
10288:       const btn = document.createElement('button');
10289:       btn.className = 'tab';
10290:       btn.textContent = t[1];
10291:       btn.setAttribute('data-active', designState.tab === t[0] ? 'true' : 'false');
10292:       btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
10293:         if (designState.tab === t[0]) return;
10294:         designState.tab = t[0];
10295:         saveDesignPrefs();
10296:         renderDesignChrome();
10297:         if (t[0] === 'raw' && designState.raw === null && !designState.loading) {
10298:           fetchDesignSystem();
10299:         }
10300:       });
10301:       tabs.appendChild(btn);
10302:     }
10303:     header.appendChild(tabs);
10304:     const close = document.createElement('button');
10305:     close.className = 'panel-close';
10306:     close.innerHTML = '&#x2715;';
10307:     close.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Close panel');
10308:     close.addEventListener('click', toggleDesignPanel);
10309:     header.appendChild(close);
10310:     return header;
10311:   }
10312:   function toggleDesignPanel() {
10313:     if (pendingApplyInFlight) { showManualApplyBusyToast(); return; }
10314:     designState.open = !designState.open;
10315:     renderDesignChrome();
10316:     updateGlobalBarState();
10317:     if (designState.open && designState.present === null && !designState.loading) {
10318:       fetchDesignSystem();
10319:     }
10320:   }
10321:   async function fetchDesignSystem() {
10322:     designState.loading = true;
10323:     designState.error = null;
10324:     renderDesignBody();
10325:     try {
10326:       const [jsonRes, rawRes] = await Promise.all([
10327:         fetch(`http://localhost:${PORT}/design-system.json?token=${TOKEN}`, { cache: 'no-store' }),
10328:         fetch(`http://localhost:${PORT}/design-system/raw?token=${TOKEN}`, { cache: 'no-store' }),
10329:       ]);
10330:       const jsonData = await jsonRes.json();
10331:       designState.present = jsonData.present === true;
10332:       designState.parsed = jsonData.parsed || null;
10333:       designState.sidecar = jsonData.sidecar || null;
10334:       designState.hasMd = !!jsonData.hasMd;
10335:       designState.hasSidecar = !!jsonData.hasSidecar;
10336:       designState.mdNewerThanJson = !!jsonData.mdNewerThanJson;
10337:       designState.raw = designState.present && rawRes.ok ? await rawRes.text() : null;

Running <code>${IMPECCABLE_COMMAND} document</code> also generates a <code>.impeccable/design.json</code> sidecar with your project's actual component snippets (button, input, nav) and tonal ramps, rendered live below the tokens.`;

10406:   function renderDesignVisual(body, parsed, sidecar) {

10424:       body.appendChild(renderOverviewCollapsible(narrative));
10425:     }
10426:     if (body.childElementCount === beforeCount) {
10427:       body.appendChild(msgDiv('empty', designEmptyMessage()));

10430:   function buildColorModels(fmColors, colorMeta, proseColors) {
10431:     if (!fmColors) return [];

10434:       const m = meta[key] || {};

10436:         role: m.role || humanizeKey(key),
10437:         name: m.displayName || humanizeKey(key),
10438:         value: normalizeCssColor(m.canonical || value),
10439:         canonical: m.canonical || null,
10440:         description: m.description || findProseDescription(proseColors, key, m.displayName),
10441:         tonalRamp: m.tonalRamp || null,
10442:       };
10443:     });
10444:   }
10445:   function buildTypographyModels(fmTypography, typographyMeta) {
10446:     if (!fmTypography) return [];
10447:     const meta = typographyMeta || {};

10463:     });
10464:   }
10465:   function buildRadiiModels(fmRounded) {

10467:     return Object.entries(fmRounded).map(([name, value]) => ({ name, value }));

10474:   function humanizeKey(k) {

10477:   function findProseDescription(proseColors, key, displayName) {

10490:   function synthesizeNarrative(parsed) {

10508:   function renderColorTiles(body, colors) {

10538:   function synthesizeRamp(c) {

10819:   function renderMarkdown(md) {

10892:       html += `<li>${it.html}</li>`;

## File: .github/skills/impeccable/SKILL.md
````markdown
 1: ---
 2: name: impeccable
 3: description: Use when the user wants to design, redesign, shape, critique, audit, polish, clarify, distill, harden, optimize, adapt, animate, colorize, extract, or otherwise improve a frontend interface. Covers websites, landing pages, dashboards, product UI, app shells, components, forms, settings, onboarding, and empty states. Handles UX review, visual hierarchy, information architecture, cognitive load, accessibility, performance, responsive behavior, theming, anti-patterns, typography, fonts, spacing, layout, alignment, color, motion, micro-interactions, UX copy, error states, edge cases, i18n, and reusable design systems or tokens. Also use for bland designs that need to become bolder or more delightful, loud designs that should become quieter, live browser iteration on UI elements, or ambitious visual effects that should feel technically extraordinary. Not for backend-only or non-UI tasks.
 4: version: 4.3.1
 5: user-invocable: true
 6: argument-hint: "[shape · audit|critique · animate|bolder|colorize|delight|layout|overdrive|quieter|typeset · adapt|clarify|distill · harden|onboard|optimize|polish · init|document|extract|live] [target]"
 7: license: Apache 2.0
 8: ---
 9: 
10: This skill gives you the tools and permission to create design that earns to be called out-of-distribution craft: Whereas before, your design work would have been safe, timid and measured, you now approach every design task as an award-winning design director with impeccable understanding for what makes exceptional design work: production-grade code, peak creativity, a clear POV, deep understanding of the needs of the client and users, and exceptional craft.
11: 
12: Core principles:
13: - Go all out. No hedging, no shortcuts. The deliverable must be complete (except assets the user must provide).
14: - Dream big and bold. Distinct, beautiful, outstanding and highly inspiring work.
15: - Verify in bounded passes, not a loop, and the ceiling covers the whole cycle: screenshots, defect scans, micro-edits, and rebuilds alike. Build fully, inspect once with a batched round (desktop and mobile together on the web; the shipped device classes on a native platform), fix everything it shows in one batch, confirm with at most one more round, and stop polishing. Open-ended self-QA burns the user's money doing worse what the finish handoffs do better.
16: 
17: ## Setup
18: 
19: 1. Run `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable context` once per session, where `<skill-base-dir>` is the directory that contains this SKILL.md (the skill folder, not a plugin root two levels above it); keep cwd at the user's project. That base directory resolves every `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable <verb>` command in this skill and its references, and `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts` is the fallback only when the runtime reports no base directory. On a Windows shell without `sh`, call `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable.cmd` instead. The launcher runs a self-contained binary that ships next to it or is downloaded once on first run; no Node or other runtime is required. Pass a named source file or route as `--target <path>`. It loads PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, the matching surface brief, and native-platform guidance when applicable; follow its directives and do not rerun it.
20: 2. Load the request's playbook: its Commands-table reference for an explicit/implied sub-command, or [reference/new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for a new surface or replacement visual world. Inspect target and incumbent visual truth before editing. When the app cannot run, start with committed visual-regression goldens or screenshot fixtures; verify target and freshness against current tokens, CSS, components, or assets, resolve conflicts, and compare theme/variant captures.
21: 3. After resolving analysis and direction, read [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, including small refinements. It carries the quality floor, the absolute bans, and the reflexes no detector catches. Do not load it for planning-only work.
22: 
23: **Launcher unavailable:** On refusal or failure, send a separate message **before the next tool call**: “Context loading did not run; I’ll read the existing project context directly.” Then read existing PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md without inventing missing context, follow applicable steps 2–3, and continue through permitted tools. This applies to planning and editing; launcher failure alone does not block either.
24: 
25: ## How to design
26: 
27: - **The brief wins.** Honor pinned aesthetics, eras, materials, fonts, and palettes even when they conflict with a saturated-pattern warning. Redirecting a clear brief toward your taste is failure.
28: - **Refinement preserves; redesign replaces.** Refinement keeps the incumbent identity, behavior, copy, and everything outside scope. Ask before replacing factual copy or adding claims. Redesign keeps product truth, content, function, native affordances, and constraints, but treats the old look as evidence and anti-reference; choose a replacement world in new-work and replace DESIGN.md. Never split the difference into polish on the discarded look.
29: - **Visual authority is evidence, not a filename.** Missing DESIGN.md alone does not make a project greenfield; new-work decides whether to preserve, expand, or replace the incumbent world.
30: 
31: ## Modes
32: 
33: The mode names what the visitor's success looks like on this surface.
34: 
35: - **Persuade:** the visitor decides and acts; design is the product. Landing pages, marketing, campaigns, pricing. Earn attention and action. Ship real imagery when the brief needs it; follow the committed world, not category habit.
36: - **Operate:** the visitor completes a task. App UI, dashboards, editors, admin, settings, tools. Scanability, consistency, native expectations, and the real usage scene outrank expression. Brand lives in precise details.
37: - **Read:** the visitor understands something. Docs, articles, guides, help, changelogs. Structure for comprehension, then make the reading experience worth staying in.
38: - **Experience:** the visitor is inside the work itself. Portfolios, galleries, showcases. Let the artifact lead from the first viewport; the interface recedes.
39: 
40: Choose the mode from the requested surface, not the product, and persist it only in that surface brief. A tool's landing page is still Persuade; a fashion house's documentation is still Read; a docs index is Read, not Persuade. See [new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for new surfaces and [operate.md](reference/operate.md) for deeper Operate/Read guidance.
41: 
42: ## Commands
43: 
44: | Command | Category | Description | Reference |
45: |---|---|---|---|
46: | `craft [feature]` | Build | Deprecated alias for an ordinary new-work request | [reference/craft.md](reference/craft.md) |
47: | `shape [feature]` | Build | Plan UX/UI before writing code | [reference/shape.md](reference/shape.md) |
48: | `init` | Build | Capture durable product context in PRODUCT.md | [reference/init.md](reference/init.md) |
49: | `document` | Build | Generate DESIGN.md from existing project code | [reference/document.md](reference/document.md) |
50: | `extract [target]` | Build | Pull reusable tokens and components into design system | [reference/extract.md](reference/extract.md) |
51: | `critique [target]` | Evaluate | UX design review with heuristic scoring | [reference/critique.md](reference/critique.md) |
52: | `audit [target]` | Evaluate | Technical quality checks (a11y, perf, responsive) | [reference/audit.md](reference/audit.md) · native: [reference/audit.native.md](reference/audit.native.md) |
53: | `polish [target]` | Refine | Final quality pass before shipping | [reference/polish.md](reference/polish.md) |
54: | `bolder [target]` | Refine | Amplify safe or bland designs | [reference/bolder.md](reference/bolder.md) |
55: | `quieter [target]` | Refine | Tone down aggressive or overstimulating designs | [reference/quieter.md](reference/quieter.md) |
56: | `distill [target]` | Refine | Strip to essence, remove complexity | [reference/distill.md](reference/distill.md) |
57: | `harden [target]` | Refine | Production-ready: errors, i18n, edge cases | [reference/harden.md](reference/harden.md) |
58: | `onboard [target]` | Refine | Design first-run flows, empty states, activation | [reference/onboard.md](reference/onboard.md) |
59: | `animate [target]` | Enhance | Add purposeful animations and motion | [reference/animate.md](reference/animate.md) |
60: | `colorize [target]` | Enhance | Add strategic color to monochromatic UIs | [reference/colorize.md](reference/colorize.md) |
61: | `typeset [target]` | Enhance | Improve typography hierarchy and fonts | [reference/typeset.md](reference/typeset.md) |
62: | `layout [target]` | Enhance | Fix spacing, rhythm, and visual hierarchy | [reference/layout.md](reference/layout.md) |
63: | `delight [target]` | Enhance | Add personality and memorable touches | [reference/delight.md](reference/delight.md) |
64: | `overdrive [target]` | Enhance | Push past conventional limits | [reference/overdrive.md](reference/overdrive.md) |
65: | `clarify [target]` | Fix | Improve UX copy, labels, and error messages | [reference/clarify.md](reference/clarify.md) |
66: | `adapt [target]` | Fix | Adapt for different devices and screen sizes | [reference/adapt.md](reference/adapt.md) · native: [reference/adapt.native.md](reference/adapt.native.md) |
67: | `optimize [target]` | Fix | Diagnose and fix UI performance | [reference/optimize.md](reference/optimize.md) |
68: | `live` | Iterate | Visual variant mode: pick elements in the browser, generate alternatives | [reference/live.md](reference/live.md) |
69: 
70: Routing:
71: 
72: - **No argument:** read [routing.md](reference/routing.md) and present its context-aware menu; never auto-run a command.
73: - **Explicit or clearly implied request to run a command:** load its reference (native variant on native platforms) and follow it. Ask once if two commands fit.
74: - **Workflow or command-selection question:** read [Workflow questions](reference/routing.md#workflow-questions).
75: - **Otherwise:** treat the request as general design work. Missing PRODUCT.md routes a new surface or replacement world through init, then new-work; a narrow refinement of existing code proceeds on the incumbent implementation as `impeccable context` directs, offering init afterward rather than blocking on it.
76: - `teach` aliases `init`. `craft` is a deprecated alias for ordinary new-work and adds nothing. `shape` owns task discovery, then enters new-work only for visual-world and surface-concept decisions.
77: 
78: After init writes PRODUCT.md, resume without rerunning `impeccable context`; init loads the native platform reference itself when the platform it recorded is `ios`, `android`, or `adaptive`.
79: 
80: **Pin / Unpin:** `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable pin <pin|unpin> <command>` creates or removes a standalone `/<command>` shortcut. Report the script's result concisely; relay stderr verbatim on error.
81: 
82: **Hooks:** `/impeccable hooks <on|off|status|ignore-rule|ignore-file|ignore-value|reset>` manages the design detector hook for this project (auto-runs the detector after UI file edits and surfaces findings). Load [reference/hooks.md](reference/hooks.md) when the user invokes it with any argument.
83: 
84: **Doctor:** `/impeccable doctor` reports and repairs drift between this project's Impeccable artifacts (PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md and its sidecar, config, surface briefs, the hook) and what this version reads. Load [reference/doctor.md](reference/doctor.md) when the user invokes it, or when they ask what is out of date, stale, or needs refreshing. A `CONTEXT_STALE` directive in Setup's output is the cheap subset of the same report; act on it there per its own instructions rather than running doctor unasked.
85: 
86: **Never repair drift as a side effect of a design task.** A `CONTEXT_STALE` finding is reported, not acted on, unless the user asks. The one exception is a finding marked `auto`, which the next write to that file performs anyway.
````

````html
  498:       * {
  499:         margin: 0;
  500:         padding: 0;
  501:         box-sizing: border-box;
  502:       }
  503:       body {
  504:         font-family:
  505:           "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas,
  506:           "DejaVu Sans Mono", "Liberation Mono", "Noto Sans Mono CJK SC",
  507:           "PingFang SC", "Hiragino Sans GB", "Microsoft YaHei", monospace;
  508:         background: var(--bg);
  509:         min-height: 100vh;
  510:         padding: 2rem;
  511:         color: var(--text);
  512:         transition:
  513:           background 0.2s ease,
  514:           color 0.2s ease;
  515:       }
  516:       html[data-preset="signal-flow"] body {
  517:         background-image:
  518:           radial-gradient(
  519:             circle at 18% -8%,
  520:             rgba(34, 211, 238, 0.14),
  521:             transparent 34rem
  522:           ),
  523:           radial-gradient(
  524:             circle at 92% 18%,
  525:             rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.12),
  526:             transparent 30rem
  527:           );
  528:         background-attachment: fixed;
  529:       }
  530:       html[data-preset="signal-flow"][data-theme="light"] body {
  531:         background-image:
  532:           radial-gradient(
  533:             circle at 18% -8%,
  534:             rgba(6, 182, 212, 0.12),
  535:             transparent 34rem
  536:           ),
  537:           radial-gradient(
  538:             circle at 92% 18%,
  539:             rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.08),
  540:             transparent 30rem
  541:           );
  542:       }
  543:       html[data-preset="blueprint"] body {
  544:         background-image:
  545:           linear-gradient(var(--grid) 1px, transparent 1px),
  546:           linear-gradient(90deg, var(--grid) 1px, transparent 1px);
  547:         background-size: 32px 32px;
  548:         background-position: -1px -1px;
  549:         background-attachment: fixed;
  550:       }
  551:       html[data-preset="editorial"] body {
  552:         background-image:
  553:           linear-gradient(
  554:             90deg,
  555:             transparent 0,
  556:             transparent 5.4rem,
  557:             color-mix(in srgb, var(--security-stroke) 18%, transparent) 5.4rem,
  558:             color-mix(in srgb, var(--security-stroke) 18%, transparent)
  559:               calc(5.4rem + 1px),
  560:             transparent calc(5.4rem + 1px)
  561:           ),
  562:           repeating-linear-gradient(
  563:             0deg,
  564:             transparent 0,
  565:             transparent 31px,
  566:             color-mix(in srgb, var(--grid) 36%, transparent) 31px,
  567:             color-mix(in srgb, var(--grid) 36%, transparent) 32px
  568:           );
  569:         background-attachment: fixed;
  570:       }
  571:       /* Gallery/embed mode keeps the generated artifact as the source of truth
  572:        while presenting only its diagram surface inside a proof card. */
  573:       html[data-embed="true"] body {
  574:         min-height: 0;
  575:         padding: 0;
  576:         overflow: hidden;
  577:         background: var(--bg);
  578:         background-image: none;
  579:       }
  580:       html[data-embed="true"] .toolbar,
  581:       html[data-embed="true"] .header,
  582:       html[data-embed="true"] .cards,
  583:       html[data-embed="true"] .diagram-nav,
  584:       html[data-embed="true"] .overview-map,
  585:       html[data-embed="true"] .focus-chip,
  586:       html[data-embed="true"] .route-probe,
  587:       html[data-embed="true"] .semantic-lens,
  588:       html[data-embed="true"] .diagram-guide,
  589:       html[data-embed="true"] .node-finder,
  590:       html[data-embed="true"] .guided-views {
  591:         display: none !important;
  592:       }
  593:       html[data-embed="true"] .container {
  594:         max-width: none;
  595:       }
  596:       html[data-embed="true"] .diagram-container {
  597:         padding: 0.5rem;
  598:         border: 0;
  599:         border-radius: 0;
  600:         box-shadow: none;
  601:       }
  602:       html[data-embed="true"] .diagram-container svg {
  603:         min-width: 0;
  604:       }
  605:       /* Share Chapter Cue lives in the HTML viewer layer, not inside the SVG.
  606:        It gives one-shot embeds a title, authored note, truthful stop order,
  607:        and lifecycle state while canonical diagram geometry stays untouched. */
  608:       .share-chapter-cue {
  609:         display: none;
  610:       }
  611:       html[data-embed="true"][data-share-playback="true"]
  612:         .share-chapter-cue:not([hidden]),
  613:       html[data-embed="true"][data-share-moment="true"]
  614:         .share-chapter-cue:not([hidden]) {
  615:         position: absolute;
  616:         z-index: 18;
  617:         top: 0.85rem;
  618:         left: 50%;
  619:         display: grid;
  620:         grid-template-columns: auto minmax(9rem, 13.5rem) minmax(0, 1fr);
  621:         align-items: center;
  622:         gap: 0.45rem 0.85rem;
  623:         width: min(52rem, calc(100% - 1.5rem));
  624:         min-height: 3.35rem;
  625:         padding: 0.55rem 0.75rem 0.65rem;
  626:         overflow: hidden;
  627:         border: 1px solid
  628:           color-mix(in srgb, var(--frontend-stroke) 42%, var(--toolbar-border));
  629:         border-radius: 0.75rem;
  630:         background:
  631:           linear-gradient(
  632:             115deg,
  633:             color-mix(in srgb, var(--frontend-fill) 52%, transparent),
  634:             transparent 45%
  635:           ),
  636:           color-mix(in srgb, var(--toolbar-menu-bg) 92%, transparent);
  637:         color: var(--toolbar-text);
  638:         box-shadow:
  639:           0 14px 42px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3),
  640:           inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.045);
  641:         backdrop-filter: blur(16px);
  642:         pointer-events: none;
  643:         animation: archify-share-cue-enter 280ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)
  644:           both;
  645:       }
  646:       html[data-preset="blueprint"] .share-chapter-cue {
  647:         border-radius: 0.2rem;
  648:         background:
  649:           linear-gradient(
  650:             90deg,
  651:             color-mix(in srgb, var(--frontend-fill) 46%, transparent),
  652:             transparent 36%
  653:           ),
  654:           var(--toolbar-menu-bg);
  655:         box-shadow: 0 10px 28px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2);
  656:         backdrop-filter: none;
  657:       }
  658:       html[data-preset="editorial"] .share-chapter-cue {
  659:         border-color: var(--panel-border);
  660:         background:
  661:           linear-gradient(
  662:             90deg,
  663:             color-mix(in srgb, var(--security-fill) 58%, transparent),
  664:             transparent 42%
  665:           ),
  666:           var(--toolbar-menu-bg);
  667:         box-shadow: 0 10px 30px color-mix(in srgb, #000 18%, transparent);
  668:         backdrop-filter: none;
  669:       }
  670:       html[data-preset="editorial"] .share-chapter-state {
  671:         color: var(--arrow-emphasis);
  672:       }
  673:       html[data-preset="editorial"] .share-chapter-state::before {
  674:         border-radius: 0;
  675:         box-shadow: none;
  676:         transform: rotate(45deg) scale(0.8);
  677:       }
  678:       .share-chapter-index {
  679:         display: grid;
  680:         gap: 0.12rem;
  681:         min-width: 5rem;
  682:         padding-right: 0.75rem;
  683:         border-right: 1px solid var(--toolbar-border);
  684:       }
  685:       .share-chapter-state {
  686:         display: inline-flex;
  687:         align-items: center;
  688:         gap: 0.36rem;

  770:        Embed mode wins when both query parameters are present. */

 1380:         top: var(--archify-radar-top, 1rem);

 1672:           linear-gradient(

 1680:         backdrop-filter: blur(18px);

 1682:       }

 1689:       }

 1696:       }
 1697:       .semantic-lens-head {
 1698:         display: grid;
 1699:         grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) auto;
 1700:         align-items: start;
 1701:         gap: 0.75rem;

 1703:         border-bottom: 1px solid var(--toolbar-border);
 1704:       }

 1729:         font-size: 1rem;

 1731:       }

 1735:       }
 1736:       .semantic-lens-instruction {
 1737:         margin: 0;

 8963:       <div class="cards">
 8964:         <div class="card">
 8965:           <div class="card-header">
 8966:             <div class="card-dot rose"></div>
 8967:             <h3>4-Tier Authorization &amp; Auth</h3>
 8968:           </div>
 8969:           <ul>
 8970:             <li>
 8971:               &bull; Better Auth session and RBAC guards (requireAuth,
 8972:               requireRole) protect mutating endpoints
 8973:             </li>
 8974:             <li>
 8975:               &bull; Resource ownership asserts user identity and
 8976:               DRAFT/PUBLISHED lifecycle state constraints
 8977:             </li>
 8978:           </ul>
 8979:         </div>
 8980:         <div class="card">
 8981:           <div class="card-header">
 8982:             <div class="card-dot amber"></div>
 8983:             <h3>Concurrency &amp; Transactions</h3>
 8984:           </div>
 8985:           <ul>
 8986:             <li>
 8987:               &bull; Parent Course Row Locking (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE)
 8988:               serializes curriculum mutations
 8989:             </li>
 8990:             <li>
 8991:               &bull; Two-Phase Reordering (-1 - i) and P2002 retry handlers
 8992:               prevent unique key collisions
 8993:             </li>
 8994:           </ul>
 8995:         </div>
 8996:         <div class="card">
 8997:           <div class="card-header">
 8998:             <div class="card-dot emerald"></div>
 8999:             <h3>Architecture &amp; Quality Rules</h3>
 9000:           </div>
 9001:           <ul>
 9002:             <li>
 9003:               &bull; Strict downward flow: UI calls Actions, Services hold
 9004:               logic, Repositories query database
 9005:             </li>
 9006:             <li>
 9007:               &bull; Sanitized Markdown reader, sandboxed 16:9 media player, and
 9008:               Sentry runtime telemetry
 9009:             </li>
 9010:           </ul>
 9011:         </div>
 9012:       </div>
 9013:     </div>
 9014:     <script>
 9015:       var Archify = {};
 9016:       var archifyI18nData = (function () {
 9017:         var node = document.getElementById("archify-i18n-data");
 9018:         try {
 9019:           return JSON.parse(node ? node.textContent : "{}");
 9020:         } catch (_) {
 9021:           return { locale: "en", messages: {} };
 9022:         }
 9023:       })();
 9024:       Archify.locale = archifyI18nData.locale || "en";
 9025:       function viewerText(key, values) {
 9026:         var messages = archifyI18nData.messages || {};
 9027:         var template = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(messages, key)
 9028:           ? messages[key]
 9029:           : key;
 9030:         return String(template).replace(
 9031:           /\{([a-zA-Z0-9_]+)\}/g,
 9032:           function (match, name) {
 9033:             return values && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(values, name)
 9034:               ? String(values[name])
 9035:               : match;
 9036:           },
 9037:         );
 9038:       }
 9039:       function viewerCount(key, count, values) {
 9040:         var suffix = Number(count) === 1 ? ".one" : ".other";
 9041:         var payload = Object.assign({}, values || {}, { count: count });
 9042:         return viewerText(key + suffix, payload);
 9043:       }
 9044:       function viewerKindLabel(value) {
 9045:         var normalized = String(value || "node").toLowerCase();
 9046:         var knownKey = "viewer.kind." + normalized;
 9047:         var known = viewerText(knownKey);
 9048:         if (known !== knownKey) return known;
 9049:         return normalized
````

````typescript
 1: import "dotenv/config";
 2: import { PrismaClient } from "@prisma/client";
 3: import { PrismaNeon } from "@prisma/adapter-neon";
 4: import { neonConfig } from "@neondatabase/serverless";
 5: import ws from "ws";
 6: neonConfig.webSocketConstructor = ws;
 7: const connectionString = process.env.DIRECT_URL || process.env.DATABASE_URL;
 8: const adapter = connectionString
 9:   ? new PrismaNeon({ connectionString })
10:   : undefined;
11: const prisma = adapter ? new PrismaClient({ adapter }) : new PrismaClient();
12: export async function seedLmsRolesAndPermissions() {
13:   const permissions = [
14:     {
15:       name: "roles:assign",
16:       description: "Assign and manage user roles",
17:       resource: "role",
18:       action: "assign",
19:     },
20:   ];
21:   for (const perm of permissions) {
22:     await prisma.permission.upsert({
23:       where: { name: perm.name },
24:       update: { description: perm.description },
25:       create: perm,
26:     });
27:   }
28:   const roles = [
29:     {
30:       name: "student",
31:       description: "Student persona enrolled in courses",
32:       permissions: [],
33:     },
34:     {
35:       name: "instructor",
36:       description: "Instructor persona who creates and manages courses",
37:       permissions: [],
38:     },
39:     {
40:       name: "admin",
41:       description: "Platform administrator with full role management authority",
42:       permissions: ["roles:assign"],
43:     },
44:   ];
45:   for (const r of roles) {
46:     const role = await prisma.role.upsert({
47:       where: { name: r.name },
48:       update: { description: r.description },
49:       create: { name: r.name, description: r.description },
50:     });
51:     for (const permName of r.permissions) {
52:       const perm = await prisma.permission.findUnique({
53:         where: { name: permName },
54:       });
55:       if (perm) {
56:         await prisma.rolePermission.upsert({
57:           where: {
58:             roleId_permissionId: {
59:               roleId: role.id,
60:               permissionId: perm.id,
61:             },
62:           },
63:           update: {},
64:           create: {
65:             roleId: role.id,
66:             permissionId: perm.id,
67:           },
68:         });
69:       }
70:     }
71:   }
72: }
73: async function main() {
74:   console.log("Seeding LMS roles and permissions...");
75:   await seedLmsRolesAndPermissions();
76:   console.log("Seeding completed successfully.");
77: }
78: if (require.main === module) {
79:   main()
80:     .catch((e) => {
81:       console.error("Seeding error:", e);
82:       process.exit(1);
83:     })
84:     .finally(async () => {
85:       await prisma.$disconnect();
86:     });
87: }
````

## File: src/__tests__/security/xss.test.ts
````typescript
  1: import { markdownToSanitizedHtml } from "@/lib/sanitizer";
  2: import * as lessonContentService from "@/services/lesson-content";
  3: import * as lessonContentRepository from "@/repositories/lesson-content";
  4: import * as authorizationService from "@/services/authorization";
  5: import { CourseStatus } from "@prisma/client";
  6: jest.mock("@/repositories/lesson-content");

 11: const mockAuthService = authorizationService as jest.Mocked<
 12:   typeof authorizationService
 13: >;
 14: describe("Security Audit: XSS Sanitization & HTML Escaping Penetration Tests", () => {
 15:   describe("1. Markdown to Sanitized HTML Pipeline", () => {
 16:     it("neutralizes raw <script> execution tags", async () => {
 17:       const hostilePayload = `
 18: # Dangerous Lesson
 19: <script>alert('XSS-ATTACK');</script>
 20: <script src="https://evil.com/malicious.js"></script>
 21: Regular markdown content.
 22:       `;
 23:       const cleanHtml = await markdownToSanitizedHtml(hostilePayload);
 24:       expect(cleanHtml).not.toContain("<script");
 25:       expect(cleanHtml).not.toContain("alert('XSS-ATTACK')");
 26:       expect(cleanHtml).not.toContain("https://evil.com/malicious.js");
 27:       expect(cleanHtml).toContain("Dangerous Lesson");
 28:       expect(cleanHtml).toContain("Regular markdown content.");
 29:     });
 30:     it("strips inline event handlers from tags (onerror, onload, onclick, onmouseover)", async () => {
 31:       const hostilePayload = `
 32: <img src="x" onerror="alert(document.cookie)" />
 33: <img src="https://example.com/image.png" onload="fetch('https://evil.com?c=' + document.cookie)" />
 34: <b onmouseover="alert('hover')">Hover me</b>
 35: <a href="https://example.com" onclick="stealData()">Safe looking link</a>
 36:       `;
 37:       const cleanHtml = await markdownToSanitizedHtml(hostilePayload);
 38:       expect(cleanHtml).not.toContain("onerror");
 39:       expect(cleanHtml).not.toContain("onload");
 40:       expect(cleanHtml).not.toContain("onmouseover");
 41:       expect(cleanHtml).not.toContain("onclick");
 42:       expect(cleanHtml).not.toContain("stealData");
 43:       expect(cleanHtml).not.toContain("document.cookie");
 44:     });
 45:     it("neutralizes javascript:, vbscript:, and data: pseudo-protocol schemes in links", async () => {
 46:       const hostilePayload = `
 47: [Malicious Link 1](javascript:alert(1))
 48: [Malicious Link 2](jav&#x09;ascript:alert(2))
 49: [Malicious Link 3](data:text/html;base64,PHNjcmlwdD5hbGVydCgxKTwvc2NyaXB0Pg==)
 50: [Malicious Link 4](vbscript:msgbox(1))
 51: [Valid Secure Link](https://learn.example.com/guide)
 52:       `;
 53:       const cleanHtml = await markdownToSanitizedHtml(hostilePayload);
 54:       expect(cleanHtml).not.toContain('href="javascript:');
 55:       expect(cleanHtml).not.toContain('href="data:');
 56:       expect(cleanHtml).not.toContain('href="vbscript:');
 57:       expect(cleanHtml).toContain('href="https://learn.example.com/guide"');
 58:     });
 59:     it("strictly isolates iframes to trusted video hosts (YouTube, Vimeo, Loom) over HTTPS", async () => {
 60:       const hostilePayload = `
 61: <iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ"></iframe>
 62: <iframe src="https://player.vimeo.com/video/123456"></iframe>
 63: <iframe src="https://www.loom.com/embed/abc123xyz"></iframe>
 64: <iframe src="https://attacker.evil.com/phishing-login"></iframe>
 65: <iframe src="http://www.youtube.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ"></iframe>
 66: <iframe src="javascript:alert(1)"></iframe>
 67:       `;
 68:       const cleanHtml = await markdownToSanitizedHtml(hostilePayload);
 69:       expect(cleanHtml).toContain("https://www.youtube.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ");
 70:       expect(cleanHtml).toContain("https://player.vimeo.com/video/123456");
 71:       expect(cleanHtml).toContain("https://www.loom.com/embed/abc123xyz");
 72:       expect(cleanHtml).not.toContain("attacker.evil.com");
 73:       expect(cleanHtml).not.toContain("http://www.youtube.com");
 74:       expect(cleanHtml).not.toContain("javascript:");
 75:     });
 76:     it("neutralizes dangerous HTML elements: object, embed, meta, base, link, svg", async () => {
````

## File: src/actions/course.ts
````typescript
  1: "use server";
  2: import { requireAuth } from "@/lib/auth-helpers";
  3: import {
  4:   actionSuccess,
  5:   actionFailure,
  6:   type ActionResult,
  7: } from "@/lib/action-result";
  8: import {
  9:   createCourseSchema,
 10:   updateCourseSchema,
 11: } from "@/lib/validations/course";
 12: import * as courseService from "@/services/course";
 13: import {
 14:   AuthenticationError,
 15:   AuthorizationError,
 16:   NotFoundError,
 17:   ValidationError,
 18:   ConflictError,
 19: } from "@/lib/errors";
 20: import type { Course } from "@prisma/client";
 21: function handleActionError(error: unknown, defaultMessage: string) {
 22:   if (error instanceof AuthenticationError) {
 23:     return actionFailure("Authentication required", "UNAUTHORIZED");
 24:   }
 25:   if (error instanceof AuthorizationError) {
 26:     return actionFailure(error.message, "FORBIDDEN");
 27:   }
 28:   if (error instanceof NotFoundError) {
 29:     return actionFailure(error.message, "NOT_FOUND");
 30:   }
 31:   if (error instanceof ValidationError) {
 32:     return actionFailure(error.message, "VALIDATION_ERROR", error.errors);
 33:   }
 34:   if (error instanceof ConflictError) {
 35:     return actionFailure(error.message, "CONFLICT");
 36:   }
 37:   return actionFailure(defaultMessage);
 38: }
 39: export async function createCourseAction(
 40:   input: unknown,
 41: ): Promise<ActionResult<Course>> {
 42:   try {
 43:     const session = await requireAuth();
 44:     const parsed = createCourseSchema.safeParse(input);
 45:     if (!parsed.success) {
 46:       const fieldErrors = parsed.error.flatten().fieldErrors;
 47:       const firstMessage = parsed.error.issues[0]?.message ?? "Invalid input";
 48:       return actionFailure(firstMessage, "VALIDATION_ERROR", fieldErrors);
 49:     }
 50:     const course = await courseService.createCourse(
 51:       session.user.id,
 52:       parsed.data,
 53:     );
 54:     return actionSuccess(course);
 55:   } catch (error) {
 56:     return handleActionError(error, "Failed to create course");
 57:   }
 58: }
 59: export async function updateCourseAction(
 60:   courseId: string,
 61:   input: unknown,
 62: ): Promise<ActionResult<Course>> {
 63:   try {
 64:     const session = await requireAuth();
 65:     const parsed = updateCourseSchema.safeParse(input);
 66:     if (!parsed.success) {
 67:       const fieldErrors = parsed.error.flatten().fieldErrors;
 68:       const firstMessage = parsed.error.issues[0]?.message ?? "Invalid input";
 69:       return actionFailure(firstMessage, "VALIDATION_ERROR", fieldErrors);
 70:     }
 71:     const updated = await courseService.updateCourse(
 72:       session.user.id,
 73:       courseId,
 74:       parsed.data,
 75:     );
 76:     return actionSuccess(updated);
 77:   } catch (error) {
 78:     return handleActionError(error, "Failed to update course");
 79:   }
 80: }
 81: export async function deleteCourseAction(
 82:   courseId: string,
 83: ): Promise<ActionResult<Course>> {
 84:   try {
 85:     const session = await requireAuth();
 86:     const deleted = await courseService.deleteCourse(session.user.id, courseId);
 87:     return actionSuccess(deleted);
 88:   } catch (error) {
 89:     return handleActionError(error, "Failed to delete course");
 90:   }
 91: }
 92: export async function publishCourseAction(
````

## File: src/app/courses/[slug]/learn/page.tsx
````typescript
 1: import { notFound, redirect } from "next/navigation";
 2: import { getCurrentUser } from "@/lib/auth-helpers";
 3: import { getCourseOverview } from "@/services/course";
 4: import { getNextLesson } from "@/services/progress";
 5: import { hasRole } from "@/services/authorization";
 6: import { NotFoundError } from "@/lib/errors";
 7: interface LearnRedirectPageProps {
 8:   params: Promise<{
 9:     slug: string;
10:   }>;
11: }
12: export default async function LearnRedirectPage({
13:   params,
14: }: LearnRedirectPageProps) {
15:   const { slug } = await params;
16:   const user = await getCurrentUser();
17:   let overviewData: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof getCourseOverview>>;
18:   try {
19:     overviewData = await getCourseOverview(slug, user?.id);
20:   } catch (error) {
21:     if (error instanceof NotFoundError) {
22:       notFound();
23:     }
24:     throw error;
25:   }
26:   const { course, modules, isEnrolled, totalLessons } = overviewData;
27:   if (totalLessons === 0 || modules.length === 0) {
28:     redirect(`/courses/${slug}`);
29:   }
30:   const firstLesson = modules[0]?.lessons[0];
31:   if (!firstLesson) {
32:     redirect(`/courses/${slug}`);
33:   }
34:   let firstPreviewLesson: { id: string } | null = null;
35:   for (const mod of modules) {
36:     const preview = mod.lessons.find((l) => l.isFreePreview);
37:     if (preview) {
38:       firstPreviewLesson = preview;
39:       break;
40:     }
41:   }
42:   const isOwner = user ? course.instructorId === user.id : false;
43:   const isAdmin = user ? await hasRole(user.id, "admin") : false;
44:   if (isOwner || isAdmin) {
45:     redirect(`/courses/${slug}/lessons/${firstLesson.id}`);
46:   }
47:   if (user && isEnrolled) {
48:     const next = await getNextLesson(user.id, course.id);
49:     if (next) {
50:       redirect(`/courses/${slug}/lessons/${next.id}`);
51:     } else {
52:       redirect(`/courses/${slug}/lessons/${firstLesson.id}`);
53:     }
54:   }
55:   if (firstPreviewLesson) {
56:     redirect(`/courses/${slug}/lessons/${firstPreviewLesson.id}`);
57:   }
58:   redirect(`/courses/${slug}`);
59: }
````

## File: src/components/features/player/player-context.tsx
````typescript
 1: "use client";
 2: import { createContext, useContext, useMemo, useState } from "react";
 3: interface PlayerContextType {
 4:   isSidebarOpen: boolean;
 5:   openSidebar: () => void;
 6:   closeSidebar: () => void;
 7:   toggleSidebar: () => void;
 8: }
 9: const PlayerContext = createContext<PlayerContextType | null>(null);
10: export function PlayerProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
11:   const [isSidebarOpen, setIsSidebarOpen] = useState(false);
12:   const value = useMemo(
13:     () => ({
14:       isSidebarOpen,
15:       openSidebar: () => setIsSidebarOpen(true),
16:       closeSidebar: () => setIsSidebarOpen(false),
17:       toggleSidebar: () => setIsSidebarOpen((prev) => !prev),
18:     }),
19:     [isSidebarOpen],
20:   );
21:   return (
22:     <PlayerContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</PlayerContext.Provider>
23:   );
24: }
25: export function usePlayerContext() {
26:   const context = useContext(PlayerContext);
27:   if (!context) {
28:     throw new Error("usePlayerContext must be used within a PlayerProvider");
29:   }
30:   return context;
31: }
````

## File: src/components/global/theme/mode-toggle.tsx
````typescript
 1: "use client";
 2: import * as React from "react";
 3: import { Moon, Sun } from "lucide-react";
 4: import { useTheme } from "next-themes";
 5: import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
 6: const emptySubscribe = () => () => {};
 7: function ModeToggle(props: React.ComponentProps<typeof Button>) {
 8:   const { resolvedTheme, setTheme } = useTheme();
 9:   const mounted = React.useSyncExternalStore(
10:     emptySubscribe,
11:     () => true,
12:     () => false,
13:   );
14:   const isDark = mounted && resolvedTheme === "dark";
15:   const toggleTheme = () => {
16:     if (!mounted) return;
17:     setTheme(isDark ? "light" : "dark");
18:   };
19:   return (
20:     <Button
21:       type="button"
22:       variant="outline"
23:       size="icon"
24:       aria-label={
25:         mounted
26:           ? isDark
27:             ? "Switch to light mode"
28:             : "Switch to dark mode"
29:           : "Toggle theme"
30:       }
31:       title={isDark ? "Switch to light mode" : "Switch to dark mode"}
32:       onClick={toggleTheme}
33:       {...props}
34:     >
35:       <Sun
36:         aria-hidden="true"
37:         className="size-4 scale-100 rotate-0 transition-all dark:scale-0 dark:-rotate-90"
38:       />
39:       <Moon
40:         aria-hidden="true"
41:         className="absolute size-4 scale-0 rotate-90 transition-all dark:scale-100 dark:rotate-0"
42:       />
43:       <span className="sr-only">Toggle theme</span>
44:     </Button>
45:   );
46: }
47: export { ModeToggle };
````

````typescript
 1: import { mergeProps } from "@base-ui/react/merge-props";

 5: const badgeVariants = cva(
 6:   "group/badge inline-flex h-5 w-fit shrink-0 items-center justify-center gap-1 overflow-hidden rounded-4xl border border-transparent px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium whitespace-nowrap transition-all focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-[3px] focus-visible:ring-ring/50 has-data-[icon=inline-end]:pr-1.5 has-data-[icon=inline-start]:pl-1.5 aria-invalid:border-destructive aria-invalid:ring-destructive/20 dark:aria-invalid:ring-destructive/40 [&>svg]:pointer-events-none [&>svg]:size-3!",
 7:   {
 8:     variants: {
 9:       variant: {
10:         default: "bg-primary text-primary-foreground [a]:hover:bg-primary/80",
11:         secondary:
12:           "bg-secondary text-secondary-foreground [a]:hover:bg-secondary/80",
13:         destructive:
14:           "bg-destructive/10 text-destructive focus-visible:ring-destructive/20 dark:bg-destructive/20 dark:focus-visible:ring-destructive/40 [a]:hover:bg-destructive/20",
15:         outline:
16:           "border-border text-foreground [a]:hover:bg-muted [a]:hover:text-muted-foreground",
17:         ghost:
18:           "hover:bg-muted hover:text-muted-foreground dark:hover:bg-muted/50",
19:         link: "text-primary underline-offset-4 hover:underline",
20:       },
21:     },
22:     defaultVariants: {
23:       variant: "default",
24:     },
25:   },
26: );
27: function Badge({
28:   className,
29:   variant = "default",
30:   render,
31:   ...props
32: }: useRender.ComponentProps<"span"> & VariantProps<typeof badgeVariants>) {
33:   return useRender({
34:     defaultTagName: "span",
35:     props: mergeProps<"span">(
36:       {
37:         className: cn(badgeVariants({ variant }), className),
38:       },
39:       props,
40:     ),
41:     render,
42:     state: {
43:       slot: "badge",
44:       variant,
45:     },
46:   });
47: }
48: export { Badge, badgeVariants };
````

````typescript
 1: import { slugify } from "../slug";

15:     expect(slugify("مقدمة إلى لغة TypeScript")).toBe(
16:       "مقدمة-الى-لغة-typescript",
17:     );
18:     expect(slugify("Привет Мир")).toBe("привет-мир");
19:     expect(slugify("你好世界")).toBe("你好世界");
20:   });
21:   it("handles leading, trailing, and repeated whitespace and punctuation", () => {
22:     expect(slugify("   ---Course: Title Here!   ")).toBe("course-title-here");

24:       "multiple-spaces-and-hyphens",
25:     );
26:   });
27:   it("returns deterministic fallback when input contains only punctuation or symbols", () => {
28:     expect(slugify("???")).toBe("item");
29:     expect(slugify("!@#$%^&*()_+", "course")).toBe("course");
30:     expect(slugify("", "lesson")).toBe("lesson");
````
