## File: src/lib/validations/catalog.ts
````typescript
 1: import { z } from "zod";
 2: import { courseLevelEnum } from "./course";
 3: export const catalogSortEnum = z.enum(["newest", "title_asc", "title_desc"]);
 4: export type CatalogSort = z.infer<typeof catalogSortEnum>;
 5: export const catalogQuerySchema = z.object({
 6:   search: z.string().trim().max(100).optional(),
 7:   category: z.string().trim().max(50).optional(),
 8:   level: courseLevelEnum.optional(),
 9:   sort: catalogSortEnum.default("newest"),
10:   page: z.coerce.number().int().positive().default(1),
11:   limit: z.coerce.number().int().positive().max(50).default(12),
12: });
13: export type CatalogQueryInput = z.infer<typeof catalogQuerySchema>;
14: export const resourceItemSchema = z.object({
15:   name: z.string().trim().min(1, "Name is required").max(100),
16:   url: z
17:     .string()
18:     .trim()
19:     .url("Invalid URL format")
20:     .refine((val) => {
21:       try {
22:         const parsed = new URL(val);
23:         return parsed.protocol === "http:" || parsed.protocol === "https:";
24:       } catch {
25:         return false;
26:       }
27:     }, "Only HTTP and HTTPS protocols are allowed"),
28: });
29: export type SafeResourceItem = z.infer<typeof resourceItemSchema>;
30: export function parseSafeResources(raw: unknown): SafeResourceItem[] {
31:   if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
32:   const safeItems: SafeResourceItem[] = [];
33:   for (const item of raw) {
34:     const parsed = resourceItemSchema.safeParse(item);
35:     if (parsed.success) {
36:       safeItems.push(parsed.data);
37:     }
38:   }
39:   return safeItems;
40: }
````

 1: export type ActionSuccess<T> = {
 2:   success: true;
 3:   data: T;
 4: };
 5: export type ActionFailure = {
 6:   success: false;
 7:   error: string;
 8:   code?: string;
 9:   details?: Record<string, string[]>;
10: };
11: export type ActionResult<T = void> = ActionSuccess<T> | ActionFailure;
12: export function actionSuccess<T>(data: T): ActionSuccess<T> {
13:   return {
14:     success: true,
15:     data,
16:   };
17: }
18: export function actionFailure(
19:   error: string,
20:   code?: string,
21:   details?: Record<string, string[]>,

## File: src/lib/slug.ts
````typescript
 1: export function slugify(text: string, fallback = "item"): string {
 2:   const normalized = text
 3:     .normalize("NFKD")
 4:     .replace(/\p{M}/gu, "")
 5:     .toLowerCase()
 6:     .trim();
 7:   const slug = normalized
 8:     .replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}]+/gu, "-")
 9:     .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "");
10:   return slug.length > 0 ? slug : fallback;
11: }
````

## File: src/lib/video.ts
````typescript
 1: import { ValidationError } from "@/lib/errors";
 2: const YOUTUBE_ID_REGEX = /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{11}$/;
 3: const VIMEO_ID_REGEX = /^\d+$/;
 4: const LOOM_ID_REGEX = /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/;
 5: export function normalizeVideoUrl(rawUrl: string): string {
 6:   const trimmed = rawUrl.trim();
 7:   if (!trimmed) {
 8:     return "";
 9:   }
10:   let parsed: URL;
11:   try {
12:     parsed = new URL(trimmed);
13:   } catch {
14:     throw new ValidationError("Invalid video URL format");
15:   }
16:   if (parsed.protocol !== "http:" && parsed.protocol !== "https:") {
17:     throw new ValidationError("Video URL must use http: or https: scheme");
18:   }
19:   const hostname = parsed.hostname.toLowerCase();
20:   if (
21:     hostname === "youtube.com" ||
22:     hostname === "www.youtube.com" ||
23:     hostname === "m.youtube.com"
24:   ) {
25:     let videoId: string | null = null;
26:     const pathname = parsed.pathname;
27:     if (pathname === "/watch") {
28:       videoId = parsed.searchParams.get("v");
29:     } else if (pathname.startsWith("/shorts/")) {
30:       const parts = pathname.split("/").filter(Boolean);
31:       videoId = parts[1] ?? null;
32:     } else if (pathname.startsWith("/embed/")) {
33:       const parts = pathname.split("/").filter(Boolean);
34:       videoId = parts[1] ?? null;
35:     }
36:     if (!videoId || !YOUTUBE_ID_REGEX.test(videoId)) {
37:       throw new ValidationError("Invalid or missing YouTube video ID");
38:     }
39:     return `https://www.youtube.com/embed/${videoId}`;
40:   }
41:   if (hostname === "youtu.be") {
42:     const parts = parsed.pathname.split("/").filter(Boolean);
43:     const videoId = parts[0] ?? null;
44:     if (!videoId || !YOUTUBE_ID_REGEX.test(videoId)) {
45:       throw new ValidationError("Invalid or missing YouTube video ID");
46:     }
47:     return `https://www.youtube.com/embed/${videoId}`;
48:   }
49:   if (hostname === "vimeo.com" || hostname === "www.vimeo.com") {
50:     const parts = parsed.pathname.split("/").filter(Boolean);
51:     const videoId = parts[0] ?? null;
52:     if (!videoId || !VIMEO_ID_REGEX.test(videoId)) {
53:       throw new ValidationError("Invalid or missing Vimeo video ID");
54:     }
55:     return `https://player.vimeo.com/video/${videoId}`;
56:   }
57:   if (hostname === "player.vimeo.com") {
58:     const parts = parsed.pathname.split("/").filter(Boolean);
59:     let videoId: string | null = null;
60:     if (parts[0] === "video" && parts[1]) {
61:       videoId = parts[1];
62:     }
63:     if (!videoId || !VIMEO_ID_REGEX.test(videoId)) {
64:       throw new ValidationError("Invalid or missing Vimeo video ID");
65:     }
66:     return `https://player.vimeo.com/video/${videoId}`;
67:   }
68:   if (hostname === "loom.com" || hostname === "www.loom.com") {
69:     const parts = parsed.pathname.split("/").filter(Boolean);
70:     let videoId: string | null = null;
71:     if ((parts[0] === "share" || parts[0] === "embed") && parts[1]) {
72:       videoId = parts[1];
73:     }
74:     if (!videoId || !LOOM_ID_REGEX.test(videoId)) {
75:       throw new ValidationError("Invalid or missing Loom video ID");
76:     }
77:     return `https://www.loom.com/embed/${videoId}`;
78:   }
79:   throw new ValidationError(
80:     "Unsupported video provider. Supported providers are YouTube, Vimeo, and Loom.",
81:   );
82: }
````

  1: import { prisma } from "@/lib/db";
  2: import {
  3:   type CourseEnrollment,
  4:   EnrollmentStatus,
  5:   Prisma,
  6: } from "@prisma/client";
  7: import { NotFoundError } from "@/lib/errors";
  8: export async function findEnrollment(
  9:   userId: string,
 10:   courseId: string,
 11: ): Promise<CourseEnrollment | null> {
 12:   return prisma.courseEnrollment.findUnique({

 16:   });

 18: export async function createEnrollment(
 19:   userId: string,
 20:   courseId: string,
 21: ): Promise<CourseEnrollment> {
 22:   try {
 23:     return await prisma.courseEnrollment.create({
 24:       data: {
 25:         userId,
 26:         courseId,
 27:         status: EnrollmentStatus.ACTIVE,
 28:         progressPercentage: 0,
 29:       },

 34:         const existing = await findEnrollment(userId, courseId);
 35:         if (existing) {

 41:       }
 42:     }

 44:   }
 45: }

 55: ): Promise<CourseEnrollment> {

 60:   });

21:   bodyHtml?: string | null;
22:   videoUrl?: string | null;
23:   resources?: Array<{ name: string; url: string }> | null;
24: };

65:       : data.resources === null
66:         ? Prisma.JsonNull
67:         : undefined;

 50: export async function createLessonAtomic(
 51:   data: {
 52:     moduleId: string;
 53:     courseId: string;
 54:     title: string;
 55:     baseSlug: string;
 56:     durationMinutes?: number | null;
 57:     isFreePreview?: boolean;
 58:   },
 59:   maxAttempts = 5,
 60: ): Promise<Lesson> {
 61:   for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++) {
 62:     const candidateSlug =
 63:       attempt === 1 ? data.baseSlug : `${data.baseSlug}-${attempt}`;
 64:     try {
 65:       return await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
 66:         const course = await lockCourseForUpdate(tx, data.courseId);
 67:         if (course.status !== CourseStatus.DRAFT) {
 68:           throw new ValidationError(
 69:             "Cannot modify curriculum of a published or archived course",
 70:           );
 71:         }
 72:         const maxLesson = await tx.lesson.findFirst({
 73:           where: { moduleId: data.moduleId },
 74:           orderBy: { orderIndex: "desc" },
 75:           select: { orderIndex: true },
 76:         });
 77:         const newIndex = maxLesson !== null ? maxLesson.orderIndex + 1 : 0;
 78:         return await tx.lesson.create({
 79:           data: {
 80:             moduleId: data.moduleId,
 81:             title: data.title,
 82:             slug: candidateSlug,
 83:             orderIndex: newIndex,
 84:             durationMinutes: data.durationMinutes,
 85:             isFreePreview: data.isFreePreview ?? false,
 86:           },
 87:         });
 88:       });
 89:     } catch (error) {
 90:       if (
 91:         error instanceof Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError &&
 92:         error.code === "P2002"
 93:       ) {
 94:         if (attempt === maxAttempts) {
 95:           throw new ConflictError(
 96:             "Failed to assign a unique order index or slug for lesson after concurrent retries.",
 97:           );
 98:         }
 99:         continue;
100:       }
101:       throw error;
102:     }
103:   }
104:   throw new ConflictError(
105:     "Failed to create lesson due to concurrency collision",
106:   );
107: }

115:   },
116: ): Promise<Lesson> {
117:   return prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
118:     const course = await lockCourseForUpdate(tx, courseId);
119:     if (course.status !== CourseStatus.DRAFT) {
120:       throw new ValidationError(

130: export async function deleteLessonAtomic(
131:   lessonId: string,
132:   courseId: string,
133: ): Promise<Lesson> {
134:   return prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
135:     const course = await lockCourseForUpdate(tx, courseId);
136:     if (course.status !== CourseStatus.DRAFT) {
137:       throw new ValidationError(
138:         "Cannot modify curriculum of a published or archived course",
139:       );
140:     }
141:     const lessonToDelete = await tx.lesson.findUnique({
142:       where: { id: lessonId },
143:       select: { id: true, moduleId: true, orderIndex: true },
144:     });
145:     if (!lessonToDelete) {
146:       throw new NotFoundError("Lesson not found");
147:     }
148:     const deleted = await tx.lesson.delete({
149:       where: { id: lessonId },
150:     });
151:     const siblings = await tx.lesson.findMany({
152:       where: {
153:         moduleId: lessonToDelete.moduleId,
154:         orderIndex: { gt: lessonToDelete.orderIndex },
155:       },
156:       orderBy: { orderIndex: "asc" },
157:       select: { id: true, orderIndex: true },
158:     });
159:     for (const sibling of siblings) {
160:       await tx.lesson.update({
161:         where: { id: sibling.id },
162:         data: { orderIndex: sibling.orderIndex - 1 },
163:       });
164:     }
165:     return deleted;
166:   });
167: }
168: export async function reorderLessonsAtomic(
169:   moduleId: string,
170:   courseId: string,
171:   orderedIds: string[],
172: ): Promise<Lesson[]> {
173:   return prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
174:     const course = await lockCourseForUpdate(tx, courseId);
175:     if (course.status !== CourseStatus.DRAFT) {
176:       throw new ValidationError(
177:         "Cannot modify curriculum of a published or archived course",
178:       );
179:     }
180:     const existingLessons = await tx.lesson.findMany({
181:       where: { moduleId },
182:       select: { id: true },
183:     });
184:     if (orderedIds.length !== existingLessons.length) {
185:       throw new ValidationError(
186:         "Invalid reorder permutation: IDs count must match existing lessons count",
187:       );
188:     }
189:     const uniqueOrderedIds = new Set(orderedIds);
190:     if (uniqueOrderedIds.size !== orderedIds.length) {
191:       throw new ValidationError(
192:         "Invalid reorder permutation: duplicate IDs are not allowed",
193:       );
194:     }
195:     const existingIdSet = new Set(existingLessons.map((l) => l.id));
196:     const allExist = orderedIds.every((id) => existingIdSet.has(id));
197:     if (!allExist) {
198:       throw new ValidationError(
199:         "Invalid reorder permutation: all IDs must match existing lesson IDs",
200:       );
201:     }
202:     for (let i = 0; i < orderedIds.length; i++) {
203:       await tx.lesson.update({
204:         where: { id: orderedIds[i] },
205:         data: { orderIndex: -1 - i },
206:       });
207:     }
208:     const updatedLessons: Lesson[] = [];
209:     for (let i = 0; i < orderedIds.length; i++) {
210:       const updated = await tx.lesson.update({
211:         where: { id: orderedIds[i] },
212:         data: { orderIndex: i },
213:       });
214:       updatedLessons.push(updated);
215:     }
216:     return updatedLessons;
217:   });
218: }

 27: async function assertCourseOwnership(

 59: export async function getCourseById(
 60:   userId: string | null,
 61:   courseId: string,
 62:   options?: courseRepository.CourseQueryOptions,
 63: ) {
 64:   const course = await courseRepository.findCourseById(courseId, options);
 65:   if (!course) {
 66:     throw new NotFoundError("Course not found");
 67:   }
 68:   if (course.status === CourseStatus.PUBLISHED) {
 69:     return course;
 70:   }
 71:   if (!userId) {
 72:     throw new NotFoundError("Course not found");
 73:   }
 74:   try {
 75:     await assertCourseOwnership(userId, course);
 76:   } catch (error) {
 77:     if (error instanceof AuthorizationError) {
 78:       throw new NotFoundError("Course not found");
 79:     }
 80:     throw error;
 81:   }
 82:   return course;
 83: }

178: export async function publishCourse(
179:   userId: string,
180:   courseId: string,
181: ): Promise<Course> {
182:   const course = await courseRepository.findCourseById(courseId);
183:   if (!course) {
184:     throw new NotFoundError("Course not found");
185:   }
186:   await assertCourseOwnership(userId, course);
187:   return courseRepository.executeCourseStatusTransition(
188:     courseId,
189:     [CourseStatus.DRAFT],
190:     CourseStatus.PUBLISHED,
191:     async (tx) => {
192:       const { moduleCount, lessonCount } =
193:         await courseRepository.countCurriculumItems(courseId, tx);
194:       if (moduleCount < 1) {
195:         throw new ValidationError(
196:           "Cannot publish a course without at least one module",
197:         );
198:       }
199:       if (lessonCount < 1) {
200:         throw new ValidationError(
201:           "Cannot publish a course without at least one lesson",
202:         );
203:       }
204:     },
205:   );
206: }

307: export async function getCatalogCourses(
308:   options: CatalogQueryInput,
309:   userId?: string | null,
310: ): Promise<CatalogCoursesResponse> {
311:   const parsed = catalogQuerySchema.parse(options);
312:   const result = await courseRepository.findPublishedCoursesPaginated(parsed);
313:   const courseIds = result.courses.map((c) => c.id);
314:   const enrollmentMap = new Map<string, CourseEnrollment>();
315:   if (userId && courseIds.length > 0) {
316:     const enrollments =
317:       await enrollmentRepository.findEnrollmentsForUserAndCourses(
318:         userId,
319:         courseIds,
320:       );
321:     for (const e of enrollments) {
322:       if (
323:         e.status === EnrollmentStatus.ACTIVE ||
324:         e.status === EnrollmentStatus.COMPLETED
325:       ) {
326:         enrollmentMap.set(e.courseId, e);
327:       }
328:     }
329:   }
330:   const items: CatalogCourseItem[] = result.courses.map((c) => {
331:     const enrollment = enrollmentMap.get(c.id);
332:     return {
333:       id: c.id,
334:       title: c.title,
335:       slug: c.slug,
336:       description: c.description,
337:       thumbnailUrl: c.thumbnailUrl,
338:       level: c.level,
339:       category: c.category,
340:       instructor: c.instructor,
341:       modulesCount: c._count.modules,
342:       totalLessons: c.totalLessons,
343:       enrollmentCount: c._count.enrollments,
344:       isEnrolled: Boolean(enrollment),
345:       progressPercentage: enrollment ? enrollment.progressPercentage : null,
346:     };
347:   });
348:   return {
349:     courses: items,
350:     totalCount: result.totalCount,
351:     page: result.page,
352:     limit: result.limit,
353:     totalPages: result.totalPages,
354:   };
355: }

363:   const course = await courseRepository.findCourseBySlug(slug, {
364:     includeCurriculum: true,
365:     includeInstructor: true,
366:   });
367:   if (!course) {
368:     throw new NotFoundError("Course not found");
369:   }
370:   if (course.status !== CourseStatus.PUBLISHED) {
371:     if (!userId) {
372:       throw new NotFoundError("Course not found");
373:     }
374:     const isOwner = course.instructorId === userId;
375:     const isAdmin = await hasRole(userId, "admin");
376:     if (!isOwner && !isAdmin) {
377:       throw new NotFoundError("Course not found");
378:     }
379:   }
380:   let enrollment: CourseEnrollment | null = null;
381:   let completedLessonIds: string[] = [];
382:   let isEnrolled = false;
383:   if (userId) {
384:     enrollment = await enrollmentRepository.findEnrollment(userId, course.id);
385:     if (
386:       enrollment &&
387:       (enrollment.status === EnrollmentStatus.ACTIVE ||
388:         enrollment.status === EnrollmentStatus.COMPLETED)
389:     ) {
390:       if (
391:         course.status === CourseStatus.PUBLISHED ||
392:         course.instructorId === userId ||
393:         (await hasRole(userId, "admin"))
394:       ) {
395:         isEnrolled = true;
396:       }
397:     }
398:     if (
399:       isEnrolled ||
400:       course.instructorId === userId ||
401:       (await hasRole(userId, "admin"))
402:     ) {
403:       const progressRecords =
404:         await lessonProgressRepository.findProgressByUserAndCourse(
405:           userId,
406:           course.id,
407:         );
408:       completedLessonIds = progressRecords
409:         .filter((p) => p.isCompleted)
410:         .map((p) => p.lessonId);
411:     }
412:   }
413:   const completedSet = new Set(completedLessonIds);
414:   const rawModules = course.modules;
415:   const sortedModules = [...rawModules].sort(
416:     (a, b) => a.orderIndex - b.orderIndex,
417:   );
418:   let totalLessons = 0;
419:   const modules: CourseOverviewModule[] = sortedModules.map((mod) => {
420:     const sortedLessons = [...mod.lessons].sort(
421:       (a, b) => a.orderIndex - b.orderIndex,
422:     );
423:     totalLessons += sortedLessons.length;
424:     return {
425:       id: mod.id,
426:       title: mod.title,
427:       description: mod.description,
428:       orderIndex: mod.orderIndex,
429:       lessons: sortedLessons.map((l) => ({
430:         id: l.id,
431:         title: l.title,
432:         slug: l.slug,
433:         orderIndex: l.orderIndex,
434:         durationMinutes: l.durationMinutes,
435:         isFreePreview: l.isFreePreview,
436:         isCompleted: completedSet.has(l.id),
437:       })),
438:     };
439:   });
440:   return {
441:     course,
442:     modules,
443:     enrollment,
444:     isEnrolled,
445:     completedLessonIds,
446:     totalLessons,
447:   };
448: }

 16: export type LessonContentDetail = {
 17:   lessonId: string;
 18:   lessonTitle: string;
 19:   courseId: string;
 20:   bodyMarkdown: string | null;
 21:   bodyHtml: string | null;

 23:   resources: Array<{ name: string; url: string }>;
 24:   isFreePreview: boolean;
 25: };
 26: export async function getLessonContent(
 27:   userId: string | null,
 28:   lessonId: string,
 29: ): Promise<LessonContentDetail> {
 30:   const hierarchy = await lessonContentRepository.findLessonHierarchy(lessonId);
 31:   if (!hierarchy) {
 32:     throw new NotFoundError("Lesson not found");
 33:   }
 34:   const course = hierarchy.module.course;
 35:   const isPublicPreview =
 36:     hierarchy.isFreePreview && course.status === CourseStatus.PUBLISHED;
 37:   if (!isPublicPreview) {
 38:     if (!userId) {
 39:       throw new AuthenticationError(
 40:         "Authentication required to view this lesson content",
 41:       );
 42:     }
 43:     const isOwner = course.instructorId === userId;
 44:     const isAdmin = await authorizationService.hasRole(userId, "admin");
 45:     if (!isOwner && !isAdmin) {
 46:       if (course.status === CourseStatus.PUBLISHED) {
 47:         const isEnrolled = await enrollmentService.isUserEnrolled(
 48:           userId,
 49:           course.id,
 50:         );
 51:         if (!isEnrolled) {
 52:           throw new AuthorizationError(
 53:             "You must enroll in this course to access this lesson",
 54:           );
 55:         }
 56:       } else {
 57:         throw new AuthorizationError(
 58:           "You do not have permission to view this lesson content",
 59:         );
 60:       }
 61:     }
 62:   }
 63:   const content =
 64:     await lessonContentRepository.findLessonContentByLessonId(lessonId);
 65:   const rawResources = content?.resources;
 66:   const parsedResources: Array<{ name: string; url: string }> = Array.isArray(
 67:     rawResources,
 68:   )
 69:     ? (rawResources as Array<{ name: string; url: string }>)
 70:     : [];
 71:   return {
 72:     lessonId: hierarchy.id,
 73:     lessonTitle: hierarchy.title,
 74:     courseId: course.id,
 75:     bodyMarkdown: content?.bodyMarkdown ?? null,
 76:     bodyHtml: content?.bodyHtml ?? null,
 77:     videoUrl: content?.videoUrl ?? null,
 78:     resources: parsedResources,
 79:     isFreePreview: hierarchy.isFreePreview,
 80:   };
 81: }
 82: export async function updateLessonContent(
 83:   userId: string,
 84:   input: UpdateLessonContentInput,
 85: ): Promise<LessonContent> {
 86:   await authorizationService.requireAnyRole(userId, ["instructor", "admin"]);
 87:   const hierarchy = await lessonContentRepository.findLessonHierarchy(
 88:     input.lessonId,
 89:   );
 90:   if (!hierarchy) {
 91:     throw new NotFoundError("Lesson not found");
 92:   }
 93:   const course = hierarchy.module.course;
 94:   if (course.status === CourseStatus.ARCHIVED) {
 95:     throw new ValidationError(
 96:       "Cannot modify lesson content of an archived course",
 97:     );
 98:   }
 99:   const isOwner = course.instructorId === userId;
100:   const isAdmin = await authorizationService.hasRole(userId, "admin");
101:   if (!isOwner && !isAdmin) {
102:     throw new AuthorizationError(
103:       "You are not authorized to modify this lesson content",
104:     );
105:   }
106:   let normalizedVideoUrl: string | null | undefined;
107:   if (input.videoUrl !== undefined) {
108:     normalizedVideoUrl = input.videoUrl
109:       ? normalizeVideoUrl(input.videoUrl)
110:       : null;
111:   }
112:   let sanitizedHtml: string | null | undefined;
113:   if (input.bodyMarkdown !== undefined) {
114:     sanitizedHtml = input.bodyMarkdown
115:       ? await markdownToSanitizedHtml(input.bodyMarkdown)
116:       : null;
117:   }
118:   return lessonContentRepository.upsertLessonContent(input.lessonId, {
119:     bodyMarkdown: input.bodyMarkdown,
120:     bodyHtml: sanitizedHtml,
121:     videoUrl: normalizedVideoUrl,
122:     resources: input.resources,
123:   });
124: }
125: export interface LessonNavigation {
126:   previousLesson: { id: string; title: string } | null;
127:   nextLesson: { id: string; title: string } | null;
128:   totalLessons: number;
129:   currentIndex: number;
130: }
131: export async function getLessonNavigation(
132:   courseId: string,
133:   currentLessonId: string,
134: ): Promise<LessonNavigation> {
135:   const course = await courseRepository.findCourseById(courseId, {
136:     includeCurriculum: true,
137:   });
138:   if (!course) {
139:     throw new NotFoundError("Course not found");
140:   }
141:   type NavigationLesson = { id: string; title: string; orderIndex: number };
142:   type NavigationModule = { orderIndex: number; lessons?: NavigationLesson[] };
143:   const rawModules = (course as { modules?: NavigationModule[] }).modules ?? [];
144:   const sortedModules = [...rawModules].sort(
145:     (a, b) => a.orderIndex - b.orderIndex,
146:   );
147:   const flattenedLessons: Array<{ id: string; title: string }> = [];
148:   for (const mod of sortedModules) {
149:     const sortedLessons = [...(mod.lessons ?? [])].sort(
150:       (a, b) => a.orderIndex - b.orderIndex,
151:     );
152:     for (const lesson of sortedLessons) {
153:       flattenedLessons.push({ id: lesson.id, title: lesson.title });
154:     }
155:   }
156:   const currentIndex = flattenedLessons.findIndex(
157:     (l) => l.id === currentLessonId,
158:   );
159:   if (currentIndex === -1) {
160:     throw new NotFoundError("Lesson does not belong to this course");
161:   }
162:   return {
163:     previousLesson:
164:       currentIndex > 0 ? flattenedLessons[currentIndex - 1] : null,
165:     nextLesson:
166:       currentIndex < flattenedLessons.length - 1
167:         ? flattenedLessons[currentIndex + 1]
168:         : null,
169:     totalLessons: flattenedLessons.length,
170:     currentIndex: currentIndex + 1,
171:   };
172: }
173: export async function getCourseLessonForPlayer(params: {
174:   courseSlug: string;
175:   lessonId: string;
176:   userId?: string | null;
177: }): Promise<{
178:   course: Course;
179:   lesson: LessonContentDetail;
180:   navigation: LessonNavigation;
181: }> {
182:   const { courseSlug, lessonId, userId } = params;
183:   const course = await courseRepository.findCourseBySlug(courseSlug);
184:   if (!course) {
185:     throw new NotFoundError("Course not found");
186:   }
187:   const hierarchy = await lessonContentRepository.findLessonHierarchy(lessonId);
188:   if (!hierarchy) {
189:     throw new NotFoundError("Lesson not found");
190:   }
191:   if (hierarchy.module.course.id !== course.id) {
192:     throw new NotFoundError("Lesson not found in this course");
193:   }
194:   const isPublicPreview =
195:     hierarchy.isFreePreview && course.status === CourseStatus.PUBLISHED;
196:   if (!isPublicPreview) {
197:     if (!userId) {
198:       throw new AuthenticationError(
199:         "Authentication required to view this lesson content",
200:       );
201:     }
202:     const isOwner = course.instructorId === userId;
203:     const isAdmin = await authorizationService.hasRole(userId, "admin");
204:     if (!isOwner && !isAdmin) {
205:       if (course.status !== CourseStatus.PUBLISHED) {
206:         throw new NotFoundError("Course not found");
207:       }
208:       const isEnrolled = await enrollmentService.isUserEnrolled(
209:         userId,
210:         course.id,
211:       );
212:       if (!isEnrolled) {
213:         throw new AuthorizationError(
214:           "You must enroll in this course to access this lesson",
215:         );
216:       }
217:     }
218:   }
219:   const content =
220:     await lessonContentRepository.findLessonContentByLessonId(lessonId);
221:   const safeResources = parseSafeResources(content?.resources);
222:   const navigation = await getLessonNavigation(course.id, lessonId);
223:   return {
224:     course,
225:     lesson: {
226:       lessonId: hierarchy.id,
227:       lessonTitle: hierarchy.title,
228:       courseId: course.id,
229:       bodyMarkdown: content?.bodyMarkdown ?? null,
230:       bodyHtml: content?.bodyHtml ?? null,
231:       videoUrl: content?.videoUrl ?? null,
232:       resources: safeResources,
233:       isFreePreview: hierarchy.isFreePreview,
234:     },
235:     navigation,
236:   };
237: }

 24:   id: string;

 26:   moduleId: string;
 27:   moduleTitle: string;
 28: };
 29: export async function toggleLessonCompletion(
 30:   userId: string,
 31:   lessonId: string,
 32:   completed: boolean,
 33: ): Promise<ToggleResult> {
 34:   const hierarchy = await lessonContentRepository.findLessonHierarchy(lessonId);
 35:   if (!hierarchy) {
 36:     throw new NotFoundError("Lesson not found");
 37:   }
 38:   const courseId = hierarchy.module.courseId;
 39:   const enrollment = await enrollmentRepository.findEnrollment(
 40:     userId,
 41:     courseId,
 42:   );
 43:   if (!enrollment || enrollment.status === EnrollmentStatus.ARCHIVED) {
 44:     throw new AuthorizationError(
 45:       "You must enroll in this course to track progress",
 46:     );
 47:   }
 48:   return prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
 49:     const progress = await lessonProgressRepository.upsertLessonProgress(
 50:       userId,
 51:       lessonId,
 52:       completed,
 53:       tx,
 54:     );
 55:     const completedCount = await lessonProgressRepository.countCompletedLessons(
 56:       userId,
 57:       courseId,
 58:       tx,
 59:     );
 60:     const totalCount = await lessonProgressRepository.countTotalLessons(
 61:       courseId,
 62:       tx,
 63:     );
 64:     const percentage =
 65:       totalCount === 0 ? 0 : Math.round((completedCount / totalCount) * 100);
 66:     const isFullyComplete = percentage === 100;
 67:     const updatedEnrollment = await enrollmentRepository.updateEnrollment(
 68:       enrollment.id,
 69:       {
 70:         progressPercentage: percentage,
 71:         completedAt: isFullyComplete ? new Date() : null,
 72:         status: isFullyComplete
 73:           ? EnrollmentStatus.COMPLETED
 74:           : EnrollmentStatus.ACTIVE,
 75:         lastAccessedAt: new Date(),
 76:       },
 77:       tx,
 78:     );
 79:     return { progress, enrollment: updatedEnrollment, percentage };
 80:   });
 81: }
 82: export async function getCourseProgress(
 83:   userId: string,
 84:   courseId: string,
 85: ): Promise<CourseProgressDetail> {
 86:   const enrollment = await enrollmentRepository.findEnrollment(
 87:     userId,
 88:     courseId,
 89:   );
 90:   if (!enrollment) {
 91:     throw new NotFoundError("Enrollment not found");
 92:   }
 93:   const progressRecords =
 94:     await lessonProgressRepository.findProgressByUserAndCourse(
 95:       userId,
 96:       courseId,
 97:     );
 98:   const completedLessonIds = progressRecords
 99:     .filter((p) => p.isCompleted)
100:     .map((p) => p.lessonId);
101:   const totalLessons =
102:     await lessonProgressRepository.countTotalLessons(courseId);
103:   const nextLesson = await getNextLesson(userId, courseId);
104:   return {
105:     enrollment,
106:     completedLessonIds,
107:     totalLessons,
108:     nextLesson,
109:   };
110: }
111: export async function getNextLesson(
112:   userId: string,
113:   courseId: string,
114: ): Promise<NextLessonResult | null> {
115:   const course = await courseRepository.findCourseById(courseId, {
116:     includeCurriculum: true,
117:   });
118:   if (!course) {
119:     throw new NotFoundError("Course not found");
120:   }
121:   const courseWithModules = course as typeof course & {
122:     modules: Array<{
123:       id: string;
124:       title: string;
125:       orderIndex: number;
126:       lessons: Array<{
127:         id: string;
128:         title: string;
129:         orderIndex: number;
130:       }>;
131:     }>;
132:   };
133:   if (!courseWithModules.modules || courseWithModules.modules.length === 0) {
134:     return null;
135:   }
136:   const progressRecords =
137:     await lessonProgressRepository.findProgressByUserAndCourse(
138:       userId,
139:       courseId,
140:     );
141:   const completedSet = new Set(
142:     progressRecords.filter((p) => p.isCompleted).map((p) => p.lessonId),
143:   );
144:   for (const mod of courseWithModules.modules) {
145:     for (const lesson of mod.lessons) {
146:       if (!completedSet.has(lesson.id)) {
147:         return {
148:           id: lesson.id,
149:           title: lesson.title,
150:           moduleId: mod.id,
151:           moduleTitle: mod.title,
152:         };
153:       }
154:     }
155:   }
156:   return null;
157: }
````

## File: docs/audits/quality-audit.md
````markdown
 1: # Pre-Flight Quality Audit Checklist
 2: 
 3: Run this systematic audit before declaring any task complete or opening a Pull Request.
 4: 
 5: ---
 6: 
 7: ## 1. Architectural Integrity
 8: 
 9: - [ ] **5-Layer Boundary Respected:** Did any database queries leak into UI components or Server Actions?
10: - [ ] **Downward Dependency Flow:** Do repositories remain free of service imports?
11: - [ ] **Thin Server Actions:** Do Actions restrict themselves to Zod validation, auth checks, and calling domain services?
12: - [ ] **Action Result Uniformity:** Does every Server Action return a typed `ActionResult<T>`?
13: 
14: ---
15: 
16: ## 2. Type Safety & Suppressions
17: 
18: - [ ] **No Unjustified `any`:** Are all domain models, props, and input shapes explicitly typed?
19: - [ ] **Zero Suppressions as Shortcuts:** Are there any unneeded `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `biome-ignore`, or `eslint-disable` comments?
20: - [ ] **Typecheck Passes:** Does `pnpm typecheck` exit with code `0`?
21: 
22: ---
23: 
24: ## 3. Next.js 16 App Router
25: 
26: - [ ] **Async Segment Props Awaited:** Are `params` and `searchParams` properly awaited in pages and metadata?
27: - [ ] **RSC by Default:** Are `"use client"` directives restricted strictly to interactive leaf components?
28: - [ ] **Cache Invalidation:** Is `revalidatePath` called inside Server Actions after data mutations?
29: - [ ] **Boundary Coverage:** Are `loading.tsx` and `error.tsx` present for dynamic routes?
30: 
31: ---
32: 
33: ## 4. UI/UX & Anti-Slop Discipline
34: 
35: - [ ] **No Generic AI Tells:** Are cards-inside-cards, generic purple-blue gradients, and arbitrary px classes eliminated?
36: - [ ] **Semantic Tokens Used:** Are colors, borders, and backgrounds mapped to `globals.css` semantic tokens?
37: - [ ] **Dark Mode Verified:** Does the component render with clear contrast under `.dark`?
38: - [ ] **Tactile Press Feedback:** Do interactive buttons include `active:scale-[0.96]`?
39: - [ ] **Hit Areas $\ge 40\times 40\text{px}$:** Are all clickable icons and buttons adequately sized?
40: - [ ] **Typography Flow:** Do headings use `text-wrap: balance` and body text use `text-wrap: pretty`?
41: 
42: ---
43: 
44: ## 5. Security & Authorization
45: 
46: - [ ] **Auth Guards Present:** Are private routes and actions protected with `requireAuth()` or `requireRole()`?
47: - [ ] **Ownership Checked:** Are instructor mutations verified against `assertCourseOwnership()`?
48: - [ ] **404 vs 403 Policy:** Do lookups for unauthorized draft or archived courses strictly return `NotFoundError (404)`?
49: - [ ] **Content Sanitized:** Is all user markdown and iframe embedding sanitized via the approved pipeline?
50: 
51: ---
52: 
53: ## 6. Testing & Honest Verification
54: 
55: - [ ] **Relevant Tests Pass:** Did you execute the change-aware test command (`pnpm test -- <path>`)?
56: - [ ] **Domain Rules Covered:** Are critical business branches and edge cases tested?
57: - [ ] **Honest Reporting:** Are any skipped or unverified checks explicitly disclosed in the final report?
58: 
59: ---
60: 
61: ## 7. Documentation & Decisions
62: 
63: - [ ] **Docs Synchronized:** If domain invariants or architecture changed, were `docs/` files updated?
64: - [ ] **ADR Recorded:** If a major architectural decision or dependency was introduced, was an ADR added to `docs/decisions/`?
65: - [ ] **Clean Diff:** Did you review `git status` and `git diff` to ensure no unrelated files or debug code were committed?
````

## File: docs/decisions/001-use-layered-architecture.md
````markdown
 1: # ADR-001: Use Layered Architecture
 2: 
 3: ## Status
 4: 
 5: Accepted
 6: 
 7: ## Date
 8: 
 9: 2026-07-20
10: 
11: ## Context
12: 
13: The project needs a clear separation of concerns to maintain code quality as it grows. Business logic must be isolated from the presentation layer.
14: 
15: ## Decision
16: 
17: We will follow a 5-layer architecture with strict downward dependencies:
18: 
19: ```
20: UI (Server & Client Components)
21:   ↓
22: Actions / Routes (@/actions/*, @/app/api/*)
23:   ↓
24: Domain Services (@/services/*)
25:   ↓
26: Repositories (@/repositories/*)
27:   ↓
28: Database (Prisma + Neon PostgreSQL)
29: ```
30: 
31: ## Consequences
32: 
33: ### Positive
34: 
35: - Clear separation of concerns.
36: - Business logic is testable in isolation.
37: - Database access is centralized in repositories.
38: - UI remains a thin presentation layer.
39: 
40: ### Negative
41: 
42: - More files and folders for simple features.
43: - Requires discipline to maintain the layers.
44: - Adds indirection for simple data fetching.
45: 
46: ## Alternatives Considered
47: 
48: - **Direct Prisma in components**: Rejected. Violates separation of concerns.
49: - **Service-only architecture**: Rejected. Mixes data access with business logic.
50: - **Feature-based architecture**: Future consideration. Can coexist with layers.
````

## File: docs/decisions/002-use-neon-with-prisma.md
````markdown
 1: # ADR-002: Use Neon PostgreSQL with Prisma
 2: 
 3: ## Status
 4: 
 5: Accepted
 6: 
 7: ## Date
 8: 
 9: 2026-07-20
10: 
11: ## Context
12: 
13: The project needs a reliable, scalable database that works well with TypeScript and serverless deployment.
14: 
15: ## Decision
16: 
17: We will use Neon PostgreSQL as the database provider with Prisma as the ORM (`@prisma/adapter-neon` via `@neondatabase/serverless`).
18: 
19: ## Consequences
20: 
21: ### Positive
22: 
23: - Serverless PostgreSQL scales automatically.
24: - Prisma provides type-safe database access.
25: - Neon adapter works with connection pooling.
26: - WebSocket support for serverless environments.
27: 
28: ### Negative
29: 
30: - Neon-specific configuration required.
31: - Connection pooling adds complexity.
32: - WebSocket setup in `lib/db.ts` adds boilerplate.
33: 
34: ## Alternatives Considered
35: 
36: - **Supabase**: Rejected. Prisma integration is less mature.
37: - **PlanetScale**: Rejected. MySQL, not PostgreSQL.
38: - **Railway**: Rejected. Not serverless-native.
````

## File: docs/decisions/003-use-shadcn-ui.md
````markdown
 1: # ADR-003: Use shadcn/ui for Component Library
 2: 
 3: ## Status
 4: 
 5: Accepted
 6: 
 7: ## Date
 8: 
 9: 2026-07-20
10: 
11: ## Context
12: 
13: The project needs a reusable component library that is accessible, customizable, and works with Tailwind CSS.
14: 
15: ## Decision
16: 
17: We will use shadcn/ui with the `base-nova` style, Lucide React icons, and semantic CSS variables in `app/globals.css`.
18: 
19: ## Consequences
20: 
21: ### Positive
22: 
23: - Components are accessible by default.
24: - Full control over component code in `src/components/ui`.
25: - No vendor lock-in.
26: - Works with Tailwind CSS v4.
27: 
28: ### Negative
29: 
30: - Components must be manually maintained/updated.
31: - Requires understanding of component internals.
32: 
33: ## Alternatives Considered
34: 
35: - **Radix UI raw**: Rejected. shadcn/ui wraps Radix/Base UI with better design defaults.
36: - **Headless UI**: Rejected. Less opinionated, more work.
37: - **Mantine**: Rejected. Too heavy, less customizable.
````

## File: docs/decisions/004-lms-domain-model.md
````markdown
 1: # ADR-004: Use Dedicated Curriculum, Enrollment, and Isolated Progress Models
 2: 
 3: ## Status
 4: 
 5: Accepted
 6: 
 7: ## Date
 8: 
 9: 2026-09-12
10: 
11: ## Context
12: 
13: A production-grade Learning Management System (LMS) must handle multi-tenant educational workflows across multiple user roles: instructors authoring curriculum, administrators supervising platforms, and students progressing through structured lessons. The data architecture must support:
14: 
15: - Hierarchical course outlines (modules and lessons) with deterministic ordering.
16: - Heavy instructional content (markdown, compiled HTML, video embeds, downloadable resources).
17: - Many-to-many enrollment tracking with aggregate completion metrics.
18: - Fine-grained per-student lesson progress tracking without cross-user leakage.
19: - Concurrency control preventing unique constraint collisions during reordering and publishing.
20: 
21: ## Problem
22: 
23: Naive LMS architectures suffer from several architectural flaws:
24: 
25: 1. **Global Progress Flags**: Storing `isCompleted` directly on the `Lesson` entity prevents multi-student progress tracking and leaks completion state across users.
26: 2. **Bloated Syllabus Queries**: Inlining rich markdown bodies, sanitized HTML, and resource attachments directly in the `Lesson` table degrades catalog and curriculum navigation query performance.
27: 3. **Ordering Drift & Collisions**: Relying on unconstrained `orderIndex` fields causes duplicate positions, gaps, and race conditions during concurrent curriculum editing.
28: 4. **IDOR Vulnerabilities**: Lacking strict parent-child verification permits students to modify other students' progress or access unpublished lesson content.
29: 
30: ## Decision
31: 
32: We adopt a dedicated 4-tier domain model implemented via Prisma ORM on Neon PostgreSQL:
33: 
34: ```
35: Course (Metadata, Lifecycle Status, Level, Instructor Relation)
36:   └── Module (Section Header, Sequential orderIndex) [@@unique([courseId, orderIndex])]
37:         └── Lesson (Lightweight Navigation, Slug, Preview Flag) [@@unique([moduleId, orderIndex])]
38:               └── LessonContent (1-to-1 Isolated Heavy Payload: Markdown, HTML, Video, Resources)
39: 
40: User
41:   ├── CourseEnrollment (Many-to-Many Join: Status, Aggregate Progress %, Timestamps)
42:   └── LessonProgress (Granular Join: [userId, lessonId], isCompleted, completedAt)
43: ```
44: 
45: Key Architectural Invariants:
46: 
47: 1. **Isolated Heavy Payloads**: `LessonContent` is stored in a dedicated 1-to-1 table with cascade deletion, keeping the primary `Lesson` entity lightweight for fast curriculum tree fetching.
48: 2. **Composite Uniqueness for Curriculum Order**: `[courseId, orderIndex]` and `[moduleId, orderIndex]` enforce sequential integrity at the database engine level.
49: 3. **Two-Phase Reordering & Row Locking**: Curriculum reordering employs two-phase updates with negative offsets under an exclusive parent row lock (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`), preventing transient unique key violations (`P2002`).
50: 4. **Strict Progress Isolation**: Student progress exists solely in the `LessonProgress` join table scoped strictly to `(userId, lessonId)` with composite uniqueness `@@unique([userId, lessonId])`. It is NEVER stored on the curriculum entity.
51: 5. **Multi-Tier Authorization (IDOR Defense)**: Every mutation asserts caller ownership (`instructorId === session.userId` or `admin`). Player endpoints strictly verify cross-course boundaries (`hierarchy.module.course.id === course.id`).
52: 
53: ## Alternatives Considered
54: 
55: - **Single Monolithic Lesson Table**: Combining metadata and body content into a single table.
56:   _Rejected_: Degrades query performance for syllabus views and player sidebar navigation where lesson body is unnecessary.
57: - **Embedded Document Store (JSONB for Modules/Lessons)**: Storing the entire curriculum outline as a JSONB array on the `Course` model.
58:   _Rejected_: Eliminates relational foreign keys, complicates incremental progress tracking, prevents atomic transactions on individual lessons, and hinders SQL indexing.
59: - **Client-Driven Reorder Swaps**: Swapping adjacent indices on client requests.
60:   _Rejected_: Susceptible to race conditions, out-of-order networks, and gaps when multiple items are reordered.
61: 
62: ## Reason
63: 
64: This model provides the optimal balance of relational integrity, high-throughput query performance, and ironclad multi-tenant security:
65: 
66: - Syllabus and sidebar queries fetch only lightweight metadata (`id`, `title`, `orderIndex`, `isFreePreview`).
67: - Student progress is completely partitioned, preventing data leaks.
68: - Database constraints guarantee collision-free ordering.
69: 
70: ## Consequences
71: 
72: ### Positive
73: 
74: - Zero risk of cross-student progress leakage.
75: - High-performance course catalog and player navigation.
76: - Deterministic, collision-safe curriculum reordering.
77: - Clear separation between public preview material and restricted content.
78: 
79: ### Negative / Trade-offs
80: 
81: - Creating and reordering curriculum items requires database transactions and parent course row locks.
82: - Reading full lesson content requires a relational join or secondary lookup.
83: 
84: ## Evidence / References
85: 
86: - [Architecture.md](file:///d:/dev%20folder/nextjs/nextjs/docs/Architecture.md)
87: - [Entities.md](file:///d:/dev%20folder/nextjs/nextjs/docs/reference/Entities.md)
88: - `prisma/schema.prisma`
89: - Automated test suites: `src/__tests__/security/idor.test.ts`, `src/services/__tests__/concurrency.test.ts`
````

## File: docs/decisions/README.md
````markdown
 1: # Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)
 2: 
 3: This directory contains the official Architectural Decision Records for this project.
 4: 
 5: ## Index of Decisions
 6: 
 7: | ADR #                                  | Title                                                              | Status   | Date       |
 8: | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- | ---------- |
 9: | [001](001-use-layered-architecture.md) | Use 5-Layer Downward Architecture                                  | Accepted | 2026-07-20 |
10: | [002](002-use-neon-with-prisma.md)     | Use Neon PostgreSQL with Prisma ORM                                | Accepted | 2026-07-20 |
11: | [003](003-use-shadcn-ui.md)            | Use shadcn/ui Component Library                                    | Accepted | 2026-07-20 |
12: | [004](004-lms-domain-model.md)         | Use Dedicated Curriculum, Enrollment, and Isolated Progress Models | Accepted | 2026-09-12 |
13: 
14: ---
15: 
16: ## When to Write an ADR
17: 
18: Write an ADR when a decision:
19: 
20: - Introduces or changes an architectural layer or boundary.
21: - Changes database provider, ORM, or major transaction pattern.
22: - Changes authentication, authorization, or security model.
23: - Introduces an impactful third-party infrastructure dependency.
24: - Alters public contracts or API conventions across multiple features.
25: 
26: _Do NOT write ADRs for local variable renaming, trivial component refactoring, or minor UI tweaks._
27: 
28: To create a new ADR, copy [`TEMPLATE.md`](TEMPLATE.md) and number it sequentially (`004-...`).
````

## File: docs/design/anti-slop.md
````markdown
 1: # Design System Contract — Anti-Slop Doctrine
 2: 
 3: Core principles to eliminate generic, template-driven AI output and ensure intentional design in every view.
 4: 
 5: ---
 6: 
 7: ## 1. The 10 Forbidden AI Tells & Remedies
 8: 
 9: 1. **Cards-inside-cards:**
10:    - _Why:_ Clutters visual hierarchy and exposes template nesting.
11:    - _Remedy:_ Flatten the layout. Differentiate content with contrasting background tones (`bg-muted/30`) or simple dividers.
12: 2. **Generic purple-to-blue gradients:**
13:    - _Why:_ The default signature of generic AI SaaS templates.
14:    - _Remedy:_ Use solid `bg-background` with a single high-contrast primary accent token.
15: 3. **Perfectly centered hero sections:**
16:    - _Why:_ Lifeless, uniform, and lacking personality.
17:    - _Remedy:_ Introduce asymmetric balance: left-aligned value propositions paired with an offset interactive preview or curriculum teaser.
18: 4. **Arbitrary pixel values (`p-[13px]`, `w-[317px]`):**
19:    - _Why:_ Breaks rhythm and undermines the design token scale.
20:    - _Remedy:_ Use standardized spacing scale classes (`p-3`, `p-4`, `space-y-6`).
21: 5. **Unnecessary `"use client"` directives:**
22:    - _Why:_ Bloats client bundles and breaks React Server Component streaming.
23:    - _Remedy:_ Strip `"use client"` from components that only render markup without client state or event handlers.
24: 6. **Broken dark mode contrast:**
25:    - _Why:_ Hardcoded text colors become unreadable when switching themes.
26:    - _Remedy:_ Always use semantic color tokens (`text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`) instead of hardcoded hex or gray utilities.
27: 7. **Missing focus rings on interactive elements:**
28:    - _Why:_ Violates WCAG accessibility criteria for keyboard navigation.
29:    - _Remedy:_ Enforce `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:outline-none`.
30: 8. **Sub-40px touch targets:**
31:    - _Why:_ Frustrating and error-prone on mobile touchscreens.
32:    - _Remedy:_ Ensure interactive targets meet the $40\times 40\text{px}$ minimum (using transparent pseudo-elements if the icon itself is smaller).
33: 9. **Excessive or non-interruptible animations:**
34:    - _Why:_ Makes the application feel sluggish and disorienting.
35:    - _Remedy:_ Use snappy spring transitions and always honor `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`.
36: 10. **Missing empty & error states:**
37:     - _Why:_ Renders blank white space or crashes when queries return zero results.
38:     - _Remedy:_ Always provide a dedicated empty state with an illustrative icon, title, description, and primary action.
39: 
40: ---
41: 
42: ## 2. Preferred Defaults vs. Legitimate Flexibility
43: 
44: The design system is a **contract, not a prison**. We enforce consistency without mechanical uniformity:
45: 
46: | Rule                   | Preferred Default                                      | Legitimate Flexible Exception                                           |
47: | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
48: | **Dial Balance**       | Variance 8, Motion 6, Density 4                        | High-density data grids (Density 7), reduced motion (Motion 0).         |
49: | **Color Accents**      | Single primary accent color                            | Status-driven semantic colors (`destructive`, `warning`, `success`).    |
50: | **Concentric Radii**   | $R_{\text{outer}} = R_{\text{inner}} + \text{padding}$ | Embedded icon buttons inside form fields can use fixed standard radius. |
51: | **Shadows vs Borders** | 3-layer shadows over borders                           | Dense data tables and subtle dividers use 1px border lines.             |
52: | **Grid Variation**     | $\ge 3$ layout families per page                       | Focused student video player view adheres to a split-pane layout.       |
````

## File: docs/design/components.md
````markdown
 1: # Design System Contract — Components
 2: 
 3: Canonical contracts and usage guidelines for UI components in `src/components/`. Built on Base UI / Radix and styled with Tailwind CSS v4.
 4: 
 5: ---
 6: 
 7: ## 1. Component Architecture & Hierarchy
 8: 
 9: ```text
10: Page → Layout → Feature → Shared → UI Primitives
11: ```
12: 
13: - **`src/components/ui/`**: Headless/shadcn primitives (Button, Input, Card, Badge, Dialog). Completely generic, no business logic.
14: - **`src/components/shared/`**: Composed reusable patterns (UserMenu, SearchBar, EmptyState).
15: - **`src/components/layout/`**: Page skeletons and wrappers (Navbar, Sidebar, AppShell).
16: - **`src/components/<feature>/`**: Feature-specific UI (e.g. `curriculum-builder.tsx`, `publish-button.tsx`).
17: 
18: ### Principles & Accessibility
19: 
20: - **Server Components first**: Keep client components (`"use client"`) as thin leaf nodes.
21: - **Interactive hit areas**: Minimum $40 \times 40\text{px}$ touch targets on all clickables.
22: - **Accessibility**: Visible focus rings (`focus-visible:ring-2`), semantic HTML, and proper ARIA labels.
23: 
24: ---
25: 
26: ## 2. Button (`@/components/ui/button`)
27: 
28: - **Variants:**
29:   - `default`: Primary actions (`bg-primary text-primary-foreground hover:bg-primary/80`).
30:   - `secondary`: Secondary supporting actions (`bg-secondary text-secondary-foreground`).
31:   - `outline`: Neutral bordered button (`border-border hover:bg-muted`).
32:   - `ghost`: Borderless icon button or toolbar item (`hover:bg-muted`).
33:   - `destructive`: Irreversible or deleting actions (`bg-destructive/10 text-destructive`).
34:   - `link`: Inline text link styling (`text-primary hover:underline`).
35: - **Sizes:** `xs` (h-6), `sm` (h-7), `default` (h-8), `lg` (h-9), `icon` (size-8), `icon-sm` (size-7).
36: - **Press Feedback:** Integrated `active:not-aria-[haspopup]:translate-y-px` and tactile scale.
37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## 3. Card (`@/components/ui/card`)
41: 
42: - **Structure:**
43:   - `<Card>`: Outer container with `rounded-xl border bg-card text-card-foreground shadow-sm`.
44:   - `<CardHeader>`: Contains title, subtitle, and top actions.
45:   - `<CardTitle>`: Bold heading with `text-wrap: balance`.
46:   - `<CardDescription>`: Subdued helper text in `text-muted-foreground`.
47:   - `<CardContent>`: Main card body.
48:   - `<CardFooter>`: Bottom action row.
49: - **Rule:** **Never nest cards inside cards.** Use `bg-muted/40` or subtle horizontal dividers (`<Separator />`) to separate internal content.
50: 
51: ---
52: 
53: ## 4. Form Controls
54: 
55: ### Input (`@/components/ui/input`) & Textarea (`@/components/ui/textarea`)
56: 
57: - Fully integrated with `border-input focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ring/50`.
58: - Always paired with a `<Label htmlFor="...">` element for accessibility.
59: 
60: ### Badge (`@/components/ui/badge`)
61: 
62: - Status indicators: `default` (primary), `secondary`, `destructive`, `outline`.
63: - Used for course status (`DRAFT`, `PUBLISHED`, `ARCHIVED`), level tags, and preview badges.
64: 
65: ---
66: 
67: ## 5. Notifications (Toasts)
68: 
69: - Component: `GooeyToaster` from `goey-toast` (`@/components/ui/goey-toaster`).
70: - Usage: `import { gooeyToast } from "goey-toast"`.
71: - Mounted once in the root app shell. Provides fluid morphing toasts for success, error, warning, and promises.
````

## File: docs/design/tokens.md
````markdown
 1: # Design System Contract — Tokens
 2: 
 3: Canonical reference for design tokens in this LMS application. All tokens are declared in `src/app/globals.css` using Tailwind CSS v4 and the OKLCH color space.
 4: 
 5: ---
 6: 
 7: ## 1. Color Palette (OKLCH)
 8: 
 9: ### Surfaces & Backgrounds
10: 
11: - `bg-background` / `text-foreground`: Root app canvas.
12: - `bg-card` / `text-card-foreground`: Card and panel surfaces.
13: - `bg-popover` / `text-popover-foreground`: Menus, dropdowns, and tooltip containers.
14: - `bg-sidebar` / `text-sidebar-foreground`: Application sidebars and drawers.
15: 
16: ### Action & Accents
17: 
18: - `bg-primary` / `text-primary-foreground`: Primary call-to-action buttons, key badges, active tabs.
19: - `bg-secondary` / `text-secondary-foreground`: Secondary buttons and pill filters.
20: - `bg-accent` / `text-accent-foreground`: Interactive item hover states and subtle highlights.
21: - `bg-muted` / `text-muted-foreground`: Secondary text, metadata captions, subdued card backgrounds.
22: - `bg-destructive` / `text-destructive`: Error alerts, delete buttons, critical validation states.
23: 
24: ### Borders & Rings
25: 
26: - `border-border`: Surface dividing borders.
27: - `border-input`: Form input boundaries.
28: - `ring-ring`: Keyboard focus indicator.
29: 
30: ---
31: 
32: ## 2. Radii & Concentric Geometry
33: 
34: The base radius is `--radius: 0.625rem` (10px). Derived geometric tokens:
35: 
36: - `--radius-sm`: `calc(var(--radius) * 0.6)` (6px) — Badges, small tags.
37: - `--radius-md`: `calc(var(--radius) * 0.8)` (8px) — Buttons, form inputs.
38: - `--radius-lg`: `var(--radius)` (10px) — Cards, dropdown menus.
39: - `--radius-xl`: `calc(var(--radius) * 1.4)` (14px) — Modal dialogs.
40: - `--radius-2xl`: `calc(var(--radius) * 1.8)` (18px) — Large preview panels.
41: - `--radius-3xl`: `calc(var(--radius) * 2.2)` (22px) — Floating bottom sheets.
42: 
43: ### Concentric Radius Formula:
44: 
45: When nesting elements with visual boundaries, the outer radius must match the inner element radius plus padding:
46: $$R_{\text{outer}} = R_{\text{inner}} + \text{padding}$$
47: 
48: ---
49: 
50: ## 3. Elevation & 3-Layer Shadow Composition
51: 
52: Prefer multi-layered shadows over harsh 1px solid borders for visual hierarchy:
53: 
54: - **Ambient Layer:** Wide, low opacity for subtle floor separation.
55: - **Key Layer:** Directional light giving crisp depth.
56: - **Rim Layer:** Subtle 1px inset highlight (`inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.08)` in dark mode).
57: 
58: ---
59: 
60: ## 4. Typography Scale & Wrapping Rules
61: 
62: - **Headlines (`h1`..`h3`):** Always apply `text-wrap: balance` to distribute line breaks symmetrically.
63: - **Body Text:** Limit reading measure to `max-w-[65ch]` with `text-wrap: pretty` to prevent orphan words.
64: - **Data & Numbers:** Always apply `tabular-nums` for timers, completion percentages, prices, and stats.
65: - **Punctuation:** Em-dashes (`—`) and en-dashes (`–`) are banned from visible UI text; use standard hyphens or clean sentence structure.
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## 5. Interaction & Hit Area Defaults
70: 
71: - **Minimum Hit Target:** Physical clickable area must be at least **$40\times 40\text{px}$** (expand small icons with transparent pseudo-elements).
72: - **Tactile Press Feedback:** Interactive controls provide `active:scale-[0.96] transition-transform duration-100 ease-out`.
73: - **Keyboard Focus:** Every interactive control must display `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:outline-none`.
````

## File: docs/domain/lms-domain.md
````markdown
 1: # LMS Domain Model & Business Invariants
 2: 
 3: Canonical reference for the Learning Management System domain models, entity relationships, lifecycle state machines, and business rules.
 4: 
 5: ---
 6: 
 7: ## 1. Domain Entities & Relational Schema
 8: 
 9: ```text
10: User (Role: student | instructor | admin)
11:   │
12:   ├── AuthoredCourses (1..N)
13:   │     └── Course (Status: DRAFT | PUBLISHED | ARCHIVED, Level, Category, Slug)
14:   │           ├── Module (1..N, orderIndex: Int)
15:   │           │     └── Lesson (1..N, orderIndex: Int, isFreePreview: Boolean)
16:   │           │           └── LessonContent (1..1, markdown, HTML, videoUrl, resources)
17:   │           └── CourseEnrollment (1..N, Status: ACTIVE | COMPLETED | ARCHIVED)
18:   │
19:   └── LessonProgress (1..N per Lesson, isCompleted: Boolean)
20: ```
21: 
22: ---
23: 
24: ## 2. Course Lifecycle State Machine
25: 
26: 1. **`DRAFT` (Initial State):**
27:    - Authoring instructors build modules, lessons, and content.
28:    - Visible strictly to the course author and system admins.
29:    - Curriculum mutations (create, edit, delete, reorder) are permitted **only** in this state.
30: 2. **`PUBLISHED` (Live State):**
31:    - Publicly readable and discoverable in the course catalog (`/courses`).
32:    - Open for student enrollments.
33:    - **Publishing Invariant:** Cannot transition `DRAFT → PUBLISHED` unless the course contains **at least 1 module** and **at least 1 lesson**.
34:    - Must be executed under a course row lock (`lockCourseForUpdate`).
35: 3. **`ARCHIVED` (Retired State):**
36:    - Course is retired from the public catalog.
37:    - No new enrollments permitted.
38:    - Visible only to the author and admins.
39:    - Terminal state for curriculum editing.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## 3. The 5 Core Domain Invariants
44: 
45: ### Invariant 1: Slug Stability & Immutability
46: 
47: - Slugs for courses and lessons are generated on initial creation via `slugify()`.
48: - Uniqueness is enforced at the database level with collision retries on `P2002`.
49: - **Rule:** Slugs are **permanently immutable**. Updates to course or lesson titles never modify existing slugs. This protects bookmarks, student URLs, and search rankings.
50: 
51: ### Invariant 2: The 404 Security Policy (Obscured Existence)
52: 
53: - When an unauthorized user (anonymous visitor or unauthenticated student) requests a `DRAFT` or `ARCHIVED` course by slug or ID, the service strictly throws `NotFoundError (404)`, **not** `AuthorizationError (403)`.
54: - Returning `403` leaks that a private or unreleased draft exists; `404` completely obscures it.
55: 
56: ### Invariant 3: Parent Course Row Locking (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`)
57: 
58: - All curriculum mutations (adding/editing/deleting/reordering modules or lessons) and status transitions serialize through the parent course row lock (`lockCourseForUpdate`).
59: - This prevents race conditions where curriculum is mutated concurrently while another process publishes or archives the course.
60: 
61: ### Invariant 4: Two-Phase Atomic Curriculum Reordering
62: 
63: - Both `[courseId, orderIndex]` and `[moduleId, orderIndex]` have unique compound constraints.
64: - Reordering operations verify that the incoming ID array is an exact permutation of existing siblings, assign temporary negative offsets (`-1 - i`) in phase 1, and then assign contiguous sequential zero-based indexes (`0..N-1`) in phase 2.
65: 
66: ### Invariant 5: Idempotent Enrollment & Atomic Progress Tracking
67: 
68: - **Enrollment:** Any authenticated user can enroll in a `PUBLISHED` course. Attempting to enroll when already enrolled is idempotent and safely returns the existing record.
69: - **Progress Tracking:** Enrolled students toggle lesson completion (`toggleLessonCompletion`). The upsert of `LessonProgress`, recalculation of completed lessons, and update of `CourseEnrollment.progressPercentage` execute within a single atomic Prisma transaction. Reaching 100% automatically sets status to `COMPLETED` and records `completedAt`.
70: 
71: ---
72: 
73: ## 4. Content & Video Sanitization Pipeline
74: 
75: - Rich content pipeline: `Raw Markdown → marked.parse() → sanitize-html → persisted bodyHtml`.
76: - Allowed URL schemes: `http:`, `https:` only.
77: - Whitelisted iframe video hosts:
78:   - YouTube (`youtube.com`, `www.youtube.com`)
79:   - Vimeo (`player.vimeo.com`, `vimeo.com`)
80:   - Loom (`loom.com`, `www.loom.com`)
81: - The client must never render unsanitized user markdown with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
````

## File: docs/Features/Instructor-Workspace.md
````markdown
 1: # Instructor Course Management Workspace
 2: 
 3: The Instructor Course Management Workspace provides authorized educators with a dedicated dashboard to author courses, design and organize modular curricula with accessible drag/keyboard controls, manage publication lifecycles, and monitor student enrollment rosters with real-time completion percentages.
 4: 
 5: ---
 6: 
 7: ## 1. Role & Access Control
 8: 
 9: - **Required Roles**: Access to `/instructor/*` routes is strictly restricted to users holding the `instructor` or `admin` role.
10: - **Route Guard**: [src/app/(dashboard)/instructor/layout.tsx](<file:///d:/dev%20folder/nextjs/nextjs/src/app/(dashboard)/instructor/layout.tsx>) enforces authentication and role membership:
11:   - Unauthenticated requests are redirected to `/sign-in`.
12:   - Non-instructor users (e.g. students) trigger Next.js `forbidden()`, returning an authentic HTTP 403 response rendered via [src/app/forbidden.tsx](file:///d:/dev%20folder/nextjs/nextjs/src/app/forbidden.tsx).
13: - **Ownership Isolation**: Every course query and mutation strictly asserts that `course.instructorId === session.userId` or that the caller is an administrator. Instructors cannot view, modify, or inspect the rosters of courses authored by other instructors.
14: 
15: ---
16: 
17: ## 2. Route Map
18: 
19: | Route                                               | Type             | Description                                                                                                            |
20: | :-------------------------------------------------- | :--------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
21: | `/instructor/courses`                               | Server Component | Dashboard listing authored courses with status badges, module counts, lesson counts, and student counts.               |
22: | `/instructor/courses/new`                           | Server Component | Form to author a new course with initial `DRAFT` status and collision-safe slug generation.                            |
23: | `/instructor/courses/[courseId]/settings`           | Server Component | Edit course metadata (title, description, level, category, cover image) and manage lifecycle state (archive / delete). |
24: | `/instructor/courses/[courseId]/curriculum`         | Server Component | Interactive curriculum builder for managing modules, lessons, and reordering.                                          |
25: | `/instructor/courses/[courseId]/lessons/[lessonId]` | Server Component | Direct navigation into lesson content editor for Markdown, video embedding, and companion resources.                   |
26: | `/instructor/courses/[courseId]/students`           | Server Component | Student roster table displaying enrolled students, enrollment dates, completion dates, and progress percentages.       |
27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: ## 3. Interactive Curriculum Builder
31: 
32: The curriculum builder ([src/components/instructor/curriculum-builder.tsx](file:///d:/dev%20folder/nextjs/nextjs/src/components/instructor/curriculum-builder.tsx)) is an interactive client component providing:
33: 
34: - **Inline Title Editing**: Double-click or click the edit icon to rename modules and lessons with keyboard shortcuts (Enter to save, Escape to cancel).
35: - **Accessible Reordering**: Keyboard and screen-reader accessible Up/Down arrow buttons with minimum 40x40px touch targets alongside responsive visual feedback (`active:scale-[0.98]`).
36: - **Atomic Two-Phase Reordering**: Reordering dispatches to PostgreSQL transactions holding `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` locks on the parent course row, preventing concurrency anomalies.
37: - **Free Preview Toggles**: One-click toggling of `isFreePreview` for introductory lessons.
38: - **Publication Lifecycle Lock**: Structural modifications (adding, deleting, or reordering modules and lessons) are restricted to `DRAFT` courses. Published courses display an informative lock banner advising instructors to unpublish before modifying structure.
39: 
40: ---
41: 
42: ## 4. Publishing Lifecycles & Validation
43: 
44: A course cannot transition to `PUBLISHED` unless:
45: 
46: 1. The caller is the course instructor or an administrator.
47: 2. The course contains **at least one module**.
48: 3. The course contains **at least one lesson**.
49: 
50: Both client-side validation ([PublishButton](file:///d:/dev%20folder/nextjs/nextjs/src/components/instructor/publish-button.tsx)) and server-side atomic transition validation ([CourseService.publishCourse](file:///d:/dev%20folder/nextjs/nextjs/src/services/course.ts)) verify these invariants under row-level database locks.
51: 
52: ---
53: 
54: ## 5. Performance & Zero N+1 Queries
55: 
56: - **Dashboard**: `findCoursesByInstructorId` utilizes Prisma's `_count` aggregation (`modules: true, enrollments: true`) and a bounded batch query for lesson counts, ensuring that loading $N$ courses requires exactly 2 SQL queries.
57: - **Student Roster**: `findEnrollmentsByCourseId` executes a single query with `include: { user: { select: ... } }`, retrieving the entire student roster with user profiles in a single round-trip.
````

## File: docs/Project Context.md
````markdown
 1: # Project Context
 2: 
 3: ## Vision
 4: 
 5: Modern, scalable, production-ready web application. Clean architecture. Long-term quality over rapid feature development.
 6: 
 7: ## Goals
 8: 
 9: Solid foundation · business logic independent from UI · maximize reuse · great DX · AI-friendly codebase · low tech debt.
10: 
11: ## Priorities
12: 
13: 1. Maintainability
14: 2. Performance
15: 3. Scalability
16: 4. Developer Experience
17: 5. Accessibility
18: 6. Security
19: 
20: ## Constraints
21: 
22: TypeScript strict · Server Components by default · minimal client JS · SEO-friendly · accessible · reusable components · clean architecture.
23: 
24: ## Non-Goals
25: 
26: Over-engineering · premature optimization · unnecessary deps · large client bundles · duplicated business logic.
27: 
28: ## Success Criteria
29: 
30: Easy to extend, test, document, AI-understand, and onboard new developers.
31: 
32: ## Documentation Rules
33: 
34: Every significant change updates the docs. ADRs before implementation when possible. Docs always reflect current state.
````

  8: import { BookOpen, LayoutDashboard, LogOut, Settings } from "lucide-react";
  9: export function UserNav() {
 10:   const router = useRouter();
 11:   const { data: session, isPending } = authClient.useSession();
 12:   const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = React.useState(false);
 13:   const menuRef = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
 14:   React.useEffect(() => {
 15:     function handleClickOutside(event: MouseEvent) {
 16:       if (menuRef.current && !menuRef.current.contains(event.target as Node)) {
 17:         setIsOpen(false);
 18:       }
 19:     }
 20:     if (isOpen) {
 21:       document.addEventListener("mousedown", handleClickOutside);
 22:     }
 23:     return () => {
 24:       document.removeEventListener("mousedown", handleClickOutside);
 25:     };
 26:   }, [isOpen]);
 27:   React.useEffect(() => {
 28:     function handleKeyDown(event: KeyboardEvent) {
 29:       if (event.key === "Escape") {
 30:         setIsOpen(false);
 31:       }
 32:     }
 33:     if (isOpen) {
 34:       document.addEventListener("keydown", handleKeyDown);
 35:     }
 36:     return () => {
 37:       document.removeEventListener("keydown", handleKeyDown);
 38:     };
 39:   }, [isOpen]);
 40:   if (isPending) {
 41:     return (
 42:       <div className="bg-muted ring-border size-8 animate-pulse rounded-full ring-1" />
 43:     );
 44:   }
 45:   if (!session?.user) {
 46:     return null;
 47:   }
 48:   const user = session.user;
 49:   const initials = user.name
 50:     ? user.name
 51:         .split(" ")
 52:         .map((n) => n[0])
 53:         .join("")
 54:         .slice(0, 2)
 55:         .toUpperCase()
 56:     : "U";
 57:   const handleSignOut = async () => {
 58:     try {
 59:       await authClient.signOut();
 60:       gooeyToast.success("Signed out successfully");
 61:       setIsOpen(false);
 62:       router.push("/sign-in");
 63:       router.refresh();
 64:     } catch {
 65:       gooeyToast.error("Failed to sign out");
 66:     }
 67:   };
 68:   return (
 69:     <div className="relative" ref={menuRef}>
 70:       <button
 71:         type="button"
 72:         onClick={() => setIsOpen((prev) => !prev)}
 73:         className="bg-primary/10 text-primary ring-primary/20 hover:ring-primary/40 focus-visible:ring-ring flex size-9 cursor-pointer items-center justify-center rounded-full text-xs font-semibold ring-1 transition-all focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:outline-none active:scale-[0.96]"
 74:         aria-expanded={isOpen}
 75:         aria-haspopup="menu"
 76:         aria-label="User navigation menu"
 77:       >
 78:         {user.image ? (
 79:           <Image
 80:             src={user.image}
 81:             alt={user.name || "User avatar"}
 82:             width={36}
 83:             height={36}
 84:             className="size-full rounded-full object-cover"
 85:           />
 86:         ) : (
 87:           <span>{initials}</span>
 88:         )}
 89:       </button>
 90:       {isOpen && (
 91:         <div
 92:           role="menu"
 93:           aria-orientation="vertical"
 94:           className="border-border bg-card text-card-foreground animate-in fade-in-50 zoom-in-95 absolute right-0 z-50 mt-2 w-56 origin-top-right rounded-xl border p-1 shadow-lg ring-1 ring-black/5 duration-100"
 95:         >
 96:           {}
 97:           <div className="border-border border-b px-3 py-2.5">
 98:             <p className="text-foreground truncate text-xs font-semibold">
 99:               {user.name || "My Account"}
100:             </p>
101:             <p className="text-muted-foreground truncate text-[11px]">
102:               {user.email}
103:             </p>
104:           </div>
105:           {}
106:           <div className="py-1">
107:             <Link
108:               href="/courses"
109:               onClick={() => setIsOpen(false)}
110:               className="text-muted-foreground hover:bg-muted hover:text-foreground flex items-center gap-2.5 rounded-lg px-3 py-2 text-xs transition-colors"
111:               role="menuitem"
112:             >
113:               <BookOpen className="size-4" aria-hidden="true" />
114:               <span>Browse Courses</span>
115:             </Link>
116:             <Link
117:               href="/instructor/courses"
118:               onClick={() => setIsOpen(false)}
119:               className="text-muted-foreground hover:bg-muted hover:text-foreground flex items-center gap-2.5 rounded-lg px-3 py-2 text-xs transition-colors"
120:               role="menuitem"
121:             >
122:               <LayoutDashboard className="size-4" aria-hidden="true" />
123:               <span>Instructor Workspace</span>
124:             </Link>
125:             <Link
126:               href="/settings/profile"
127:               onClick={() => setIsOpen(false)}
128:               className="text-muted-foreground hover:bg-muted hover:text-foreground flex items-center gap-2.5 rounded-lg px-3 py-2 text-xs transition-colors"
129:               role="menuitem"
130:             >
131:               <Settings className="size-4" aria-hidden="true" />

135:           <div className="border-border border-t py-1">
136:             <button

## File: src/components/features/catalog/course-pagination.tsx
````typescript
 1: import Link from "next/link";
 2: import { ChevronLeft, ChevronRight } from "lucide-react";
 3: export interface CoursePaginationProps {
 4:   currentPage: number;
 5:   totalPages: number;
 6:   searchParams?: Record<string, string | string[] | undefined>;
 7: }
 8: export function CoursePagination({
 9:   currentPage,
10:   totalPages,
11:   searchParams = {},
12: }: CoursePaginationProps) {
13:   if (totalPages <= 1) return null;
14:   const createPageUrl = (page: number) => {
15:     const params = new URLSearchParams();
16:     for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(searchParams)) {
17:       if (value && key !== "page") {
18:         if (Array.isArray(value)) {
19:           for (const v of value) params.append(key, v);
20:         } else {
21:           params.set(key, value);
22:         }
23:       }
24:     }
25:     params.set("page", String(page));
26:     return `/courses?${params.toString()}`;
27:   };
28:   const pages: number[] = [];
29:   const startPage = Math.max(1, currentPage - 2);
30:   const endPage = Math.min(totalPages, currentPage + 2);
31:   for (let i = startPage; i <= endPage; i++) {
32:     pages.push(i);
33:   }
34:   return (
35:     <nav
36:       className="flex items-center justify-center gap-1.5 pt-6 pb-2"
37:       aria-label="Course catalog pagination"
38:     >
39:       {}
40:       {currentPage > 1 ? (
41:         <Link
42:           href={createPageUrl(currentPage - 1)}
43:           className="border-input bg-background hover:bg-muted text-foreground inline-flex min-h-10 min-w-10 items-center justify-center rounded-md border text-sm font-medium transition-transform active:scale-[0.96] motion-reduce:transform-none"
44:           aria-label="Go to previous page"
45:         >
46:           <ChevronLeft className="h-4 w-4" aria-hidden="true" />
47:         </Link>
48:       ) : (
49:         <span
50:           className="border-input/50 text-muted-foreground/40 inline-flex min-h-10 min-w-10 cursor-not-allowed items-center justify-center rounded-md border text-sm"
51:           aria-disabled="true"
52:         >
53:           <ChevronLeft className="h-4 w-4" aria-hidden="true" />
54:         </span>
55:       )}
56:       {}
57:       {pages.map((p) => {
58:         const isCurrent = p === currentPage;
59:         return isCurrent ? (
60:           <span
61:             key={p}
62:             className="bg-primary text-primary-foreground inline-flex min-h-10 min-w-10 items-center justify-center rounded-md text-sm font-semibold tabular-nums shadow-xs"
63:             aria-current="page"
64:           >
65:             {p}
66:           </span>
67:         ) : (
68:           <Link
69:             key={p}
70:             href={createPageUrl(p)}
71:             className="border-input bg-background hover:bg-muted text-foreground inline-flex min-h-10 min-w-10 items-center justify-center rounded-md border text-sm font-medium tabular-nums transition-transform active:scale-[0.96] motion-reduce:transform-none"
72:             aria-label={`Go to page ${p}`}
73:           >
74:             {p}
75:           </Link>
76:         );
77:       })}
78:       {}
79:       {currentPage < totalPages ? (
80:         <Link
81:           href={createPageUrl(currentPage + 1)}
82:           className="border-input bg-background hover:bg-muted text-foreground inline-flex min-h-10 min-w-10 items-center justify-center rounded-md border text-sm font-medium transition-transform active:scale-[0.96] motion-reduce:transform-none"
83:           aria-label="Go to next page"
84:         >
85:           <ChevronRight className="h-4 w-4" aria-hidden="true" />
86:         </Link>
87:       ) : (
88:         <span
89:           className="border-input/50 text-muted-foreground/40 inline-flex min-h-10 min-w-10 cursor-not-allowed items-center justify-center rounded-md border text-sm"
90:           aria-disabled="true"
91:         >
92:           <ChevronRight className="h-4 w-4" aria-hidden="true" />
93:         </span>
94:       )}
95:     </nav>
96:   );
97: }
````
