## File: docs/reference/Entities.md
````markdown
 1: # LMS Domain Entity Reference
 2: 
 3: Comprehensive specification of relational entities, fields, constraints, relations, and invariants in the Next.js LMS platform.
 4: 
 5: ---
 6: 
 7: ## 1. Authentication & RBAC Entities
 8: 
 9: ### User
10: 
11: - Primary entity for system accounts and instructor/student profiles.
12: - **Table:** `user`
13: - **Core fields:**
14:   - `id`: Unique identifier (String, cuid)
15:   - `name`: Display name (String)
16:   - `email`: Unique email address (String)
17:   - `emailVerified`: Email verification status (Boolean)
18:   - `image`: Auth provider avatar image URL (String, optional)
19: - **Profile fields:**
20:   - `headline`: Professional headline, max 100 chars (String, optional)
21:   - `bio`: Biography summary, max 1000 chars (String, optional)
22:   - `avatarUrl`: Custom profile avatar URL (String, optional)
23:   - `website`: Portfolio/personal website URL (String, optional)
24: - **Relations:** `userRoles[]`, `sessions[]`, `accounts[]`, `authoredCourses[]`, `enrollments[]`, `lessonProgress[]`
25: 
26: ### Role & Permission
27: 
28: - **Role (`role`):** Standard RBAC roles (`admin`, `instructor`, `student`).
29: - **Permission (`permission`):** Granular entitlements `resource:action` with `@@unique([resource, action])`.
30: - **Join Tables:** `user_role` (`@@unique([userId, roleId])`) and `role_permission` (`@@unique([roleId, permissionId])`).
31: 
32: ---
33: 
34: ## 2. Curriculum Entities
35: 
36: ### Course
37: 
38: - Core curriculum container representing an educational course.
39: - **Table:** `course`
40: - **Fields:**
41:   - `id`: CUID (PK)
42:   - `title`: String (3..100 chars)
43:   - `slug`: Globally unique string (immutable, auto-generated from title)
44:   - `description`: Text (optional, max 1000 chars)
45:   - `thumbnailUrl`: String (optional)
46:   - `status`: `CourseStatus` (`DRAFT` | `PUBLISHED` | `ARCHIVED`, default: `DRAFT`)
47:   - `level`: `CourseLevel` (`BEGINNER` | `INTERMEDIATE` | `ADVANCED` | `ALL_LEVELS`)
48:   - `category`: String (optional, max 50 chars)
49:   - `instructorId`: FK $\to$ `User`
50: - **Relations:** `instructor` (User), `modules` (`Module[]`, ordered by `orderIndex`)
51: - **Indexes:** `@@index([instructorId])`, `@@index([status])`, unique `slug`
52: 
53: ### Module
54: 
55: - Section/chapter grouping lessons within a course.
56: - **Table:** `module`
57: - **Fields:** `id`, `title` (2..100 chars), `description` (optional), `orderIndex` (Int, 0-based), `courseId` (FK $\to$ Course)
58: - **Constraints:** `@@unique([courseId, orderIndex])` (guarantees contiguous, deterministic ordering)
59: - **Relations:** `course` (Cascade delete), `lessons` (`Lesson[]`, ordered by `orderIndex`)
60: 
61: ### Lesson
62: 
63: - Atomic unit of instruction within a curriculum module.
64: - **Table:** `lesson`
65: - **Fields:** `id`, `title` (2..100 chars), `slug` (unique per module), `orderIndex` (Int, 0-based), `durationMinutes` (optional), `isFreePreview` (Boolean, default `false`), `moduleId` (FK $\to$ Module)
66: - **Constraints:** `@@unique([moduleId, slug])`, `@@unique([moduleId, orderIndex])`
67: - **Relations:** `module` (Cascade delete), `content` (`LessonContent?`, 1-to-1)
68: 
69: ### LessonContent
70: 
71: - Heavy educational content isolated from lightweight navigation queries.
72: - **Table:** `lesson_content`
73: - **Fields:** `id`, `lessonId` (FK $\to$ Lesson, unique), `bodyMarkdown` (optional, max 50k chars), `bodyHtml` (compiled/sanitized), `videoUrl` (YouTube/Vimeo/Loom), `resources` (JSON array of `{ name, url }`)
74: - **Access:** Editable by author/admin on `DRAFT` and `PUBLISHED`. Readable publicly if `isFreePreview === true` & `PUBLISHED`, otherwise enrolled students/author/admin only.
75: 
76: ---
77: 
78: ## 3. Enrollment & Progress Entities
79: 
80: ### CourseEnrollment
81: 
82: - Student enrollment in a course with aggregate completion metrics.
83: - **Table:** `course_enrollment`
84: - **Fields:** `id`, `userId` (FK $\to$ User), `courseId` (FK $\to$ Course), `status` (`ACTIVE` | `COMPLETED` | `ARCHIVED`), `progressPercentage` (Int 0..100), `enrolledAt`, `completedAt`, `lastAccessedAt`
85: - **Constraints:** `@@unique([userId, courseId])` (one active enrollment per student per course)
86: 
87: ### LessonProgress
88: 
89: - Per-user, per-lesson progress tracking. Strictly user-scoped and never shared.
90: - **Table:** `lesson_progress`
91: - **Fields:** `id`, `userId` (FK $\to$ User), `lessonId` (FK $\to$ Lesson), `isCompleted` (Boolean), `completedAt`, `lastAccessedAt`
92: - **Constraints:** `@@unique([userId, lessonId])`
93: - **Critical Invariant:** Progress is NEVER a column on `Lesson`; it is always user-isolated via `LessonProgress`.
````

  1: generator client {

  8: 
  9: // ──────────────────────────────────────────────
 10: // Better Auth Models
 11: // ──────────────────────────────────────────────
 12: 
 13: model User {
 14:   id            String    @id @default(cuid())
 15:   email         String    @unique
 16:   name          String?
 17:   emailVerified Boolean   @default(false)
 18:   image         String?
 19:   headline      String?
 20:   bio           String?
 21:   avatarUrl     String?
 22:   website       String?
 23:   createdAt     DateTime  @default(now())
 24:   updatedAt     DateTime  @updatedAt
 25:   sessions      Session[]
 26:   accounts      Account[]
 27:   userRoles     UserRole[]
 28:   authoredCourses Course[] @relation("AuthoredCourses")
 29:   enrollments   CourseEnrollment[]
 30:   lessonProgress LessonProgress[]
 31: 
 32:   @@map("user")
 33: }
 34: 
 35: model Session {
 36:   id        String   @id
 37:   expiresAt DateTime
 38:   token     String
 39:   createdAt DateTime @default(now())
 40:   updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
 41:   ipAddress String?
 42:   userAgent String?
 43:   userId    String
 44:   user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
 45: 
 46:   @@unique([token])
 47:   @@index([userId])
 48:   @@map("session")
 49: }
 50: 
 51: model Account {
 52:   id                    String    @id
 53:   accountId             String
 54:   providerId            String
 55:   userId                String
 56:   user                  User      @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
 57:   accessToken           String?
 58:   refreshToken          String?
 59:   idToken               String?
 60:   accessTokenExpiresAt  DateTime?
 61:   refreshTokenExpiresAt DateTime?
 62:   scope                 String?
 63:   password              String?
 64:   createdAt             DateTime  @default(now())
 65:   updatedAt             DateTime  @updatedAt
 66: 
 67:   @@index([userId])
 68:   @@map("account")
 69: }
 70: 
 71: model Verification {
 72:   id         String   @id
 73:   identifier String
 74:   value      String
 75:   expiresAt  DateTime
 76:   createdAt  DateTime @default(now())
 77:   updatedAt  DateTime @updatedAt
 78: 
 79:   @@index([identifier])
 80:   @@map("verification")
 81: }
 82: 
 83: // ──────────────────────────────────────────────
 84: // Authorization Models (RBAC)
 85: // ──────────────────────────────────────────────
 86: 
 87: model Role {
 88:   id            String           @id @default(cuid())
 89:   name          String           @unique
 90:   description   String?
 91:   createdAt     DateTime         @default(now())
 92:   updatedAt     DateTime         @updatedAt
 93:   userRoles     UserRole[]
 94:   rolePermissions RolePermission[]
 95: 
 96:   @@map("role")
 97: }
 98: 
 99: model Permission {
100:   id            String           @id @default(cuid())
101:   name          String           @unique
102:   description   String?
103:   resource      String
104:   action        String
105:   createdAt     DateTime         @default(now())
106:   updatedAt     DateTime         @updatedAt
107:   rolePermissions RolePermission[]
108: 
109:   @@unique([resource, action])
110:   @@map("permission")
111: }
112: 
113: model UserRole {
114:   id        String   @id @default(cuid())
115:   userId    String
116:   roleId    String
117:   user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
118:   role      Role     @relation(fields: [roleId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
119:   createdAt DateTime @default(now())
120: 
121:   @@unique([userId, roleId])
122:   @@index([userId])
123:   @@index([roleId])
124:   @@map("user_role")
125: }
126: 
127: model RolePermission {
128:   id           String     @id @default(cuid())
129:   roleId       String
130:   permissionId String
131:   role         Role       @relation(fields: [roleId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
132:   permission   Permission @relation(fields: [permissionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
133:   createdAt    DateTime   @default(now())
134: 
135:   @@unique([roleId, permissionId])
136:   @@index([roleId])
137:   @@index([permissionId])
138:   @@map("role_permission")
139: }
140: 
141: // ──────────────────────────────────────────────
142: // Course & Curriculum Models
143: // ──────────────────────────────────────────────
144: 
145: enum CourseStatus {
146:   DRAFT
147:   PUBLISHED
148:   ARCHIVED
149: }
150: 
151: enum CourseLevel {
152:   BEGINNER
153:   INTERMEDIATE
154:   ADVANCED
155:   ALL_LEVELS
156: }
157: 
158: model Course {
159:   id           String       @id @default(cuid())
160:   title        String
161:   slug         String       @unique
162:   description  String?
163:   thumbnailUrl String?
164:   status       CourseStatus @default(DRAFT)
165:   level        CourseLevel  @default(ALL_LEVELS)
166:   category     String?
167:   instructorId String
168:   instructor   User         @relation("AuthoredCourses", fields: [instructorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
169:   modules      Module[]
170:   enrollments  CourseEnrollment[]
171:   createdAt    DateTime     @default(now())
172:   updatedAt    DateTime     @updatedAt
173: 
174:   @@index([instructorId])
175:   @@index([status])
176:   @@map("course")
177: }
178: 
179: model Module {
180:   id          String   @id @default(cuid())
181:   title       String
182:   description String?
183:   orderIndex  Int
184:   courseId    String
185:   course      Course   @relation(fields: [courseId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
186:   lessons     Lesson[]
187:   createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
188:   updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt
189: 
190:   @@unique([courseId, orderIndex])
191:   @@index([courseId])
192:   @@map("module")
193: }
194: 
195: model Lesson {
196:   id              String         @id @default(cuid())
197:   title           String
198:   slug            String
199:   orderIndex      Int
200:   durationMinutes Int?
201:   isFreePreview   Boolean        @default(false)
202:   moduleId        String
203:   module          Module         @relation(fields: [moduleId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
204:   content         LessonContent?
205:   progress        LessonProgress[]
206:   createdAt       DateTime       @default(now())
207:   updatedAt       DateTime       @updatedAt
208: 
209:   @@unique([moduleId, slug])
210:   @@unique([moduleId, orderIndex])
211:   @@index([moduleId])
212:   @@map("lesson")
213: }
214: 
215: model LessonContent {
216:   id           String   @id @default(cuid())
217:   lessonId     String   @unique
218:   lesson       Lesson   @relation(fields: [lessonId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
219:   bodyMarkdown String?
220:   bodyHtml     String?
221:   videoUrl     String?
222:   resources    Json?
223:   createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
224:   updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt
225: 
226:   @@map("lesson_content")
227: }
228: 
229: // ──────────────────────────────────────────────
230: // Enrollment & Progress Models
231: // ──────────────────────────────────────────────
232: 
233: enum EnrollmentStatus {
234:   ACTIVE
235:   COMPLETED
236:   ARCHIVED
237: }
238: 
239: model CourseEnrollment {
240:   id                 String           @id @default(cuid())
241:   userId             String
242:   courseId           String
243:   status             EnrollmentStatus @default(ACTIVE)
244:   progressPercentage Int              @default(0)
245:   enrolledAt         DateTime         @default(now())
246:   completedAt        DateTime?
247:   lastAccessedAt     DateTime         @default(now())
248:   user               User             @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
249:   course             Course           @relation(fields: [courseId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
250: 
251:   @@unique([userId, courseId])
252:   @@index([userId])
253:   @@index([courseId])
254:   @@map("course_enrollment")
255: }
256: 
257: model LessonProgress {
258:   id             String    @id @default(cuid())
259:   userId         String
260:   lessonId       String
261:   isCompleted    Boolean   @default(false)
262:   completedAt    DateTime?
263:   lastAccessedAt DateTime  @default(now())
264:   user           User      @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
265:   lesson         Lesson    @relation(fields: [lessonId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
266: 
267:   @@unique([userId, lessonId])
268:   @@index([userId])
269:   @@index([lessonId])
270:   @@map("lesson_progress")
271: }

## File: docs/API/Database.md
````markdown
  1: # Database
  2: 
  3: PostgreSQL on Neon. Prisma ORM. Repositories are the only layer that talks to Prisma.
  4: 
  5: ## Principles
  6: 
  7: Simple, normalized, scalable, easy to maintain. **No business logic in the database.**
  8: 
  9: ## Access Flow
 10: 
 11: ```
 12: UI → Actions → Services → Repositories → Prisma → PostgreSQL
 13: ```
 14: 
 15: ## Schema
 16: 
 17: ### Authentication Models (Better Auth)
 18: 
 19: #### User
 20: 
 21: | Field         | Type     | Notes         |
 22: | ------------- | -------- | ------------- |
 23: | id            | String   | PK (CUID)     |
 24: | email         | String   | Unique        |
 25: | name          | String?  | Optional      |
 26: | emailVerified | Boolean  | Default false |
 27: | image         | String?  | Optional      |
 28: | createdAt     | DateTime | Auto          |
 29: | updatedAt     | DateTime | Auto          |
 30: 
 31: Relations: `sessions[]`, `accounts[]`, `userRoles[]`
 32: 
 33: #### Session
 34: 
 35: | Field     | Type     | Notes     |
 36: | --------- | -------- | --------- |
 37: | id        | String   | PK        |
 38: | token     | String   | Unique    |
 39: | userId    | String   | FK → User |
 40: | expiresAt | DateTime | —         |
 41: | ipAddress | String?  | Optional  |
 42: | userAgent | String?  | Optional  |
 43: | createdAt | DateTime | Auto      |
 44: | updatedAt | DateTime | Auto      |
 45: 
 46: Relations: `user`
 47: 
 48: #### Account
 49: 
 50: | Field                 | Type      | Notes     |
 51: | --------------------- | --------- | --------- |
 52: | id                    | String    | PK        |
 53: | accountId             | String    | —         |
 54: | providerId            | String    | —         |
 55: | userId                | String    | FK → User |
 56: | accessToken           | String?   | Optional  |
 57: | refreshToken          | String?   | Optional  |
 58: | idToken               | String?   | Optional  |
 59: | accessTokenExpiresAt  | DateTime? | Optional  |
 60: | refreshTokenExpiresAt | DateTime? | Optional  |
 61: | scope                 | String?   | Optional  |
 62: | password              | String?   | Hashed    |
 63: | createdAt             | DateTime  | Auto      |
 64: | updatedAt             | DateTime  | Auto      |
 65: 
 66: Relations: `user`
 67: 
 68: #### Verification
 69: 
 70: | Field      | Type     | Notes |
 71: | ---------- | -------- | ----- |
 72: | id         | String   | PK    |
 73: | identifier | String   | —     |
 74: | value      | String   | —     |
 75: | expiresAt  | DateTime | —     |
 76: | createdAt  | DateTime | Auto  |
 77: | updatedAt  | DateTime | Auto  |
 78: 
 79: ### Authorization Models (RBAC)
 80: 
 81: #### Role
 82: 
 83: | Field       | Type     | Notes     |
 84: | ----------- | -------- | --------- |
 85: | id          | String   | PK (CUID) |
 86: | name        | String   | Unique    |
 87: | description | String?  | Optional  |
 88: | createdAt   | DateTime | Auto      |
 89: | updatedAt   | DateTime | Auto      |
 90: 
 91: Relations: `userRoles[]`, `rolePermissions[]`
 92: 
 93: #### Permission
 94: 
 95: | Field       | Type     | Notes         |
 96: | ----------- | -------- | ------------- |
 97: | id          | String   | PK (CUID)     |
 98: | name        | String   | Unique        |
 99: | resource    | String   | Resource type |
100: | action      | String   | Action type   |
101: | description | String?  | Optional      |
102: | createdAt   | DateTime | Auto          |
103: | updatedAt   | DateTime | Auto          |
104: 
105: Relations: `rolePermissions[]`
106: 
107: Unique constraint: `[resource, action]`
108: 
109: #### UserRole
110: 
111: | Field     | Type     | Notes     |
112: | --------- | -------- | --------- |
113: | id        | String   | PK (CUID) |
114: | userId    | String   | FK → User |
115: | roleId    | String   | FK → Role |
116: | createdAt | DateTime | Auto      |
117: 
118: Relations: `user`, `role`
119: 
120: Unique constraint: `[userId, roleId]`
121: 
122: #### RolePermission
123: 
124: | Field        | Type     | Notes           |
125: | ------------ | -------- | --------------- |
126: | id           | String   | PK (CUID)       |
127: | roleId       | String   | FK → Role       |
128: | permissionId | String   | FK → Permission |
129: | createdAt    | DateTime | Auto            |
130: 
131: Relations: `role`, `permission`
132: 
133: Unique constraint: `[roleId, permissionId]`
134: 
135: ## Commands
136: 
137: ```bash
138: pnpm prisma migrate dev     # create + apply migration
139: pnpm prisma generate        # generate Prisma Client
140: pnpm prisma studio          # open Prisma Studio
141: pnpm prisma db push         # push schema changes (dev only)
142: ```
143: 
144: Never modify production DBs manually. Always version-control migrations.
145: 
146: ## Naming
147: 
148: - Models: singular PascalCase.
149: - Fields: camelCase.
150: - Relations: explicit names where needed.
151: 
152: ## Authorization Flow
153: 
154: ```
155: User → UserRole → Role → RolePermission → Permission
156: ```
157: 
158: Example permissions:
159: 
160: - `users:read` - Read user data
161: - `users:write` - Create/update users
162: - `users:delete` - Delete users
163: - `sessions:revoke:any` - Revoke any user's session (admin)
164: 
165: ## Performance
166: 
167: Add indexes only when justified. Avoid unnecessary joins. Paginate large results. Select only required fields.
168: 
169: Existing indexes:
170: 
171: - `Session.userId`
172: - `Account.userId`
173: - `Verification.identifier`
174: - `UserRole.userId`, `UserRole.roleId`
175: - `RolePermission.roleId`, `RolePermission.permissionId`
176: 
177: ## Security
178: 
179: - Never expose password hashes, secrets, or internal identifiers without authorization
180: - Validate input before any DB operation
181: - All authorization checks happen server-side in services
182: - Session ownership must be verified before revocation
183: - Never trust client-provided user IDs, roles, or permissions
````

## File: docs/Authentication.md
````markdown
 1: # Authentication
 2: 
 3: Better Auth integration with RBAC.
 4: 
 5: ## Why Better Auth
 6: 
 7: Open-source, self-hosted, no vendor lock-in. Built-in Prisma adapter. DB-backed sessions with cookie cache. Email/password + OAuth + plugin ecosystem. Strong TS support.
 8: 
 9: ## Flow
10: 
11: ```
12: Actions → Services → Repositories → Better Auth → Prisma → PostgreSQL (Neon)
13: ```
14: 
15: - **Actions:** validate input, invoke services, return structured results.
16: - **Services:** business logic + authorization decisions.
17: - **Repositories:** persistence only.
18: - **Better Auth:** auth infrastructure only — app talks to it through services/repos.
19: 
20: ## Domain Separation
21: 
22: - **Auth layer (Better Auth):** sessions, accounts, verification, password reset, email verification.
23: - **Domain layer (app):** user, roles, permissions, user-role, role-permission.
24: 
25: App never talks to Better Auth directly except via configured clients.
26: 
27: ## RBAC
28: 
29: One user → many roles (many-to-many). Permissions inherited from roles. Architecture supports future direct user permissions.
30: 
31: Default roles: `student`, `instructor`, `admin`.
32: 
33: Role assignment is strictly restricted: only users with the `admin` role (or possessing `roles:assign` permission) can assign or remove roles from users. Self-elevation of roles by non-admins is strictly prevented in `AuthorizationService`.
34: 
35: ### Instructor Role & Workspace Guards
36: 
37: - Access to the `/instructor/*` workspace is guarded at the Server Component layout level ([src/app/(dashboard)/instructor/layout.tsx](<file:///d:/dev%20folder/nextjs/nextjs/src/app/(dashboard)/instructor/layout.tsx>)) using `requireAnyRole(session.user.id, ["instructor", "admin"])`.
38: - Unauthenticated requests are redirected to `/sign-in`.
39: - Authenticated non-instructors (such as students) trigger Next.js `forbidden()`, returning HTTP 403 status code rendered by [src/app/forbidden.tsx](file:///d:/dev%20folder/nextjs/nextjs/src/app/forbidden.tsx).
40: - All instructor domain services strictly enforce individual resource ownership (`course.instructorId === session.userId` or admin role) on both read queries and write mutations.
41: 
42: ## File Map
43: 
44: ```
45: src/lib/
46:   auth.ts            # Better Auth server config
47:   auth-client.ts     # Better Auth React client
48:   auth-helpers.ts    # requireAuth, requireRole, getCurrentUser
49:   action-result.ts   # ActionResult discriminated union and builders
50:   db.ts              # Prisma client singleton
51:   env.ts             # Zod-validated env vars
52:   errors/            # Typed domain errors
53:   validations/       # Zod schemas (auth, profile, pagination)
54: src/repositories/
55:   user.ts, role.ts, permission.ts, user-role.ts, role-permission.ts, session.ts
56: src/services/
57:   auth.ts, authorization.ts, session.ts, user.ts, profile.ts
58: src/actions/
59:   auth.ts, profile.ts
60: src/components/
61:   profile/           # Profile form components
62: middleware.ts        # Route protection (root)
63: ```
64: 
65: ## Environment
66: 
67: | Variable             | Purpose                          |
68: | -------------------- | -------------------------------- |
69: | `DATABASE_URL`       | Neon pooled connection           |
70: | `DIRECT_URL`         | Neon direct (for Prisma CLI)     |
71: | `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` | Encryption secret (min 32 chars) |
72: | `BETTER_AUTH_URL`    | Base URL                         |
73: 
74: ## Migration
75: 
76: ```bash
77: pnpm prisma migrate dev --name add-better-auth-and-rbac
78: ```
````

## File: docs/Coding Standards.md
````markdown
 1: # Coding Standards
 2: 
 3: ## General
 4: 
 5: TypeScript strict mode. Readable > clever. Simple > abstract. Never duplicate business logic.
 6: 
 7: ## File Naming
 8: 
 9: | Type       | Convention            |
10: | ---------- | --------------------- |
11: | Components | `PascalCase.tsx`      |
12: | Hooks      | `useCamelCase.ts`     |
13: | Utilities  | `camelCase.ts`        |
14: | Constants  | `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE.ts` |
15: | Types      | `types.ts`            |
16: 
17: ## Imports
18: 
19: Always use path aliases (`@/...`). Never relative paths crossing multiple directories.
20: 
21: ## Components
22: 
23: **Prefer:** Server Components, small size, composition, single responsibility.
24: **Avoid:** huge components, nested conditionals, business logic in UI.
25: 
26: ## Styling
27: 
28: Tailwind only. No inline styles. No CSS duplication.
29: 
30: ## State Management (priority order)
31: 
32: 1. Server state
33: 2. URL state (search/route params)
34: 3. Local state (`useState`)
35: 4. Context (only for truly global: theme, auth)
36: 
37: No premature global state.
38: 
39: ## Business Logic
40: 
41: Business logic lives only in Services. Never in components, hooks, or repositories.
42: 
43: ## Database
44: 
45: All DB access through repositories. Never call Prisma from UI.
46: 
47: ## Server Actions & Error Handling
48: 
49: All Server Actions must return a standardized `ActionResult<T>`:
50: 
51: ```typescript
52: export type ActionResult<T = void> =
53:   | { success: true; data: T }
54:   | {
55:       success: false;
56:       error: string;
57:       code?: string;
58:       details?: Record<string, string[]>;
59:     };
60: ```
61: 
62: - Use `actionSuccess(data)` and `actionFailure(error, code, details)` from `@/lib/action-result`.
63: - Use `requireAuth()` and `requireRole(roleName)` from `@/lib/auth-helpers` for action boundary guards.
64: - Validate inputs with Zod schemas before calling Services.
65: - Catch typed `AppError` exceptions and map to user-friendly messages without leaking database internals.
66: 
67: ## Performance
68: 
69: Server Components, lazy loading, memoize only when measured to help. No premature optimization.
70: 
71: ## Security
72: 
73: Validate server input. Sanitize user content. Secrets in env vars. Least privilege.
74: 
75: ## Media & HTML Content Sanitization
76: 
77: - **Explicit Sanitization Pipeline:**
78:   - `Markdown Input → marked.parse() → sanitize-html → persisted bodyHtml → UI`.
79:   - The client must never render unsanitized Markdown or HTML with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
80: - **Security Policy:**
81:   - Schemes: `http:` and `https:` only. Reject all `javascript:`, `data:`, `file:`, `blob:`.
82:   - No inline event-handlers (`onload`, `onerror`, `onclick`).
83:   - Strict WHATWG URL parsing for `<iframe>` and `<img>` sources.
84:   - Video embed whitelist: YouTube (`youtube.com`, `www.youtube.com`), Vimeo (`player.vimeo.com`, `vimeo.com`), Loom (`loom.com`, `www.loom.com`).
85:   - No generic cloud storage provider frameworks in Task 04.
86: 
87: ## Testing
88: 
89: Every important business rule has tests. Critical UI flows have component or integration tests.
90: 
91: ## Documentation
92: 
93: Architecture changes require doc updates. Docs must reflect current reality.
````

 17:   data?: T;

 20: export async function signInAction(

 22: ): Promise<ActionResponse> {

 24:   if (!parsed.success) {
 25:     return {
 26:       success: false,
 27:       error: parsed.error.issues[0]?.message ?? "Invalid input",
 28:     };
 29:   }
 30:   try {
 31:     await authService.signIn(parsed.data.email, parsed.data.password);
 32:     return { success: true };
 33:   } catch (error) {
 34:     if (error instanceof Error) {
 35:       return { success: false, error: error.message };
 36:     }
 37:     return { success: false, error: "Sign in failed" };
 38:   }
 39: }

 45:     return {
 46:       success: false,
 47:       error: parsed.error.issues[0]?.message ?? "Invalid input",
 48:     };

 57:     return { success: true };

 59:     if (error instanceof Error) {
 60:       return { success: false, error: error.message };
 61:     }
 62:     return { success: false, error: "Sign up failed" };
 63:   }
 64: }

 67:     await authService.signOut();

 69:   } catch (error) {
 70:     if (error instanceof Error) {
 71:       return { success: false, error: error.message };

 75: }

  1: import { auth } from "@/lib/auth";
  2: import * as userRepository from "@/repositories/user";
  3: import * as sessionRepository from "@/repositories/session";
  4: import * as roleRepository from "@/repositories/role";
  5: import * as userRoleRepository from "@/repositories/user-role";
  6: import * as authorizationService from "@/services/authorization";
  7: import {
  8:   AuthenticationError,
  9:   AuthorizationError,
 10:   NotFoundError,
 11: } from "@/lib/errors";
 12: import { headers } from "next/headers";
 13: export async function getCurrentSession() {
 14:   const session = await auth.api.getSession({
 15:     headers: await headers(),
 16:   });
 17:   if (!session) {
 18:     throw new AuthenticationError();
 19:   }
 20:   return session;
 21: }
 22: export async function signIn(email: string, password: string) {
 23:   return auth.api.signInEmail({
 24:     body: { email, password },
 25:     headers: await headers(),
 26:   });
 27: }
 28: export async function signUp(
 29:   email: string,
 30:   password: string,
 31:   name: string,
 32:   role?: string,
 33: ) {
 34:   const result = await auth.api.signUpEmail({
 35:     body: { email, password, name },
 36:     headers: await headers(),
 37:   });
 38:   if (result?.user?.id && role === "instructor") {
 39:     const instructorRole = await roleRepository.findRoleByName("instructor");
 40:     if (instructorRole) {
 41:       await userRoleRepository.assignRoleToUser(
 42:         result.user.id,
 43:         instructorRole.id,
 44:       );
 45:     }
 46:   }
 47:   return result;
 48: }
 49: export async function signOut() {
 50:   return auth.api.signOut({
 51:     headers: await headers(),
 52:   });
 53: }
 54: export async function getUserById(id: string) {
 55:   const user = await userRepository.findUserById(id);
 56:   if (!user) {
 57:     throw new NotFoundError("User not found");
 58:   }
 59:   return user;
 60: }
 61: export async function getUserByEmail(email: string) {
 62:   return userRepository.findUserByEmail(email);
 63: }
 64: export async function getUserWithRoles(id: string) {
 65:   const user = await userRepository.findUserWithRoles(id);
 66:   if (!user) {
 67:     throw new NotFoundError("User not found");
 68:   }
 69:   return user;
 70: }
 71: export async function getUserSessions(userId: string) {
 72:   return sessionRepository.findSessionsByUserId(userId);
 73: }
 74: export async function revokeSession(sessionId: string, currentUserId: string) {
 75:   const session = await sessionRepository.findSessionById(sessionId);
 76:   if (!session) {
 77:     throw new NotFoundError("Session not found");
 78:   }
 79:   const ownsSession = session.userId === currentUserId;
 80:   const hasAdminPermission = await authorizationService.hasPermission(
 81:     currentUserId,
 82:     "sessions:revoke:any",
 83:   );
 84:   if (!ownsSession && !hasAdminPermission) {
 85:     throw new AuthorizationError(
 86:       "You do not have permission to revoke this session",
 87:     );
 88:   }
 89:   return sessionRepository.deleteSession(sessionId);
 90: }
 91: export async function revokeAllSessions(userId: string) {
 92:   return sessionRepository.deleteSessionsByUserId(userId);
 93: }
 94: export async function updateUserProfile(
 95:   id: string,
 96:   data: { name?: string; image?: string },
 97: ) {
 98:   const user = await userRepository.findUserById(id);
 99:   if (!user) {
100:     throw new NotFoundError("User not found");
101:   }
102:   return userRepository.updateUser(id, data);
103: }

## File: docs/Development/Git.md
````markdown
 1: # Git Workflow Guide
 2: 
 3: Trunk-based development workflow for the Next.js LMS platform. `master` is the production branch and `dev` is the integration branch.
 4: 
 5: ---
 6: 
 7: ## 1. Branch Strategy
 8: 
 9: ```text
10: master (production / releases)
11:   ↑
12:   │ merge via PR after full verification
13:   │
14:  dev (integration / protected)
15:   ↑
16:   │ merge via PR
17:   │
18: dev/<feature-name> (working branch)
19: ```
20: 
21: - **`master`**: Production-ready code. Protected. Direct commits forbidden.
22: - **`dev`**: Active integration branch. Protected. Direct commits forbidden.
23: - **`dev/<feature>`**: Feature and bug fix branches created off `dev` (e.g. `dev/course-player`, `dev/auth-guards`).
24: 
25: ---
26: 
27: ## 2. Feature Development Lifecycle
28: 
29: 1. **Create branch:**
30: 
31:    ```bash
32:    git checkout dev
33:    git pull origin dev
34:    git checkout -b dev/<feature-name>
35:    ```
36: 
37: 2. **Commit conventions:**
38:    Use Conventional Commits: `type(scope): description`
39:    - `feat`: New user-facing feature
40:    - `fix`: Bug fix
41:    - `docs`: Documentation updates
42:    - `refactor`: Architectural or code restructuring without behavior change
43:    - `test`: Adding or updating test suites
44:    - `chore`: Dependency updates, tooling configuration
45: 
46: 3. **Pre-PR verification (All checks must pass):**
47: 
48:    ```bash
49:    pnpm check       # ESLint + TypeScript + Knip + Prettier
50:    pnpm test        # Jest test suite
51:    pnpm build       # Next.js production build verification
52:    ```
53: 
54: 4. **Create PR to `dev`:**
55:    - Summarize changes, testing performed, and security implications.
56:    - Clean up branch after merge: `git branch -d dev/<feature-name>`.
57: 
58: ---
59: 
60: ## 3. Release Process
61: 
62: 1. Verify `dev` passes all automated tests and quality checks.
63: 2. Bump version in `package.json` following Semantic Versioning (SemVer).
64: 3. Create PR from `dev` into `master`.
65: 4. Tag release on `master`:
66:    ```bash
67:    git checkout master
68:    git pull origin master
69:    git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "Release vX.Y.Z"
70:    git push origin vX.Y.Z
71:    ```
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: ## 4. Safety Invariants
76: 
77: - **Never** commit secrets, private keys, or `.env` files.
78: - **Never** use `git push --force` on shared branches (`dev`, `master`). Use `--force-with-lease` on local feature branches only.
79: - **Database Migrations:** Schema changes must include verified Prisma migrations (`pnpm db:migrate:dev`).
````

## File: docs/Architecture.md
````markdown
  1: # Architecture
  2: 
  3: ## Layers
  4: 
  5: ```
  6: UI → Actions/Routes → Services → Repositories → Database (Prisma + PostgreSQL)
  7: ```
  8: 
  9: ## Responsibilities
 10: 
 11: | Layer            | Does                                                     | Must NOT                                 |
 12: | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
 13: | **UI**           | Render, user interaction                                 | Business logic, direct DB access         |
 14: | **Actions**      | Auth, input validation (Zod), call services              | Business logic, direct repo access       |
 15: | **Services**     | Business rules, multi-repo workflows, complex validation | Know about HTTP, depend on UI frameworks |
 16: | **Repositories** | Queries, CRUD, data mapping                              | Business logic, business rules           |
 17: | **Database**     | Persistence                                              | —                                        |
 18: 
 19: ## Domain Services & Repositories Registry
 20: 
 21: | Domain Area                | Service Layer (`@/services/*`)     | Concrete Repositories (`@/repositories/*`)                       | Primary Responsibilities                                     |
 22: | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
 23: | **Authentication & Users** | `auth.ts`, `session.ts`, `user.ts` | `user.ts`, `session.ts`                                          | Credentials, session management, user lifecycle              |
 24: | **RBAC Authorization**     | `authorization.ts`                 | `role.ts`, `permission.ts`, `user-role.ts`, `role-permission.ts` | Role checks (`admin`, `instructor`, `student`), permissions  |
 25: | **Profile Management**     | `profile.ts`                       | `user.ts`                                                        | Self-ownership profile updates and avatar metadata           |
 26: | **Courses & Publishing**   | `course.ts`                        | `course.ts`                                                      | Course CRUD, slug generation, publishing state machines      |
 27: | **Curriculum Structure**   | `curriculum.ts`                    | `module.ts`, `lesson.ts`                                         | Modules, lessons, atomic two-phase reordering                |
 28: | **Lesson Content & Media** | `lesson-content.ts`                | `lesson-content.ts`                                              | Markdown compilation, HTML sanitization, video normalization |
 29: | **Enrollment**             | `enrollment.ts`                    | `enrollment.ts`                                                  | Student course enrollment, batch status decoration           |
 30: | **Progress & Completion**  | `progress.ts`                      | `lesson-progress.ts`, `enrollment.ts`                            | Atomic progress tracking, percent calculation, next lesson   |
 31: 
 32: ---
 33: 
 34: ## 4-Tier Authorization Doctrine
 35: 
 36: Every server operation enforces security in depth across four distinct layers:
 37: 
 38: ```
 39: [Tier 1: Authentication Guard]
 40:   ↓ (Assert valid Better Auth session; anonymous users denied on protected routes)
 41: [Tier 2: Role Authorization]
 42:   ↓ (Assert required roles: "instructor" or "admin" for authoring operations)
 43: [Tier 3: Resource Ownership]
 44:   ↓ (Assert resource ownership: course.instructorId === session.userId or sessionUserId === targetUserId)
 45: [Tier 4: Lifecycle State Guard]
 46:   ↓ (Assert state invariants: DRAFT for curriculum edits; PUBLISHED for enrollment; ARCHIVED locked)
 47: ```
 48: 
 49: 1. **Tier 1 (Authentication):** Enforced via `requireAuth()` in Server Actions and route handlers. Anonymous users cannot mutate data.
 50: 2. **Tier 2 (Role Authorization):** Enforced via `requireRole(...)` or `requireAnyRole(...)`. Students cannot access instructor workspaces or authoring endpoints.
 51: 3. **Tier 3 (Resource Ownership / IDOR Defense):** Services strictly verify that callers own the resource they are mutating. Instructors cannot modify courses, modules, lessons, or content belonging to other instructors. Students cannot mutate or query other students' progress.
 52: 4. **Tier 4 (Lifecycle State Constraints):** Courses must be in `DRAFT` status for curriculum mutations. Courses cannot be published without at least 1 module and 1 lesson. `ARCHIVED` courses are locked against modifications and denied to regular students.
 53: 
 54: ---
 55: 
 56: ## Principles
 57: 
 58: 1. **Separation of concerns** — business logic only in services; data access only in repos.
 59: 2. **Dependency direction** — flows downward only. Repositories never import services.
 60: 3. **Server Components first** — use Client Components only for state, effects, event handlers, browser APIs.
 61: 4. **Thin routes** — pages compose components and call actions/services; no logic in pages.
 62: 5. **Reusable abstractions** — never introduce a second pattern when one exists.
 63: 
 64: ## When to Add Each Layer
 65: 
 66: - **Repository:** every DB table.
 67: - **Service:** any business rule, multi-step workflow, or operation touching multiple repos.
 68: - **Action:** every user-initiated mutation and any client-component data fetch.
 69: 
 70: ## Type Safety
 71: 
 72: - Never `any`.
 73: - Export reusable types close to the feature.
 74: - Zod for runtime validation; infer TS types from schemas.
 75: 
 76: ---
 77: 
 78: ## Concurrency & Transaction Patterns
 79: 
 80: ### 1. Parent Course Row Locking (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`)
 81: 
 82: All curriculum mutations and course lifecycle transitions are serialized through an explicit parent course row lock (`lockCourseForUpdate(tx, courseId)`):
 83: 
 84: ```
 85: BEGIN TRANSACTION
 86:   ↓
 87: SELECT * FROM course WHERE id = :courseId FOR UPDATE
 88:   ↓ (Status must remain DRAFT for curriculum mutations)
 89: Execute mutation / Verify state
 90:   ↓
 91: COMMIT
 92: ```
 93: 
 94: This synchronization boundary guarantees that:
 95: 
 96: - Concurrent curriculum mutations cannot occur while a course is being published or archived.
 97: - A course cannot be published concurrently with a module/lesson creation, reorder, or deletion.
 98: - Cascading `deleteCourse` is safely serialized against concurrent curriculum mutations.
 99: 
100: ### 2. Atomic Curriculum Reordering
101: 
102: Reordering of modules and lessons guarantees exact sequential ordering `0..N-1` with no duplicates or gaps:
103: 
104: - **In-Transaction Verification:** The current sibling list is fetched inside the transaction after acquiring the lock. The provided ID array must be an exact permutation of existing siblings (no foreign, duplicate, or missing IDs).
105: - **Two-Phase Update:** When unique constraints on `[parentId, orderIndex]` exist, reordering assigns temporary negative offsets (`-1 - i`) in phase 1, followed by final contiguous zero-based indexes (`0..N-1`) in phase 2, preventing transient unique key violations.
106: 
107: ### 3. Concurrency-Safe Retries (`P2002`)
108: 
109: - For operations susceptible to concurrent insert collisions (slug generation, sequential `orderIndex` assignment), retries wrap the entire `prisma.$transaction(...)` boundary.
110: - Each retry attempt begins a completely fresh transaction after full rollback of the preceding attempt, ensuring consistent reads of the latest committed state.
111: 
112: ---
113: 
114: ## Course Catalog & Learning Player Architecture
115: 
116: ### 1. Catalog & Overview Routes
117: 
118: - **`/courses`**: Server Component reading validated query params (`search`, `category`, `level`, `sort`, `page`). Queries published courses via bounded pagination (`limit=12`) with batch enrollment decoration. Zero client-side fetching libraries or external search engines.
119: - **`/courses/[slug]`**: Server Component presenting course metadata, instructor credentials, and full curriculum outline (`CourseSyllabus`). Enforces public visibility for published courses, requiring instructor author or admin authorization for draft/archived previews.
120: - **`/courses/[slug]/learn`**: Deterministic server-side redirect entry. Routes enrolled students to their next incomplete lesson (or lesson 1 if 100% completed), or first free preview lesson for anonymous/unenrolled visitors.
121: 
122: ### 2. Student Learning Player (`/courses/[slug]/lessons/[lessonId]`)
123: 
124: - **Security & Authorization Invariants:**
125:   - Mandatory cross-course boundary check: verifies `lesson.module.course.id === course.id`. Cross-course lesson requests strictly return `NotFoundError` (preventing ID enumeration).
126:   - Enrollment & Preview Gate: Unenrolled visitors can only access lessons where `isFreePreview === true`. Non-preview lesson requests by unenrolled users safely redirect to `/courses/[slug]?enrolled=false`.
127:   - Archived Course Protection: Enrolled students cannot access lessons of archived courses.
128: - **Player Component Layout:**
129:   - `PlayerHeader`: Breadcrumbs, back-to-overview link, mobile curriculum drawer toggle.
130:   - `PlayerSidebar`: Desktop sticky sidebar and mobile drawer with course progress bar, module accordions, completion checkmarks, locked indicators, and active lesson indicator.
131:   - `PlayerVideo`: Secure sandboxed 16:9 iframe embed supporting YouTube, Vimeo, Loom.
132:   - `PlayerContent`: Sanitized lesson markdown reader using typography tokens.
133:   - `PlayerResources`: Validated downloadable and reference links (http/https only).
134:   - `PlayerFooter`: Persistent previous/next lesson navigation and `LessonCompletionButton`.
````

## File: docs/Tech Stack.md
````markdown
 1: # Technology Stack
 2: 
 3: | Category       | Choice                          | Why                                                       |
 4: | -------------- | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
 5: | Framework      | Next.js 16                      | Server Components, App Router, performance, ecosystem     |
 6: | Language       | TypeScript 5.9                  | Type safety, refactorability, fewer runtime errors        |
 7: | UI             | React 19                        | Server Components, concurrent rendering, mature ecosystem |
 8: | Styling        | Tailwind v4                     | Utility-first, small bundle, fast iteration               |
 9: | Components     | shadcn/ui (Base Nova)           | Accessible, fully customizable, no vendor lock-in         |
10: | Notifications  | goey-toast (with framer-motion) | Morphing, accessible notifications for user actions       |
11: | Authentication | Better Auth 1.7                 | Type-safe session management, RBAC, secure cookies        |
12: | Database       | PostgreSQL (Neon Serverless)    | Reliable, scalable, serverless-friendly WebSocket driver  |
13: | ORM            | Prisma 7.10                     | Type-safe queries, migrations, first-class TS support     |
14: | Validation     | Zod 4                           | Type inference, reliable runtime validation               |
15: | Forms          | React Hook Form                 | Minimal re-renders, strong TS support                     |
16: | Testing        | Jest 30 + RTL                   | Standard Next.js testing stack                            |
17: | Lint / Format  | ESLint 9 + Prettier 3           | Standard Next.js flat linting and Tailwind formatting     |
18: | Git hooks      | Husky + lint-staged             | Quality gates on commit                                   |
19: | Monitoring     | Sentry 10                       | Error monitoring, performance tracing, and source maps    |
20: 
21: ## Principles
22: 
23: Every dependency must justify its existence: improve maintainability, DX, performance, or solve a real problem.
24: 
25: ## Testing Rules
26: 
27: - Unit tests for pure functions/utilities.
28: - Integration tests for API endpoints and DB interactions.
29: - Monitor coverage, but don't enforce at the cost of maintainability.
30: 
31: ## Dependency Decisions & Version Policy
32: 
33: - **Prisma**: Kept at stable `7.10.0`. Prisma 8 is currently in release candidate (`8.0.0-rc.13`) and is rejected per stability policy.
34: - **ESLint & Prettier**: Configured with ESLint 9 flat config (`eslint-config-next`) and Prettier with `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` for class sorting and formatting.
35: - **Node-Postgres (`pg`, `@prisma/adapter-pg`)**: Removed from project dependencies. Production and development both exclusively use `@neondatabase/serverless` with `@prisma/adapter-neon` over WebSocket.
36: - **Better Auth**: Upgraded to `1.7.3` (patch update for stability and bug fixes).
37: - **Goey Toast**: Added `goey-toast` (`0.5.0`) with `framer-motion` (`13.2.0`) to provide interactive, accessible notifications for client actions.
````

## File: AGENTS.md
````markdown
  1: # Antigravity AI Guide — Next.js LMS
  2: 
  3: Canonical instruction entry point for AI coding agents in this repository.
  4: 
  5: ## 1. Project Identity & Stack
  6: 
  7: - **Domain:** Production-grade Learning Management System (LMS).
  8: - **Core Stack:** Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui.
  9: - **Data & Auth:** Prisma ORM, Neon PostgreSQL (`@prisma/adapter-neon`), Better Auth.
 10: - **Quality Tooling:** ESLint, Prettier, Jest, Knip.
 11: 
 12: ## 2. Architecture & Layer Boundaries
 13: 
 14: Strict downward dependency flow:
 15: 
 16: ```
 17: UI (Server & Client Components)
 18:   ↓
 19: Actions / Route Handlers (@/actions/*, @/app/api/*)
 20:   ↓
 21: Domain Services (@/services/*)
 22:   ↓
 23: Repositories (@/repositories/*)
 24:   ↓
 25: Database (Prisma + Neon PostgreSQL)
 26: ```
 27: 
 28: - **UI:** Presentation only. Never import Prisma or repositories directly.
 29: - **Actions / Routes:** Input validation (Zod) and auth guards only. Must return `ActionResult<T>`. No business logic.
 30: - **Services:** All business logic, transaction boundaries, and state transitions live here.
 31: - **Repositories:** Data access and queries only. No business logic.
 32: - **Database:** Managed via Prisma schema and Neon migrations.
 33: 
 34: ## 3. Agent Operating Workflow
 35: 
 36: Antigravity must follow the operating system and task governance specifications:
 37: 
 38: - **Operating System:** Orchestration & 11-Step Cognitive Cycle
 39: - **Task Protocol:** Task Tiers, Scope Lock, Approval Gates, & Invariants
 40: 
 41: Follow the 11-step cognitive cycle:
 42: Understand → Inspect → Route Skills → Verify Architecture → Plan → Implement → Verify → Audit → Document → Git Review → Report.
 43: 
 44: ### 3.1 Risk-Based Task Tiers & Approval Gates
 45: 
 46: Tasks must be triaged by **risk profile** (architectural, security, database, API contract, domain, concurrency, dependency impact), NOT by line or file count:
 47: 
 48: - **Tier 1 (PATCH):** Low-risk, local, well-understood changes (typos, CSS polish, isolated bug fix, test adjustment, or an isolated refactor with zero behavior, contract, architectural, data, or security impact).
 49:   - _Workflow:_ Inspect → Edit → Verify. No formal approval gate required.
 50: - **Tier 2 (FEATURE):** Changes introducing or modifying meaningful application behavior using existing data models and security boundaries (new UI component, Server Action, service logic, repository query).
 51:   - _Workflow:_ Inspect → Scoped Plan (with Scope Lock) → **HUMAN APPROVAL GATE** → Implement → Verify → Self-Review.
 52: - **Tier 3 (ARCHITECTURE / HIGH RISK):** Significant architectural, security, database, infrastructure, or concurrency changes (Prisma schema/migrations, Better Auth, RBAC, 4-Layer Security adjustments, row locks, breaking API contracts, any dependency addition/removal).
 53:   - _Workflow:_ Deep Inspect → Architectural Proposal / ADR → **STRICT HUMAN APPROVAL GATE** → Phased Implement → Full Verification → Self-Review → Human Final Review.
 54: 
 55: ### 3.2 The Scope Lock Guardrail
 56: 
 57: Approval of a plan creates a strict, temporary boundary:
 58: 
 59: - Every Tier 2/3 plan must state **Allowed Changes** and **Protected / Out of Scope** areas.
 60: - **Zero Unapproved Scope Creep:** If implementation reveals an out-of-scope change is necessary, the agent **MUST STOP IMMEDIATELY** and request approval via a `⚠️ SCOPE EXPANSION DETECTED` notice.
 61: 
 62: ### 3.3 Dependency Installation Guardrail
 63: 
 64: AI agents must **NEVER** install, remove, upgrade, or downgrade project dependencies (`pnpm add`, `pnpm remove`, `pnpm update`, `npm install`, etc.) without prior explicit human approval. Any dependency addition is automatically **Tier 3**.
 65: 
 66: ## 4. Skill Routing & Context Control
 67: 
 68: Do NOT load all skills for every task.
 69: Select the **minimum sufficient skill set** matching the task intent before reading detailed guides.
 70: 
 71: ## 5. Source of Truth Hierarchy
 72: 
 73: 1. **Actual Code & Tests:** Ground truth of runtime behavior and contracts.
 74: 2. **`docs/`:** Project documentation, architecture guides, and ADRs.
 75: 3. **Agent Rules & Skills:** Operating rules and specialized skill instructions.
 76: 4. **General AI Knowledge:** Fallback only. Never prioritize over repository evidence.
 77:    _If documentation conflicts with tested code, investigate and escalate instead of guessing._
 78: 
 79: ## 6. Safety & Behavior Invariants
 80: 
 81: - Never expose secrets, credentials, or private keys.
 82: - Never claim a check or test passed if it was not executed.
 83: - No destructive Git commands (`reset --hard`, `clean -fd`, `push --force`) without explicit approval.
 84: - Minimal diffs only: touch strictly what is required for the user request.
 85: - Preserve existing working behavior and tests.
 86: 
 87: ## 7. Error Suppression Policy
 88: 
 89: Fix the root cause first. Avoid suppressions (`any`, unsafe casts, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `biome-ignore`, `eslint-disable`) as shortcuts.
 90: A suppression is permissible only when technically justified, narrowly scoped, documented when non-obvious, and preferable to a worse workaround.
 91: 
 92: ## 8. Escalation & Stop Rules
 93: 
 94: When encountering architectural conflicts, domain ambiguities, security boundary uncertainties (e.g., 403 vs 404), or destructive schema changes:
 95: **STOP immediately** and report using the escalation protocol.
 96: 
 97: ## 9. Design Context
 98: 
 99: Interface design decisions are **not** improvised. Before any UI work:
100: 
101: - **`PRODUCT.md`** (project root) — strategic design context. Register: `product`. Platform: `web`. Primary users: students and instructors, equally. Personality: encouraging, generous, human, with Linear's restraint underneath. Read the five Design Principles before touching a screen. Two audiences are equally primary, so never optimize a screen for one at the cost of the other.
102: - **`DESIGN.md`** (project root) — the normative visual system. Tokens live in its YAML frontmatter; the six sections carry the rules. Non-negotiables: zero chroma on every neutral, hairline rings at rest with shadow only on hover, radii capped at 14px on cards, 16px floor for anything a user must read to decide something, no status communicated by color alone, and no gradient text / nested cards / side-stripe borders.
103: - **`.impeccable/design.json`** — machine-readable sidecar (shadow scale, motion tokens, tonal ramps, component snippets). Consult when a token is not in `globals.css`.
104: - **`src/app/globals.css`** — the OKLCH source of truth. Semantic tokens only; raw Tailwind palette colors are forbidden. `emerald-500` in the progress and sidebar components is a known un-tokenized violation.
105: - **`.agents/skills/lms-ui-ux/SKILL.md`** — interaction conventions (hit areas, press feedback, state coverage). Its three-layer shadow stack is superseded by `DESIGN.md`'s hairline-at-rest rule.
106: 
107: Accessibility floor for all UI: WCAG 2.2 AA, every animation has a `prefers-reduced-motion` path, and every state carries an icon or text so it survives color blindness and monochrome contexts.
````

## File: proxy.ts
````typescript
 1: import { type NextRequest, NextResponse } from "next/server";
 2: const publicRoutes = ["/", "/sign-in", "/sign-up"];
 3: const authRoutes = ["/sign-in", "/sign-up"];
 4: function isPublicRoute(pathname: string): boolean {
 5:   return publicRoutes.some(
 6:     (route) => pathname === route || pathname.startsWith(`${route}/`),
 7:   );
 8: }
 9: function isAuthRoute(pathname: string): boolean {
10:   return authRoutes.some(
11:     (route) => pathname === route || pathname.startsWith(`${route}/`),
12:   );
13: }
14: function hasSessionCookie(request: NextRequest): boolean {
15:   const cookies = request.cookies;
16:   return cookies
17:     .getAll()
18:     .some(
19:       (cookie) =>
20:         cookie.name.startsWith("better-auth.") ||
21:         cookie.name.startsWith("__Secure-better-auth."),
22:     );
23: }
24: export async function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
25:   const { pathname } = request.nextUrl;
26:   if (pathname.startsWith("/api/auth")) {
27:     return NextResponse.next();
28:   }
29:   if (
30:     pathname.startsWith("/_next") ||
31:     pathname.startsWith("/favicon") ||
32:     pathname.startsWith("/monitoring")
33:   ) {
34:     return NextResponse.next();
35:   }
36:   const hasSession = hasSessionCookie(request);
37:   if (!hasSession && !isPublicRoute(pathname)) {
38:     const signInUrl = new URL("/sign-in", request.url);
39:     signInUrl.searchParams.set("callbackURL", pathname);
40:     return NextResponse.redirect(signInUrl);
41:   }
42:   if (hasSession && isAuthRoute(pathname)) {
43:     return NextResponse.redirect(new URL("/", request.url));
44:   }
45:   return NextResponse.next();
46: }
47: export const config = {
48:   matcher: ["/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)"],
49: };
````

62:         uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
63:       - name: Setup Node.js
64:         uses: actions/setup-node@v4
65:         with:
66:           node-version: 22
67:           cache: pnpm
68:       - name: Install dependencies
69:         run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
70:       - name: Generate Prisma client
71:         run: pnpm prisma:generate
72:       - name: Build
73:         run: pnpm build
74:         env:
75:           DATABASE_URL: "postgresql://placeholder:placeholder@localhost:5432/placeholder"

## File: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md
````markdown
  1: # Development Guide
  2: 
  3: Practical workflow guide for developers working on the Next.js LMS platform.
  4: 
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: ## 1. Quick Start
  8: 
  9: ```bash
 10: pnpm install
 11: cp .env.example .env       # Set DATABASE_URL and auth secrets
 12: pnpm db:generate           # Generate Prisma client
 13: pnpm db:push               # Push schema to local/Neon database
 14: pnpm dev                   # Start development server on http://localhost:3000
 15: ```
 16: 
 17: **Prerequisites:** Node.js 22+, pnpm 9+, PostgreSQL (Neon or local).
 18: 
 19: ---
 20: 
 21: ## 2. Core Conventions & Architecture
 22: 
 23: To avoid duplication and drift, full specifications live in their authoritative documents:
 24: 
 25: - **Architecture & Layer Hierarchy:** Follow the 5-layer downward rule (`UI → Actions/Routes → Services → Repositories → Database`). See **[Architecture Guide](Architecture.md)**.
 26: - **Coding Standards:** Strict TypeScript (no `any`), Zod runtime validation, and naming rules. See **[Coding Standards](Coding%20Standards.md)**.
 27: - **Design System & Anti-Slop:** Design tokens, component contracts, and aesthetic doctrine. See **[Design Tokens](design/tokens.md)** and **[Anti-Slop Doctrine](design/anti-slop.md)**.
 28: - **Git & Release Workflow:** Branching strategy (`master` / `dev` / `dev/<feature>`), commit conventions, and release tagging. See **[Git Workflow Guide](Development/Git.md)**.
 29: - **Master Documentation Index:** See **[Master Index](INDEX.md)**.
 30: 
 31: ---
 32: 
 33: ## 3. Common Development Commands
 34: 
 35: ```bash
 36: # Code quality & verification
 37: pnpm check                          # Full verification: ESLint + tsc + knip + Prettier
 38: pnpm lint                           # Run ESLint
 39: pnpm lint:fix                       # Run ESLint with auto-fix
 40: pnpm format                         # Run Prettier code formatting
 41: pnpm format:check                   # Check Prettier formatting
 42: pnpm typecheck                      # TypeScript typecheck (tsc --noEmit)
 43: pnpm test                           # Run Jest test suite
 44: 
 45: # Database workflows
 46: pnpm db:generate                    # Regenerate Prisma client
 47: pnpm db:push                        # Fast push schema to database
 48: pnpm db:migrate:dev                 # Create and apply new Prisma migration
 49: pnpm db:studio                      # Open Prisma Studio web GUI
 50: 
 51: # Adding UI components
 52: pnpx shadcn@latest add <component>  # Add a shadcn/ui primitive
 53: ```
 54: 
 55: > [!TIP]
 56: > When adding new environment variables, remember to update `.env.example`, your local `.env`, and validate them in `src/lib/env.ts` using Zod.
 57: 
 58: ---
 59: 
 60: ## 4. Debugging & Error Monitoring (Sentry)
 61: 
 62: This project integrates **Sentry** for client, server, and edge exception tracking and performance telemetry.
 63: 
 64: ### Configuration Files
 65: 
 66: - `sentry.client.config.ts`: Client-side telemetry, session replay, and tracing.
 67: - `sentry.server.config.ts`: Server-side Node.js runtime exception capture and performance spans.
 68: - `sentry.edge.config.ts`: Edge runtime exception handling.
 69: - `src/instrumentation.ts`: Hooks Next.js server error instrumentation (`onRequestError = Sentry.captureRequestError`).
 70: - `src/app/global-error.tsx`: Root React Error Boundary capturing unhandled layout crashes.
 71: 
 72: ### Environment Variables
 73: 
 74: | Variable                 | Description                                             | Required   |
 75: | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
 76: | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` | Client DSN URL                                          | Production |
 77: | `SENTRY_DSN`             | Server DSN URL (falls back to `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`) | Production |
 78: | `SENTRY_ORG`             | Sentry organization slug                                | CI / Build |
 79: | `SENTRY_PROJECT`         | Sentry project slug                                     | CI / Build |
 80: | `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`      | Sentry auth token for source map uploads                | CI / Build |
 81: 
 82: ### Logging Notes
 83: 
 84: - Server Component and Server Action errors log to the **terminal** console, not the browser devtools.
 85: - Prisma query logging can be enabled in `src/lib/db.ts` via `new PrismaClient({ log: ["query", "error", "warn"] })`.
 86: 
 87: ---
 88: 
 89: ## 5. Performance Checklist
 90: 
 91: - [ ] Prefer Server Components by default; keep Client Components (`"use client"`) as thin leaf nodes.
 92: - [ ] Wrap asynchronous boundaries with React `Suspense` and dedicated `loading.tsx` skeletons.
 93: - [ ] Optimize all images using `next/image` with explicit dimensions or fill attributes.
 94: - [ ] Ensure database queries in repositories have index backing and use cursor pagination for unbounded lists.
 95: 
 96: ---
 97: 
 98: ## 6. Active Toolchain Roadmap
 99: 
100: - **Automated Accessibility:** Integrate automated axe-core / Lighthouse auditing into CI/CD.
101: - **Visual Regression:** Playwright or Chromatic for visual regression testing across themes.
102: - **Performance Baselines:** Establish Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) and API latency metrics.
````

## File: README.md
````markdown
  1: # Next.js LMS Platform
  2: 
  3: > A production-grade Learning Management System (LMS) built with Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui, Prisma ORM, Neon PostgreSQL, and Better Auth.
  4: 
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: ## Key Features
  8: 
  9: - **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC):** Multi-tier authorization supporting Students, Instructors, and Administrators via Better Auth with session management and route guards.
 10: - **Course Catalog & Discovery:** Server-side search, category and proficiency level filtering, sorting, and bounded pagination with automatic enrollment state decoration.
 11: - **Student Learning Player:** Interactive course player featuring dynamic curriculum sidebar navigation, video embeds (YouTube, Vimeo, Loom), server-sanitized markdown reader, downloadable resources, and granular per-lesson progress completion tracking.
 12: - **Instructor Course Management:** Dedicated instructor authoring workspace for course creation, curriculum organization (modules and lessons), atomic two-phase curriculum reordering, rich markdown editor with live sanitized preview, and publishing state machines.
 13: - **User Profiles:** Self-service profile management with bio, headline, website, and avatar customization.
 14: - **Enterprise Security & Concurrency:** IDOR protection on all resources, server-side XSS sanitization (`sanitize-html` and `marked`), parent course row locking (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`), and atomic database transactions.
 15: 
 16: ---
 17: 
 18: ## Tech Stack
 19: 
 20: | Category             | Technology                              |
 21: | -------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
 22: | **Framework**        | Next.js 16 (App Router)                 |
 23: | **Language**         | TypeScript 5.9                          |
 24: | **UI Library**       | React 19                                |
 25: | **Styling**          | Tailwind CSS v4 + tw-animate-css        |
 26: | **Components**       | shadcn/ui (base-nova) + Lucide Icons    |
 27: | **Database**         | PostgreSQL (Neon serverless)            |
 28: | **ORM**              | Prisma 7.10                             |
 29: | **Authentication**   | Better Auth 1.7                         |
 30: | **Validation**       | Zod                                     |
 31: | **Forms**            | React Hook Form + `@hookform/resolvers` |
 32: | **Testing**          | Jest 30 + React Testing Library         |
 33: | **Tooling & Linter** | ESLint 9 + Prettier 3 + Knip            |
 34: | **Monitoring**       | Sentry (`@sentry/nextjs`)               |
 35: 
 36: ---
 37: 
 38: ## Architecture
 39: 
 40: This project strictly adheres to a **5-layer architecture** with downward-only dependency flow:
 41: 
 42: ```
 43: UI Layer (Server & Client Components)
 44:   ↓
 45: Actions / Routes (@/actions/*, @/app/api/*)
 46:   ↓
 47: Domain Services (@/services/*)
 48:   ↓
 49: Repositories (@/repositories/*)
 50:   ↓
 51: Database (Prisma + Neon PostgreSQL)
 52: ```
 53: 
 54: - **UI:** Pure presentation. Never queries database or repositories directly. Interactive elements are isolated client leaves (`"use client"`).
 55: - **Actions / Routes:** Input validation via Zod schemas and session/role guards. Standardized `ActionResult<T>` responses.
 56: - **Domain Services:** Centralized business logic, transactions, state machines, and 4-tier authorization.
 57: - **Repositories:** Clean data access, queries, and atomic database mutations.
 58: - **Database:** Managed via Prisma schemas with indexes supporting foreign keys and query paths.
 59: 
 60: ---
 61: 
 62: ## Quick Start
 63: 
 64: ### 1. Clone & Install Dependencies
 65: 
 66: ```bash
 67: git clone <repository-url>
 68: cd nextjs
 69: pnpm install
 70: ```
 71: 
 72: ### 2. Configure Environment Variables
 73: 
 74: Create `.env` based on `.env.example`:
 75: 
 76: ```bash
 77: cp .env.example .env
 78: ```
 79: 
 80: Ensure the following variables are configured:
 81: 
 82: ```env
 83: # Database (Neon PostgreSQL)
 84: DATABASE_URL="postgresql://user:password@endpoint.neon.tech/neondb?sslmode=require"
 85: 
 86: # Better Auth Configuration
 87: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET="your-secure-random-secret-key-at-least-32-chars"
 88: BETTER_AUTH_URL="http://localhost:3000"
 89: NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL="http://localhost:3000"
 90: 
 91: # Sentry (Optional for local dev)
 92: NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN=""
 93: ```
 94: 
 95: ### 3. Database Migration & Client Generation
 96: 
 97: ```bash
 98: pnpm db:generate
 99: pnpm db:push
100: # or run migrations:
101: # pnpm db:migrate
102: ```
103: 
104: ### 4. Run Development Server
105: 
106: ```bash
107: pnpm dev
108: ```
109: 
110: Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) in your browser.
111: 
112: ---
113: 
114: ## Available Scripts
115: 
116: | Command            | Description                                                               |
117: | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
118: | `pnpm dev`         | Start Next.js development server                                          |
119: | `pnpm build`       | Create production build                                                   |
120: | `pnpm start`       | Start production server                                                   |
121: | `pnpm test`        | Run complete Jest test suite (unit, integration, security)                |
122: | `pnpm typecheck`   | Run TypeScript compiler check without emitting files                      |
123: | `pnpm lint`        | Run ESLint across codebase                                                |
124: | `pnpm format`      | Format files using Prettier                                               |
125: | `pnpm check`       | Run full quality gate: ESLint, TypeScript check, Knip, and Prettier check |
126: | `pnpm db:generate` | Regenerate Prisma Client                                                  |
127: | `pnpm db:push`     | Sync Prisma schema with Neon database                                     |
128: | `pnpm db:studio`   | Open Prisma Studio database viewer                                        |
129: 
130: ---
131: 
132: ## Project Structure
133: 
134: ```
135: src/
136: ├── actions/             # Server Actions (Zod parsing, auth guards, ActionResult)
137: ├── app/                 # Next.js App Router (pages, layouts, route handlers)
138: │   ├── (auth)/          # Authentication routes (/sign-in, /sign-up)
139: │   ├── (dashboard)/     # Protected instructor & user dashboards
140: │   ├── (marketing)/     # Public landing & static pages
141: │   ├── courses/         # Course catalog, syllabus, and learning player
142: │   └── api/             # API route handlers (Better Auth, webhooks)
143: ├── components/
144: │   ├── features/        # Domain-scoped UI components (auth, catalog, player, etc.)
145: │   ├── global/          # Global layout, header, footer, theme providers
146: │   └── ui/              # shadcn/ui design primitives (button, card, dialog, etc.)
147: ├── lib/                 # Core utilities, errors, validators, auth config
148: ├── providers/           # React context providers (Theme, Auth)
149: ├── repositories/        # Concrete data access layer (Prisma models)
150: ├── services/            # Domain business logic & transaction boundaries
151: └── __tests__/           # Security penetration tests (IDOR, XSS)
152: ```
153: 
154: ---
155: 
156: ## Documentation Links
157: 
158: - **[Master Index](docs/INDEX.md)** — Canonical project documentation hub
159: - **[Architecture Guide](docs/Architecture.md)** — Detailed 5-layer boundaries and concurrency patterns
160: - **[Domain Entities Reference](docs/reference/Entities.md)** — Comprehensive entity and relation definitions
161: - **[ADR 001: Layered Architecture](docs/decisions/001-use-layered-architecture.md)**
162: - **[ADR 002: Neon with Prisma](docs/decisions/002-use-neon-with-prisma.md)**
163: - **[ADR 003: shadcn/ui Component Strategy](docs/decisions/003-use-shadcn-ui.md)**
164: - **[ADR 004: LMS Domain Model](docs/decisions/004-lms-domain-model.md)**
165: 
166: ---
167: 
168: ## License
169: 
170: [MIT](./LICENSE)
````
